records.script: This year's winner has done a phenomenal job exploring their scape to grow their team and make a huge impact in their pond. This team dives into the sea to quest for new workshops that train students in areas such as CAD and block programming. They expand their mission by hosting over 100 day camps, summer camps, workshops and events. As the seas are vast, this team works with 15 different schools from 7 districts, and does outreach to 2 foreign countries for a total impact of 290,000 people over the past 3 years. By George!, this team has made investments. With an annual operating revenue of over $125k, they make every penny count and established a new STEM center 14 times larger than their previous space. They used this new facility as a vessel to host multiple socials, further community workshops and in true maritime fashion train those in the art of the sea whittling. This team is a good steward of their new vessel to continue to quest and explore advanced manufacturing techniques.

This insightful team outreaches across the world with their out of this world name. With their African outreach and local tractor pulls, this team was a true inspiration. Congratulation to Team 34, the Rockets!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: From their sleek reinforced elevator down to their clean cornered bumpers, this team soared above the competition. Their robust design with low center of gravity and quick programming allowed for wheelies as a feature, not a bug. They may have left their leaf blowers at home this season, but the judges are still beaked out about this team. Congratulations to Team 4028, The Beak Squad!

FIRST in Their Community Award (Judge's Award) This year's judges award was dedicated based on the heavy advocacy we saw for themselves and their surrounding community. They approached this season incorporating their known limitations and supply chain difficulties, showing their deep understanding of the engineering process. Seeing the passion and dedication in these students was sweeter than pie. Congratulations to Team 3814, PiBotics!

They may be new, but don't be mistaken - when challenges rose, they weren't shaken! With teamwork, talent, and rookie flair, they proved their skills beyond compare! They're Team 10011, the Gem City Gridrunners, - your Rookie All-Star!

This young team clearly demonstrates the FIRST mission. They reach out to mentor FLL and FTC teams and volunteers at FIRST events. They are "busting" through the challenges. Congratulations to Team 9097, MachBusters!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: In the deep BLUE sea of FIRST Reefscape this team has shown their dedication to sustainability in their team and their community. The judges were over the moon with their onboarding and advocacy programs. Congratulations to Team 2220, Blue Twilight!
The thunderous sound of this team's spirit is unified in community using creative minds of 3rd graders for naming inspiration. Congratulations to Team 3630, Stampede!
This winning team demonstrated their "respawned" engineering process using their tech binder with detailed drawings to labeled subsystem totes.
Focused on FIRST Core Values with helping other teams with parts and codes, this mythical name showed how gracious professionalism flowed. Congratulations to Team 2783, Engineers of Tomorrow!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team's shining example of creativity took them to the automotive supply for parts. They put the "fun" in funnel. Congratulations to Team 7428, Gigawatts.

This team dazzled us, showing bright color that shines with purpose. Take a deep dive: from pit checklists to the build manual, all subsystems align by color. Their CAD designers are fully certified, for good reason, but their name has no rhyme. Congratulations to Team 144, Operation Orange!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This winning team not only described innovated controls, they lit them up in the shape of a reef. By their innovative controls, the press of a button, the scores coral-ated. Congratulations to Team 6517, So-Kno Robo!
This team's robot was well-designed... and their autonomous features were exceptional. Proving they had all their GEARS in a row. Congratulations to Team 2338, Gear it Forward!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team REALLY stood out from the crowd. Their image could make others green with envy. They have recently rebranded with new logo and mascot that symbolizes power, wealth, courage, and prestige. Congratulations to Team 3966, Gryphon Command!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division
records.script: This team’s commitments to making a difference is as inspiring as the innovations they create. They have developed STEM curriculums for students with special needs, created adaptive learning devices, and designed prosthetics for children in their community. They bring joy through hands on learning. This team truly lives their motto, “makers lead the way.” Congratulations, Team number 5951, Makers Assemble

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: When their elevator drops, the sound will leave you in a DAZE. They don't MISS a beat. This team's robot BLOSSOMED throughout the competition. Congratulations, Team number 341, Miss Daisy

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division
records.script: The judge’s have created the: Leader in STEM Education Award They set aside their school rivalries to come together to spread STEM far and wide. They pass out cards to teach binary and number placement. This team is creating the future leaders in education. Congratulations, Team number 1629, Garrett Coalition (GaCo)

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division
records.script: This young team is already making big impacts in their local community, ROCKETING STEM to new schools through exciting projects using accessible materials to make learning BLAST OFF. They fly on the wing of a beautiful blue macaw. The Rookie All-Star Award is presented to: 10466, Federal Force

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division
records.script: Moving out of rookie status has not impeded this team’s path to success. From spinning 3D filament to developing voice activated robots, they CLAWED their way forward. Their reach into South America brings STEM to those who have no exposure SOARING to the stars. Congratulations, Team number 9459, SESI SENAI RPRT HAWKS

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Rebuilding over the last few seasons to ensure their success has been no AVERAGE task. This team kept from getting BEACHED by leveraging their Google Drive repository of historical team documents. They utilize their FLL and FTC pipeline of students to foster future FRC members. They connect with their community to ensure continued team support. These JOES have set their eyes on the Chicago skyline to ensure that they have set future members up for success. Congratulations, Team number 3620, Average Joes

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division
records.script: This team’s energy and passion pulled the judges into their pits. Their BRIGHT ORANGE colors match their enthusiasm for FIRST and willingness to share it with others. Whether it’s OPERATING their robot on the field or passing out earrings in the pits, their spirit is infectious. Congratulations, Team number 6358, The Buhlean Operators

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division
records.script: This team FLIES high with their adapted automotive design and manufacturing process. Their innovative yet effective team organization allowed for accuracy in their design and engineering process, while building a solid NEST for their future student leaders. Congratulations, Team number 2834, Bionic Black Hawks

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division
records.script: Being the most prepared team in the building is always their goal. When your robot is down and out, they RACE to the rescue. The application of Alliance Readiness ensures fairness in every match. Congratulations, Team number 1987, Broncobots

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team slides horizontally into the SPOTLIGHT scoring easily. These STARS are ready for their closeup, manipulating coral like a scene from a blockbuster. Congratulations, Team number 7211, Hollywood

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division
records.script: This team demonstrates elegance in their unbreakable design. From crashes to hard matches, they never needed to use any of their nine lives. This CAT purred their way to victory! Congratulations, Team number 1756, Argos

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: As teammates walked around the field with a giant template and cameras, they made people laugh. Their practical view for a replacement system showed their out of the box thinking. Using an innovative new vision system instead of reading April Tags, made VR technology proud. Congratulations, Team number 1732, Hilltopper Robotics

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division
records.script: This team hit the mark even when the SEA was rough. They slide into alignment from PORT to STARBOARD guaranteeing their scoring success. With their gyro, they wait to deliver coral until the ship stops shaking. Congratulations, Team number 2481, Roboteers

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Archimedes Division
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Draped in purple and full of spirit, this team created a presence as bold and timeless as their namesake. With striking GREEK theme and thoughtful design, they’ve truly brought their brand to life. Congratulations, Team number 3182, Athena’s Warriors

This team actively fostered a relationship with their community. They plotted a course to make an impact by setting specific goals for their own opportunities and landing them. This team broke away from the rest of the competition by creating a ripple effect across their state. Congratulations Team 3937 – Breakaway.

This team makes inspiring others look as easy as a wafting breeze. Like a bolt from the sky, they shock their community with an outsized impact. This year, there can be only one winner of the Engineering Inspiration Award. Congratulations Team 4499 – The Highlanders.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: In a world where robots usually resemble tangled wires and last minute duct tape fixes, one team dared to blend aerospace-grade engineering with jaw-dropping aesthetics. With a design so sleek and functional, even a B-2 Bomber might take notes, their machine didn’t just compete – it dominated with style. Congratulations Team 16 – Bomb Squad.

This team illuminates resilience through their ability to overcome significant challenges while maintaining excellence in robotics. Operating out of multiple state-wide locations they have successfully continued to grow. Their ability to adapt, problem-solve, and push forward in the face of adversity make them the recipient of the judges resilience award. Congratulations Team 323 – Lights Out.

This rookie team came in with a blast! This colorful team never backed down, bringing a rock solid robot that was both beautiful and reliable. With an impressive debut, they have launched themselves into FRC with style. Congratulations Team 10101 – Critical Hit.

Rising to the sky when most of the teams in their region flew away, this team rides the wind in their city to be the “FIRST” leader. This team soars like a Bird. Congratulations Team 1781 – Lindblom Electric Eagles.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has been crazy about STEM since the 1990’s. When it comes to dedication, team and family come first. Their efforts within their community has increased interest in science and mathematics. While Most kids do not like the swamp, these kids rise to the occasion by helping local therapists to see the water better. Congratulations to Team 179 – Children of the Swamp.
Valiantly riding in from the west, this team’s spirit shined bright like a knights armor. Congratulations Team 2036 – Boulder Valley Black Knights.

This team clearly described their engineering design process and created an aesthetically elegant and supremely functional robot that efficiently addressed a specific game challenge. Trying to match their success from 2016, this team created a robot that can snatch coral off the ocean floor at a break-neck speed and place them at the top tiers of the reef. Congratulations Team 2481 - Roboteers.

This team has truly been “trailblazing” the competition and community with competitive spirit, kindness, and dedication to learning. Through their efforts on and off the field, they are inspiring the next generation of engineers and leaders. They embody gracious professionalism. Congratulations Team 7525 – The Pioneers.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team built a unique design and exhibits thoughtful innovation. It’s not just a robot, it’s a force of nature just like the legendary dragon it was inspired by. Congratulations Team 4500 – RoboHounds.

This team impressed the judges with their commitment to modularity and careful balance of weight and strength. They prevent errors from sneaking up on them with their dual fail-safes and multiple backups. Their high quality robot is sleek and stealthy like a jungle cat. Congratulations to Team 6424 – Stealth Panther Robotics.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team refused to let the chaos slither into their game play by downloading their program log after each match. Their various sensors and strategic programming keeps their game play stitched together like a good pair of jeans. With a deadly injection of 3D rendered simulations, this team stung the competition. Congratulations Team 8044 – Denham Venom.

This award goes to the team with a robot that showed superior self-sufficiency, consistency, and precision. Their bot was nearly as intelligent and independent as the team members it was built by. Look for their name once their wheels touch the red dust of mars. Congratulations Team 118 - Robonauts.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Bringing beautiful vibrant colors to technology, this team used an original theme to show they are titans among their peers. Congratulations Team 9429 – Tech Titans.

Fueled by innovation and the drive to improve, this team turns isolation into connection and ideas into impact. With every kilometer travelled, their influence grows stronger, igniting change across their vast community. On an unstoppable upward trajectory, they continue pushing the limits of what’s possible. One thing is certain—you just Can’t Control how far they’ll go!

Guided by their moral compass, they welcome all genders and backgrounds, driving innovation with heart. Through sustained effort—past, present, and future—this team proudly upholds the FIRST values, shaping a world where STEM is for everyone. With the roar of Thunder, they charge forward, inspiring generations to come!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team designed an efficient, aesthetic and capable robot, you could even say that it’s deadly on the field. Their robot is a futuristic masterpiece with industrial grade precision. Maybe just a little too good at it’s job, it turns heads and all that people see is red.

This noble team has championed the cause of STEM far beyond their own borders, making connections with organisations great and small. Their robot stunned us with their creativity. This team isn’t just impressive—they’re TURTLE-Y amazing!

Though only new, this team hit the road at full speed. With their eyes firmly on the future, they spread their love of robots, engineering and FIRST from remote communities to children's hospitals. We're *blown away* by this year's Rookie All-stars...

This team is clearly fluent in the universal language of success! They’ve shown remarkable growth, turning challenges into opportunities and proving they’re ready to reach even greater heights. Throughout the competition, they have translated their briiliance into well-deserved recognition.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Sustainability isn’t just a practice for them—it’s a way of life, and they never back down! From upcycling materials and 3D printing with sustainable resources to repurposing sponsor-provided scraps, they’ve mastered the art of turning “trash” into treasure while uplifting other teams and giving back to communities near and far. With a passion for innovation and a drive to support others, this team runs away with the Sustainability Award.

When the sky darkened, all members of this team eagerly jumped in to help. They provided upskilling lessons and support to ensure every member is on the same page, embodying true spirit and dedication. They were champions of teamwork, followed by thunderous applause wherever they went.

Some Australian fauna spend their summers sleeping in the sun. This team clawed hard through this season’s challenge to understand functions and design innovative mechanisms. They can now rest in their demonstration of Engineering Excellence.

Teamwork isn’t about who has the best idea, it’s about setting aside egos, collaborating, and finding the best solution together. This team embodies sportswomanship, always competing with respect and lifting others up along the way. With clearly defined sub-teams, every member has a role, making their professionalism easy to see in both their organization and attitude. Their commitment to teamwork, collaboration, and respect, the judges believe this team is purring with success and ready to ROAR!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Not all algae are create equal, consistent scoring is a challenge of precision and strategy. This team have become a true crowd favourite. Their ability to fire the algae into the barge, rivals the skills of an NBA superstar.

This team embodies the spirit of quality with precision and poise. Their indestructible robot is no accident with planning, process, and an electronics powerhouse that drives every flawless movement. With absolute reliability, even Alexander the Great would ride it to victory.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Their robot is a marvel of precision and practicality, seamlessly integrating with its human player to make a finely tuned proud duet. It handled the pressures of competition with ease, making split-second decisions under stress and performing flawlessly every time. We are proud to present the Innovation in Control award to…

Their robot wasn’t just fast — it was a lightning bolt on wheels! Zipping across the field with ninja-like agility, it scored again and again during autonomous mode, hitting its targets with laser-sharp accuracy. It was less of a robot and more of a perfectly programmed powerhouse, thinking and moving like a true autonomous champion.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: When there is a call to create something extraordinary, this teams rises to the occasion. They had the team integrated into the robot design, the branding, and displayed it on and off the field. This team that comes together as pack is the winner of the Imagery Award.

This team's passion, dedication to each other, and love of their community really sparkles. Boldly going where no team has gone before, they have created unique FIRST teams that give groups (that might be traditionally overlooked in STEM) a place to belong. Strong partnerships allow this team to plant the seeds of inspiration in uncharted worlds by providing scholarships, technical support in their home language, and volunteering countless hours with organizations that support foster youth, homeless pets, and the environment. This team's impact has expanded beyond their home world, shining brighter than a supernova! Congratulations to team 9134, Prepa Tecmilenio - DEVOLT!!!

This team makes sweet music every time they go on the road. operating on a shoestring, they collaborate with a professional organization to make STEM available and accessible for students of all backgrounds. This team is no dog - but they go, baby, go! Congratulations team # 4146 - SaberCats.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team really appreciated the importance of being low to the ground while also having a unique window to the competition. While getting dust in the robot drive wheels can be a problem on the "mesa", this team definitely has it covered. Congratulations to team 2478 - Westwood Robotics.

The lack of infrastructure did not deter this team from embracing the philosophy of FIRST. From the judge's perspective, this team really measured up! This team provided the cheese to close the mousetrap that impressed the judges. Congratulations team 4565 Skyline Robotics.

After awaking from a many-year slumber, this team has armored up with innovation. They are doing a grand job of knighting their squires. They have successfully jousted with challenges and forged a bright future. Congrats team 996, the Mecha Knights

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Having traveled a vast distance, this team has developed strategies to ensure growth with guaranteed fun and mentors outside of the traditional FIRST orbit. Like a spirit, they plan to haunt competitions for years to come. Congratulations team 7333 - GHOST.
This team traveled from a state away -they slithered into the snow to play. The striking way they share their team, in many languages can be seen. Congratulations team 8717 the Cyber Vipers

This team readily demonstrated engineering excellence in their approach, including being able to kick out extra coral in the chute. Their ability to lock out certain components was equally impressive. While they describe themselves as silly or squirrelly, they are definitely not a "Nut". Congratulations to team 2486 - the Coconuts.

This team rises above to support all teams whether it is controls, programming, or help getting out of the snow. These birds are ready to lend a helping wing. With smiles on their beaks, their gracious professionalism is degrees above all. Congratulations team 6413 - Degrees of Freedom.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Following a star-lined path, this team solved the game's challenge from the inside out. They stay grounded as their bottom fell through and pinned themselves to the cages whether red or blue. Congratulations team 7425 Green Valley Robotics

This team knows how to repeatedly strike with precision while adding a fresh twist. Their robot is a masterpiece of quality and durability. Like a true predator, this scorpion-inspired machine is built to last. Congratulations to team 6995 - The NOMADS

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team's mechanical and software groups worked together to create a design that was easy to control. They wiggled their way into scoring coral. With their score they spring ahead of the competition. Congratulations to Team 6560 the Charging Champions

This team has truly embraced the bits and bytes of robot automation. By leveraging state space sequencing, they developed an innovative way to automate elevator positioning, demonstrating a deep understanding of automation as well as technical excellence. They certainly have taken a BYTE out of their competition. Congratulations to team 9432 - Team 8-bit

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: For this team no obstacle is insurmountable. As a small team, they weave their core values into everything they do. Scaling challenges and spreading the mission of FIRST in their community, you can spot them in their yellow hard hats and ropes - Team 3009 -The high Scalers.

Many many seconds ago in a galaxy we call our own, this team went across their world championing FIRST core values. Recognizing the need to combat lack of STEM knowledge in their community, city, nation and their planet, they handed out free kits to spread the mission of FIRST, launching over 400 FIRST classroom teams. Several of the teams they started and mentored have since won at FIRST events, including at FIRST Global and are on track to complete the “Kamen Run” in under 12 parsecs. Not content with increasing STEM awareness across the globe, this team uses every opportunity to keep their fighting skills top notch - no matter whether they are on the red, blue, or gold team. No surprise that this team is ready to launch their impact to intergalactic levels.

This team not only lifts an arm in competition, they provide a helping hand to a host of teams and their community. They spread the mission of FIRST within and beyond competition from fields to tutoring access. Like the tide they lift all ships in the Bay.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team's robot strikes a perfect balance between paint and performance. The modular design is both advantageous and convenient to pack. Pac-man doesn't have anything on this Blinky!

When a challenge appears, this team keeps their heads up. Their resilience caught the judge's attention as they overcame challenges in clever ways. Like a circuit that powers the robot, these phantom circuits know that their can-do attitude is the key to success.

This team was forged from a quest of knowledge for all. They have already begun lighting the way for others through meticulous documentation and dedicated mentorship. With the fine shining of their armor they're igniting their way to a bright future.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team knows how to strategically re-use parts. Through many forms of outreach, they bring FIRST principles to children in their community one library, battery and scrimmage at a time. For their work to build a world where robotics is accessible to every student, these cobras took command of the their future.

This team embodies the spirit of FIRST with their enthusiasm and positivity, both at the competition and in their community. You can spot them swimming together with all their members in every aspect of the robot build; sharing their school's successes. With orange headbands and shiny scales, these "guppies" have taken their teamwork to the next level.
This team shined brightly in their meticulous engineering documentation, optimized coral collection and organized manufacturing schedule. This team demonstrated excellence worthy of victory.

Coming from a far away place, this team's gracious professionalism bubbles up to the top! Recognizing the intense pressures of competition this team strives to ensure that each and every team has a fair and equal chance to compete. Whether they are loaning tool or programming expertise, you can always find this friendly pod swimming through the pits to offer up a helping fin!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team impressed the judges with the unique shape of their robot. Their tall sideboard offered a functional advantage on the field of play and their turret made the judges purr with delight.
This team's mission and robot was well planned out and executed. Their impressive design process was really a really exciting matter. Now it is time for us to count your smiles.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Controlling a robot is no mean feat among us. This team avoids many pitfalls of the reef alignment challenge to quickly score. Going beyond the call of duty, they certainly proved they have more than an 8-bit control system.

This team's depth of understanding of programming concepts impressed the judges. Using vectors, this robot navigates smoothly from point to point. At the push of a button or two, this team's robot smoothly sails across the field to score.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team knows how to handle the heat. They and their robot are instantly recognizable and memorable whether alone or together. Their powerful imagery might make you thirsty, but it won't make you blue and they crushed the field by a herringbone.

This team exemplifies FIRST’s mission through a focused and sustained effort to promote STEM within their community. They have doubled the chances of their members attending post-secondary institutions, and tripled the chances of their members pursuing STEM careers. They have demonstrated the utmost care and connection to their home, and a commitment to future generations by securing millions of dollars in funding, and assuring that robotics is integrated into local school curriculums across their island. In the past two years, their strong focus on building sustainable STEM programs in Indigenous communities has grown beyond their island to New Zealand, and Canada’s Yukon. This team’s efforts to create lasting impact in their community through perseverance via their Ho’omau (“Ho-o-mau”) Academy had judges singing their praises, and agreeing wholeheartedly with their most meaningful initiative, E Ola Na Opio, which translates to THE YOUTH SHALL THRIVE.

This team has incubated a sister team and supported FRC teams with a focus on off-season events. They have educated parents and policy-makers on the need for project-based learning… and successfully applied for robotics to be a required course for school graduation.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team’s elegant and effective design combines speed, accuracy, and dependability. Its amazing what kids can do with one arm. But it should not come as a surprise that this team can deal with coral reefs!
Learning to code is the basis of a smooth running robot. And you can never introduce it too early. With their fun app that anyone, anywhere can access. This team is top on their block.

This team’s outreach activities, sustainability, and partnerships have impacted their whole community. They prototyped their way to a great intake. Every day is a good hair dry with their scrunchies for safety.

This team created a sturdy robot, giving them a solid foundation to build on. Their fresh approach to the gameplay brought them success in the qualifiers. Since their formation in 2021, they have been committed to generating excitement for robotics in their school and region.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team’s dedication to sustainable practices was evident in every aspect of their work. They have sparked much interest in continuing the team spirit, including the creation of a rookie sibling.
This team’s enthusiasm for creativity in STEM helped bring them closer to their community. Their shop skills and mascot redesign gave everyone the warm fuzzies.

This team showed us Excellence in Engineering with elegance and play. They showed us that teamwork in design runs deep with their ocean of wealth. They made a splash with the judges on and off the field.

This team was never shy to offer a helping hand; lending parts and assistance whenever asked. They are a pillar of support, both figuratively and literally and were the first to arrive and help assemble the field. This team turns up the heat when it comes to forging strong partnerships in the FIRST community.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team was on a mission to sweep the ocean floor and repair the coral reef. Their creative approach to manipulating the ocean fauna was unique. Their one armed bandit effectively captured the oceans wealth.
This team’s robot endured the rigors of ever round without bending. Despite the team’s name, their design is anything but Chaotic.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: It takes more than a pretty machine to finish a task. With a steely eye on their goal, this team has alloyed machine and software, with outstanding results. They ironed out the kinks in their control and simulation environment to take this honor.
This team’s three piece auto set a tall bar. They repeatedly succeeded at scoring on the top of the reef. This team was as smooth as mashed potatoes.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: The team stood out to the judges based on the buzz they generated here, and their imagery extends back home to their hive. They are truly the Bee’s knees of imagery.

A equipe vencedora do FIRST Impact Award demonstrou um impacto significativo e sustentável na comunidade e na promoção dos valores do programa FIRST. Com ex-alunos seguindo carreiras em STEAM e permanecendo envolvidos com o FIRST, a equipe demonstra um compromisso contínuo com a educação e o desenvolvimento de líderes. Eles lançaram o programa de capacitação de professores de escolas públicas e integraram a robótica em todas as séries escolares, sendo pioneira na progressão completa da FIRST. Além disso, a equipe promove a inclusão e a diversidade e desempenhou um papel vital durante uma das maiores catástrofes do Brasil, voluntariando mais de 2.000 horas para apoiar as vítimas. Com parcerias significativas e iniciativas sustentáveis, a equipe exemplifica os valores de profissionalismo, humanidade, excelência e um exemplo para todas as equipes de FRC do Brasil, justificando assim plenamente a conquista do prêmio.

Esta equipe viu oportunidades onde outros viam desafios. Transformou um grande investimento público em um recurso educacional poderoso. Com criatividade e acessibilidade, sua caixa mágica já levou a FIRST para o mundo a fora. E como um gigante que se fortalece na união, combinam inovação, colaboração e impacto para transformar o mundo !

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Eles usaram um Design inovador e funcional. O seu mascote também entrou na arena com eles, sempre apontando para a direção certa, dessa forma fica difícil perder a mira. Acorda que o galo tá cantando, vem pegar seu prêmio…

Uma das principais obrigatoriedades para acessar este evento é também uma grande preocupação dessa equipe. Utilizando inteligência artificial e visão computacional para detectar quem está infringindo esta regra, também desenvolvem novos competidores para que eles coloquem seus conhecimentos em pratica. Seu sistema nos observa a todo momento com suas varias cabeça e olhos.

Como uma locomotiva, feita para passar por muitas estações, seus tripulantes organizam a bordo importantes projetos sociais, conectando tecnologia e comunidade. Eles percorrem os trilhos da inovação, tendo como guia o triângulo da bandeira mineira, símbolos de força e união.

Algumas equipes crescem. Outras, renascem. Com novos integrantes e um novo nome, uniram-se às suas equipes irmãs, encontrando força em suas raízes. O resultado? Uma trajetória de superação e aprendizado. Eles provaram que, mesmo em meio às mudanças, a estrela do norte continua viva e pronta para brilhar.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Com as cores do amor, da inovação e da união, esta equipe transforma o mundo ao seu redor! Trazendo iniciativas que não apenas impactam por meio de ações sustentáveis, mas também garantem a continuidade da equipe ao inspirar e formar novas gerações, eles mostram que o futuro da robótica é tão duradouro quanto sua paixão. Quando duas forças se unem, nasce uma verdadeira tempestade de inovação, guiada pelas cores vermelho, branco e azul!
Quando essa equipe entra na arena é impossível não entrar no ritmo. A energia dessa equipe vem como uma flecha para quem está ao redor. Convidamos a tribo para receber o prêmio.

Esta equipe demonstrou um profundo conhecimento dos processos de engenharia para concepção do seu robô. Apresentou um projeto de engenharia bem documentado, com um “robot book” impecável, descrevendo todos os processos para construção: pré-detalhamento, matriz SWOT e construção de protótipos. Neste distrito, esta equipe, além de profissional, é federal.

Com espírito engenhoso, a equipe encaixou cada engrenagem do respeito e da colaboração. Engrenou equipes, se reinventou e manteve o mecanismo em sincronia usando o sol como energia. Eles são fanáticos por profissionalismo gracioso.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Dizem que estes répteis gostam de ficar sozinhos tomando sol, porém na verdade são muito hospitaleiros e vivem cercados de gente. Criativos, eles juntaram vários elementos de forma inusitada. Varrendo todos os corais que encontram pelo chão, pontuam sem parar !

Essa equipe apesar de não estar em seu habitat natural consegue nadar com confiabilidade pela arena. Garantindo robustez e agilidade ao seu robô, trabalhando com todos os elementos do jogo. Esse réptil está completando 20 anos de evolução e abocanhou esse prêmio como um robô de alta qualidade.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Eles não se abalam por nada, estão prontos para resistir a qualquer instabilidade. Fizeram tecnologia e muita lógica para se estabilizar. Eles vão fazer chover bolas de sabão para comemorar em Blumenau.

Quando está equipe se encontrou perdida em águas profundas. Com sua visão computacional eles souberam encontrar o menor caminho. Atuou como os tubarões, usando seus sensores para buscar o caminho para seus objetivos.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Nesta jornada, seu barco navega em busca de soluções inovadoras. Entre corais e correntes de tecnologia, seu robô carrega a essência da equipe, provando que a robótica pode ser tão vistosa quanto às próprias ondas do mar. Trazendo a maresia leve pro cerrado, guiado pela sabedoria de antenas sempre atentas, transformando imaginação em identidade e desafio em aventura.

A equipe vencedora do FIRST Impact Award é composta por jovens talentosos e dedicados que se destacam no cenário da robótica com projetos inovadores e um compromisso notável com a educação, são reconhecidos pelo empenho em iniciativas de mentoria e assistência, ajudando a criar e apoiar novas equipes de robótica no mundo inteiro. Com uma forte presença nas redes sociais e uma abordagem inovadora para a educação desenvolvem projetos que promovem equidade, diversidade e inclusão, garantindo que mais jovens tenham acesso às oportunidades oferecidas pela robótica. Iniciativas que oferecem projetos STEAM acessíveis e de baixo custo que comprovadamente já impactaram mais de 100.000 jovens. Essa equipe é fanática pela robótica e com a engrenagem perfeita transforma vidas e inspira futuras gerações.

Esta equipe demonstrou estar mega atenta aos caminhos para a valorização da engenharia dentro das comunidades escolares, demonstrando com suas ações a missão da FIRST. Desenvolveram materiais para inserir crianças em um universo tecnológico que ajuda a iluminar suas vidas e guiá-las para o mundo da engenharia e ciência e com isso alçarem altos voos em suas jornadas. Como a ave que os representa, possuem robustez e força, provando que todas as crianças e jovens, podem voar alto.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Essa equipe nos impressionou com a elegância e funcionalidades do seu robô. Mostraram soluções de design inteligentes e mecanismos muito compactos. Eles provaram que tem a engenharia sob controle.

Essa equipe trouxe diversos truques e ferramentas para o PIT. Soluções de robô expostas e ideias divertidas chamaram a atenção de todos. Eles mostraram que para disseminar a STEAM e nossos valores devemos levar a criatividade ao infinito.

Essa equipe se orgulha por estar disseminando em sua região a paixão pela robótica. Entenderam a importância de capacitar professoras, envolveram as prefeituras e idealizaram campeonatos. Quando o assunto é inspirar outros jovens, eles acertaram o X da questão.

Como un gran pasaro, volarán lejos para cruzar fronteras. Volando solos en cielos nunca antes explorados, superando barreras monetarias y aduaneras, están en el camino correcto para mayores logros. Directo desde los Andes, vamos a tomar un té?

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: ⁠Esta equipe nos demonstrou que muitas coisas que poderiam virar poeira, podem se tornar arte e uma ferramenta para sustentabilidade de pessoas e famílias. Trouxeram para nós ações para a redução do impacto ambiental demonstrando ter entendido os objetivos da competição e missão da FIRST. Mostraram para nós um plano de ações para continuidade da equipe com as novas gerações e engajamento com seus patrocinadores, que a estrela desta equipe continue a brilhar sempre.

Diretamente de um vale, um time unido que transforma desafios em conquistas. Mostraram sua força, companheirismo e sinergia em cada ação. Por trás de sua aparência feroz, seu mascote é um verdadeiro guardião, sempre pronto para abraçar e unir a equipe com seus músculos

Assim como um animalzinho, a equipe se mostrou ágil e engenhosa. Com um robô projetado para a excelência, a equipe mostrou como cada detalhe no processo conta durante a jornada. A equipe têm um robô que nos fez lembrar a agilidade e olhar atento de uma VESPA!

A equipe tem os core values estampados em suas atitudes. Entenderam que a troca entre membros, mentores e patrocinadores não é só material, mas principalmente intelectual. Compartilharam suas ideias para mais de 8 países. Foram atômicos em mostrar como os Orbis invadiram os céus.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Sua jornada começou lá pelos lados do Planalto Central. Virando e girando, criaram a melhor posição para pontuar. Uniram cérebro e máquina para encantar.

Eles descansam tranquilos pelos campos dos sertões. Porém quando entram na arena mostram toda sua qualidade, com força na união e rodando com durabilidade. Resistente como o aço, esses touros são demais.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: No meio de todos os obstáculos encontrados no fundo do oceano, houve uma equipe que com sua ampla visão conseguiu focar nos objetivos, se destacando por seu controle de velocidade, posicionamento e capacidade de se adaptar no ambiente marinho. Venham abocanhar seu prêmio!

Essa equipe reuniu vários elementos que, juntos, compuseram uma excelente solução de automação. Seu robô apresenta uma operação autonoma muito consistente, entregando uma perfomance singular, com alta velocidade. Com eles, a cidade ficará a salvo.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Algumas cores não passam despercebidas, mas poucas conseguem se tornar uma verdadeira assinatura. Do robô ao Pit, dos uniformes aos acessórios e projetos, a equipe abraçou uma identidade visual intensa, cuidadosamente projetada para criar uma imagem marcante e harmoniosa. Com uma estética ousada e tom vibrante, a equipe vencedora é aquela que veste, constrói e vive a vida cor-de-rosa.

Finding an Impact winner truly challenged the judges. We found our answer in the natural world. Whether participating in local community events and parades or reaching out across the globe, these jungle dwellers leave their mark. Taking the time to ask what voices are missing in FIRST shows this team's commitment to making FIRST available for all. Go Baby Go all the way to Championships.

This award recognizes a team that inspires its community to greater heights in respect for engineering. They provided design guides to introduce engineering to many students who might not otherwise get involved, and about a third of their school is involved with the team. There’s a saying that it’s not easy being green, but they made it look effortless with green everywhere in their pit and robot, and a robot petting zoo to make things fun. It was a totally appropriate look for a Gator!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This high-flying team performed well, and looked good doing it. The clean integration and coordination of their mechanisms was truly something to behold. It allowed them to zip around the field fast enough to give you "whiplash".

From hosting FLL to building with skill, Their robot's design shows technical will. SWOT analysis and controls so sublime, Show culture well-rounded time after time. As titanic forces both on and off the field, Their connection to community fully revealed.
This sweet new team has come a long way. The buzz is all about their kindness and cooperation, but they will axe their way to the top!

All teams have to overcome obstacles to carry on, with challenges finding space, mentors, and funding. Despite the pandemic and losing their original space, they built steadily improved robots and created an extensive outreach program. Once things were going well, they then were shut out for a while by the recent fires. Despite all that, they exploded back and are here and looking to their future.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team rings a bell when it comes to achieving sustainability. They have cultivated the seeds in them community spreading STEM awareness. This tribe is the flower of the competition.

All FIRST teams love robots and their communities. This small team has really focused on being an embodiment of STEM to their community as much as they can with their resources. Their community and school events has flown high, even creating a baby bird. For flying high with the spirit of FIRST, we congratulate Team 7607, the Blackbirds.
This team used their excellent engineering to climb high in the rankings. It was the equations in their engineering notebook that really dazzled the judges, though. Somebody give them a banana!

When others were in need, this team in BLUE stepped up with steady support. Sharing tools, knowledge, and encouragement, their actions gave hope and opportunity, showing that true professionalism means lifting others as you rise.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team rose from the dark depths with twin towers. With this "do it yourself" approach to create a light as a feather robot, the creativity was obvious. We love watching twitchy go.
From deep in the reef came a crew whose robot was sturdy and true. / Its arm telescoped just right glided through with might. / From space they descend but on ground they contend.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Many robots use an array of cameras to circumnavigate the field. However, this robot ALSO used theirs to autonomously locate more coral on the floor. It's no surprise that they're having such an EPIC competition season.

This team impressed the judges with their sophisticated code for coordinating the motion of multiple mechanisms. The robot combined unique senses and passive mechanisms to reach the top at record speeds. Their software simulation let them swing around the field, while staying out of the "hurt box".

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Though not new to the scene, new efforts brought bright colors with team unity as a primary goal. Meticulous work with font & paint chips, their brand can be seen all over the community. Surf's up, dude!

Breaking down barriers is just the beginning of this team's impact. Where others might be held back by disability, distance, or disadvantage, this team ensures that barriers to STEAM education are never obstacles that can't be overcome. They don’t just teach the next generation — they reach every generation. From preschoolers to nursing home residents, this team is proving that no one is too young, too old, or too different to find a home in STEAM. Through international mentorship, online programs, and sending robots to the far corners of the world — even Antarctica — their classroom now spans every continent. This team isn’t just opening doors. They’re building entirely new ones — and making sure no one is left behind when they swing open.

The door’s always open at this large and enthusiastic team, which has created a robust pipeline starting with their strong presence at local community events, summer LEGO camps and numerous FLL teams. Judges were particularly impressed by their continuous reflections and the use of survey data to assess their outreach effectiveness and identify areas for expansion such as securing a $12,000 grant to fund FLL teams in underserved communities. Over the past two years, they have even hosted an Engineering Expo at their school by recruiting their state senator to publicize the event, drawing over 1,500 attendees.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team’s robot has well-designed structures and mechanisms made with CNC machined, 3D printed, and welded components that showcase both modularity and robustness. Their elevator and arm soars through the air and dives onto the reef to score coral -- with a very, VERY specific angle. Their custom designs, including 3D printed TPU swerve wheels, enables strong, functional performance of their avian automation to fly through their routines with high efficiency.

While this team has tripled in size since inception, their contribution to FIRST has been immeasurable. The judges were impressed by how they BRIDGED gaps in local STEM programs by creating FLL teams and a summer camp that is free for participants, and hosting a long-standing regional and a local kickoff event. Their inaugural summer off-season event really rocked the boat.

This team tirelessly shares their FIRST knowledge to foster growth, with significant outreach efforts in local communities. Their dedication to teamwork and inclusion strengthens their group while inspiring others to join the FIRST movement, like hardworking bees in a flourishing garden.

This young team has turned challenge into opportunity—creating a space where knowledge is passed down, newcomers are embraced, and every voice has a place. In just two years, they’ve quadrupled in size, rebuilding after the loss of their lead mentor and a fire that threatened to halt their journey. But they kept moving forward—emerging from Karl the Fog with a sense of purpose and unity.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team isn’t just building robots; they’re cultivating a sustainable future. By recycling materials, organizing beach cleanups, and engaging in conservation efforts, they actively embody their school’s ‘One Planet Living’ ethos. Their structured approach to leadership and documentation ensures their mission endures for generations to come.

This team's contagious energy electrified the crowd! They didn’t just compete—they celebrated every match. They lit up the field with their joyful cheers and signature dance. Their unshakable positivity embodies the enthusiasm and teamwork that define the spirit of this award.

From initial brainstorming to design iteration, this team was able to develop designs for ease of assembly and serviceability, including intentional failure points to avoid robot failure during matches. On the reef, you may find this team shooting algae into the barge or snacking on fish. With full robot CAD, FEA of critical parts, and a custom vision system for robot alignment, their engineering prowess is undeniable.

This team leads with heart, building a culture of kindness, respect, and teamwork that shines on and off the field. They lift others up—sharing tools, lending hands, and celebrating every team’s wins like their own. Thanks to their prime location, they go the extra mile—literally—finding and delivering parts to teams in need so no one’s left behind.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This year, every team learned just how difficult it is to move a 148 lb robot even a few inches while also extended 6 feet in the air. One team beat this challenge with a full size intake that orients, shifts, and flips the coral -- just as a start. The robot then firmly grabs the coral and uses a lift, another flip, and a strategic extension along an extra degree of freedom to reach the reef and score!

This team has proven they’re in their element—and it shows. With a simplified design built for battle and a checklist system that would make an air traffic controller proud, their machine hasn’t just survived the competition—it’s thrived in it. No breakdowns, no drama, just quiet, relentless performance match after match. In a regional full of diverse teams, this hometown team set the standard and showed everyone how it’s done.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Unlike their namesake, this team focused on consuming *algae*. They tuned hundreds of parameters to develop a robust vision system to find algae in the wild, regardless of where it is on the field. With the push of a button, they can zoom towards it like a hungry flightless bird.

There are many teams that have made waves, but there was one but whose current ran deep. For the autonomous period, they simply list the posts they want, and the coral is scored. In teleop, they hit a button, and POOF, it's on!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team embraced the reefscape theme with an aquatic design that flows through everything. Named after a formidable sea monster from Greek mythology, their robot Scylla turns heads with its clean lines and appealing patterns. The team collaborates while designing and refining their art through feedback and iterations. With a cohesive theme and polished execution, they blend myth, creativity, and aesthetics.

This year's winning team has built a remarkably sustainable program, empowering students year after year to excel in STEM fields. With an impressive outreach program that has reached over 6,000 students, they’ve partnered with local schools and a museum to spark curiosity — even creating a memorable yellow bug robot for children to explore engineering concepts. Known for their unwavering commitment to promoting women in STEM and proudly representing their red, white, and blue colors with the strength of true patriots, this team’s impact has left a lasting mark. Congratulations to team 4135, the Iron Patriots.

This year, the Engineering Inspiration Award is presented to a team that has truly exemplified what it means to be an ambassador of STEM education in their local community through numerous impactful outreach efforts. This team has engaged in a wide variety of initiatives that have significantly advanced not only their program but have had quantifiable impact with many students in their community. This team have SWOOPED down from their NEST and impacted over 3000 students, significantly raising awareness about the importance of STEM. Their commitment to inclusivity ensures that every student, regardless of their background or abilities, has the opportunity to explore the exciting world of engineering. They partner with local schools, providing mentorship and guidance to younger students. They have host numerous outreach events, including FLL tournaments, co-host an off-season FRC competition, developed a six week summer camp for low-income, minority families, and a program to educate students with disabilities centered around STEM and robotics. For their outstanding commitment to fostering a love for engineering and technology within their community, and for their unique and impactful outreach programs, we are proud to present the Engineering Inspiration Award to Team 2073, EagleForce.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: "Many teams build with strength and might, but some go further to design just right. With modular swaps and weight cut back, this team’s sleek machine is dressed in orange and black. For engineering and style that truly awe, the Industrial Design Award goes to 972 Iron Claw!"

This year’s recipient of the Judges Award has consistently gone above and beyond, not only in their technical endeavors but also in their commitment to inspiring the next generation of STEM leaders. They have dedicated countless hours to outreach events in the Sacramento Regional community, specifically targeting underrepresented groups in STEM education, ensuring that all students have the opportunity to engage with science and technology. Their initiatives include weekly hands-on workshops, mentorship programs, and engaging activities that spark interest in robotics and engineering among young learners. By fostering an inclusive environment, they are breaking down barriers and making a lasting systematic difference in their community. It is with great pleasure that I announce the winner of this year's Judges Award: Team 3598, the Systematic Eliminators! Your dedication to outreach and your passion for inspiring others in the field of STEM exemplify the true spirit of FIRST.

A rookie team, fresh on the scene, with perseverance and a robot so keen. In a world where gears and circuits spin, a team stands out for the world they begin. They cook up solutions, with toys they fixed, and inspire young minds with STEM as their mix- please congratulate team 10212 circuit bakers

This award honors a young team that rose to the challenge, kneading community support to perfection. They teamed up with their local libraries, schools, and ftc teams, proving they have unstoppable might. Our Rising All Star that’s shining so bright lets's all raise a toast to Team 9400, BagelBytes

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This award honors a team whose eco-friendly mindset truly embody sustainability and ‘otta’ be an example for all. This group cuts down on waste by using reusable components, off-the-shelf transmissions, and even rethinking buttons, shirts, and manufacturing processes. Please join us in congratulating Team 6665, C-Otters, winner of the Sustainability Award for their innovative, green approach to FRC!

This team soars above the competition, bringing an infectious energy that lifts the entire event. With their signature feathers, relentless enthusiasm, and dedication to lifting up others, they create an atmosphere that’s impossible to ignore. From their nest in the valley to the roar of the stands, their spirit takes flight, proving they are truly a flock like no other! Congratulations to team 1671 Buchanan Bird Brains winner of the Team Spirit Award

Some teams build great robots, but truly elite teams design machines that are as clever as they are competitive. With a beautifully machined elevator for precise placement and an intake hiding a climber like a cobra waiting to strike, this team’s engineering was both elegant and powerful. Even when faced with an almost solo match, they never backed down—proving that no matter the challenge, this team always finds a way to SCREAM past expectations Congratulations to this year’s Excellence in Engineering Award winner… TEAM SCREAM – FRC 4522

"Some teams build robots, some build champions—but this team? They build opportunities. This team has not only dominated on the field but has changed lives beyond it. They created the first FTC League in the Valley region, sponsor 12 FTC teams, and dedicate their time to shaping the next generation of STEM leaders. Through their Summer Robo Camp and STEM for Girls Conference, they ensure that knowledge, innovation, and opportunity are within everyone’s reach. For their unwavering dedication to Gracious Professionalism and their impact on the future of STEM, please join us in celebrating this year’s winners… Team 8768, the CTEC Titans!"

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Time for the Creativity Award, honoring a team whose design reeled us in from the start.” “With a rotating ‘coral grip’ that screws tubes onto the rack, bounces balls into the chute, and alerts the driver only when needed, this bot really makes waves—then hangs on the chains to seal the deal.” “Dive in and cheer for Team 4698, Raider Robots, winners of the Creativity Award for their truly buoyant approach to autonomous control

In a sea of precision, they rise with careful flair, From organized and meticulous wiring to each coral placed with accuracy This team is taking over the Quality Award, Team 2135 Presentation Invasion!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: “This award goes to a team that pushed autonomy to new heights. Their robot blends driver feedback and advanced automation for a truly next-level performance." “With automated scoring for tubes and balls, the driver only steps in when the controller rumbles—otherwise, the robot can even hang on the chains solo at match’s end.” “Congratulations to Team 1678, Citrus Circuits, winner of the Innovation in Control Award for their groundbreaking autonomous design!”

They roll through auto, they make it so neat, Four coral secured, no chance for defeat. Like cheese dust that lingers, their skills stay supreme, Their tracking is flawless, their coding’s a dream! They roll to success with precision and proof, The Autonomous Award goes to The Cheesy Poofs!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: From a distance, the arena hums with the electrifying energy of innovation, where every robot showcases the dedication and creativity of its team. As you draw closer to the pit, a bold, vibrant green catches your eye—a testament to the meticulous craftsmanship of Team . Their robot, gleaming in its signature hue, along with their coordinated attire, symbolizes the unity and passion driving their success. Congratulations to Team 7528, Nuts and Bolts, for earning the prestigious Imagery Award!

Achieving global influence, these young people have forged valuable partnerships with national and international organizations. Always pushing toward the goal yet never holding the ball, they inspire youth, peers and elders alike. They’ll gladly be your dragon, providing a “sparc” for your journey, especially if you can’t quite see them.

They light the way where darkness long had grown. Through hands-on outreach, young minds begin to soar. With lessons shared and passions deeply sown, they open doors once locked to those before. A roaring force that lifts up dreams untold, these dinos inspire and claim the prize in gold! The engineering inspiration award goes to Team 5817- Uni-Rex!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: With sleek Gray lines, seamless integration, and a form that follows flawless function, this team proves that good design is no accident. "Sting Grey" is a masterpiece built to last. Every inch is designed for performance, speed, and class. Congratulations Team 973, Greybots!

Dean Kamen says, "They leave, even after only 1 season, with a vision, with confidence, and with a sense that they can create their own futures." As judges, we were emotionally captivated by how FIRST brought friends together, built resilience, and created new pathways for futures after high school. This is what FIRST is all about. We are excited to award the Judges' Award to Cougar Pride Robotics- Team 8087!

They come from a city known for sunshine and perseverance. New to the game, but they showed the heart of veterans. They tackled every obstacle with curiosity, courage, and class. Let's hear it for your Rookie All-Star- Team 10336!

This team is a group of dreamers whose budget limited their ability to compete last year. Realizing sponsorship is partnership, they are back, bigger and better. Their impact reaches beyond the field to the rural community where they teach English and bring STEM to those communities. Congratulations to 8585! You are a Rising All Star!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Saving scrap metal isn't the only thing that makes this team sustainable, but this team's commitment to sustaining their membership is what really impressed the judges. This SUPER team finds the time to give their members the full FIRST experience, despite only participating for two years. It's going to take more than Kryptonite to stop this team!
They cheered for all through triumph and through test, with battle cries and horns upon their crest, the team spirit award is claimed by Team 701, the RoboVikes, the best!
With sticky persistence, this team engineered elegance. They iterated functional solutions with deep intelligence. With all their arms, their robot grasped the competition.

This team is always quick to answer the call. They make parts off the field in order to get bots on the field. The judges couldn't help but notice their demonstration of gracious professionalism when stopped by teams and coaches expressing gratitude to the Titans.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Drawing on the muses of ancient Greece, this team’s designs are effective and graceful. Coming down from the north with dramatic and efficient shapes, Coral, Algae, and Cages all knew their place in this robot. Lifted to new heights with graceful elevator and a dramatic polycarbonate gear, the Creativity award goes to Team 971 Spartan Robotics.

From design processes and documentation, this team's dedication to quality is clear. Their meticulous wiring creates a robot as intricately and carefully constructed as a nest. This high standard of work created a truly "sqwuak"-worthy design. Congratulations, Team 1671, the Buchanan Bird Brains!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: When control met strategy, this team stood out. By fusing object detection, robot coordination, and human input, they became a playoff powerhouse. This team has been Dunkin on the competition.
This team's autonomous is pinch worthy. Their robot lobbed game pieces to the reef with consistency and precision. Led by their crimson antenna, this autonomous is truly Torr-ific!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team's royal presence stands out in a crowd. Their innovative branding and integration in their initiatives has a positive influence on their team, community, and beyond. This team will rocket to the top!

This team has taken a deep DIVE into what it means to create an impact. They started small at school, then expanded their reach by training new coaches and securing funds to grow the FIRST network across their school district. With confidence, persistence, and professionalism, they have inspired everyone from toddlers to city officials. They may be NERDY, but this small robotics team is certainly mighty!

This team’s strong media presence SPARKS the discovery of FIRST and STEM. Their yearn for knowledge beyond robotics IGNITES hope. Through running summer camps and creating many robotics teams in their country, they flamed of inspiration for many. They are passing the torch to the next generations. "BONNE CHANCE!"

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: With a strong foundation of circuitry, this team designed multiple innovative mechanisms. They showed flexibility by placing multiple belts on a single axis. Their creative solutions are as flashy at their pink and green team colors.
The judges were impressed by the speed of this robot. Coral could not hide from this squid. From their custom Swerve Drive to the impressive Control Panel, CALAMARI ruled the ocean.
These birds entered into FRC this year. As a rookie team, they forged opportunities in their community. They soared over the competition. Fly Iron Eagles, Fly!
When facing a red tide of financial difficulties, this team cast a wide net to ensure success, overcoming language barriers to educate new members. They led by example to grow their Ohana.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Through inclusivity and mentorship, this team is trying to change the world. They understand sustainability is not only about the environment, but also nurturing future generations. Together we rise, together we change!

Tenacious, courageous, enduring, extraordinary. When this team speaks, we are compelled to listen: their enthusiasm is infectious. Climbing to new heights, these Hall of Famers bring their commitment to family, FIRST, and community.

We celebrate a team that mastered the REEFSCAPE challenge with true pack brilliance. They displayed engineering prowess with design and prototype, a caliper success. This team shows that NERDS are indeed inheriting the Earth.

At events and throughout the season, you can find them around the corner. When you need help, a member wearing green will be the helper. Year after year, they are always on the move, trucking teams and equipment from one state to another.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: In the world of varsity robotics, one team grabbed their problem by the ropes. Who needs more motors or programmers? These queens of the jungle let their creativity roar!
This team has data at the core. From hidden wiring to consistently high scores, this team impressed many judges with how they fought the war.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: The speed and accuracy of this robot had opponents seeing red. Navigating all realms of the sea – source, reef, and barge – made their robot A-STAR. New paths were born on the field at a touch of the screen.
This team swam smoothly across the field, autonomously crowning the reef 3 times per match. With their lobster claw, they placed coral to perfection.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team shines bright and brings light where they live. Through adversity and challenges, they bring inspiration to their neighborhood. Rising like a rose from the concrete, this team reaches new heights.

This team’s impact extends far beyond the competition field, building lasting partnerships and empowering the next generation of engineers. Their efforts have impacted hundreds of teams worldwide, and by helping establish engineering classes at their school, they’ve demonstrated an unmatched commitment to supporting both the local and broader community. They created a hub for FRC teams with a full field that serves both local and international teams. With over half of their members being alumni of their outreach programs, they have created a foundation that supports students from elementary school to FRC. Their energy is electrifying and their dedication to mentoring others is truly powerful. They have closed the circuit on innovation, ensuring that the current of progress will keep flowing for years to come.

This team did a great job of “painting a picture” of how the mission of FIRST can make an impact within their local and global community By partnering with local institutions to teach and mentor FTC and FLL teams, they have been able to recruit future members and teach them the Core Values of FIRST. This extends to their skills classes, summer academies, community engagement, and an extensive online footprint, as they go for “baroque” to inspire the next generation of FIRST members. "Orange" you glad you joined us.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: From the crisp lines of their bumpers, to the smooth paths of their trailblazing autonomous scoring routines, this robot has a strong grasp on the competition. When they noticed a small listing in their climb, the modular system allowed a simple shift to adjust for their center of mass. Sensor fusion effectively doubles the width of their claw allowing for flexible intake and optimized scoring options. Each of their robust subsystems are removable for blazing fast refinements and repairs.

The judges want to recognize this winning team for being the complete package, both on and off the field. Their robot went above and beyond, with a creative and well-crafted auto-indexing intake. They found clever ways to merge engineering training with fundraising and outreach, by creating kits designed and machined by students, while selling the finished products to raise funds. They “ride the wave” of their team’s success and skills by helping others succeed, machining parts and teaching software techniques to other FRC teams. They may bend, but they certainly don’t break.

Focused on promoting neurodiversity, this team has embraced their unique strengths to build a strong foundation for their future at FIRST. They showed remarkable resilience when faced with challenges, including a major breakdown at this competition. They exemplified gracious professionalism by seeking help and getting back in the game. It seems they have already mastered the FIRST tradition of learning to fix things quickly— a skill that will serve them well in the years to come.

With demonstrated skills in building robots, this re-built team transformed their strategy to emphasize community outreach. Over the past year, they’ve reached thousands of people, launched new FLL teams, engaged with more than 100 students, and published their resources — all with a mission to make STEM more accessible to under-represented groups. With their unwavering dedication to inclusivity, innovation, and impact ….

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Get ready to be blown away where sustainability and robotics go hand-in-hand like gears-and-motors! With community projects, exciting workshops and mentorship programs, this winning team is sparking a STEM-tastic revolution! Off-season competitions are a “reel” good time, by creating a “buzz” where innovation meets inspiration! They’re not just building bots; they’re building bridges—like the Golden Gate—connecting teams across San Francisco with resources and support.

This team made their presence known in the best way possible - with non-stop cheering, infectious energy and a true sense of community. They welcomed visitors with candies, giftbags, bingo games and boundless enthusiasm. They are not only the “brightest star” in their constellation, but they are also the loudest.

The teams ability of applying engineering principles to solve challenges effectively both on and off the fields really stands out. Their dedication to in-depth documentation ensured that their hard work and strategies translated seamlessly in their performance. Their robotic functionality demonstrates reliability and consistency. FIRST really struck a “pot of gold” with this team.

[a poem] This team believes in more than the game, Lifting others is their claim to fame. From metal scraps to shining bricks, They build the future with clever tricks. A Super Pit, a shared space wide, Helping teams compete with pride! Their motto speaks of what’s in store, Tomorrow is theirs—they open the door! In white they stand, a guiding light, Congrats to Plus Ultra—pure and bright!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This robot, like an eager angler fish pining for the surface, featured a jaw with a prominent underbite to pull themselves out of the water. While an overabundance of unstable elements and heavy metals in their robot’s diet may have prevented this clever fish from also eating Algae with the same mechanism, this team managed to perform “swimmingly” in matches by deftly depositing fresh coral in the reef at all levels.

[a poem] This team's design is geared with manufacturing in mind, Their elevator and funnel never got into a bind. With robust and efficient scoring a defensive exemption, Their systems certainly never had any gremlin!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team’s single-driver strategy featured user input with adaptive haptics, and simple materials to make an effective robot. They optimized energy to hit all their silver linings by using cardboard to intake and manage game pieces effortlessly. They are “scrappy….. but not so crappy”.

This team's autonomous routine impressed us all with its 3-piece performance. In the pit, they displayed their key competencies in their control board, auto-alignment, and stall detection. This is only their second year, but they've already mastered the “3-key salute”

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: [a poem] Brilliant branding, bold and bright, Bumpers blue and built just right! Buzzing, bustling, bringing the fun, Balonku beams while banners stun! Big and balanced, bold with spots, Bow to the best… The Boba Bots!"

This team goes into their com; finding a space like gears in a working system. Each member is an integral part of this team’s mission to their communities, focusing on their impact on underrepresented students and those with disabilities. With their ability to spread addictive manufacturing to everyone they can.

Supporting each team with passion and pride. Guiding young minds with knowledge and care. In a purple den, their passion runs deep, Lifting up others so dreams take a leap. They weave bright futures in The Loom they share, With vision and heard, they light the way, Inspiring the future – starting today!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Their electric light gives them a purple flare. This team’s robot scores L fours without a care. Fire on high! Their pendulum arm jets into the air.
With smooth actuation, coral's gentle hold, No human can replace this robot’s grace. A hidden belt, the wondrous arm ascends, Through brain pan's electrical maze, its power transcends.

We had this team high our list. Coming far from home they lifted our spirits with their teamwork and field performance. We look up to them as they perform beyond their experience. This award goes to the rookies from the Rockies.
