This team isn’t shy when it comes to leadership and growth. With documentation and teamwork built to last, these Bears are charging fast.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team is rooted in strong family values and is primarily driven by student members. With a strong commitment to sustainability, they focus on recycling and reusing materials for their projects, reducing waste while giving back to their local community. They prioritize collaboration with local sponsors rather than large corporations, aiming to support their community through initiatives like painting curbs in neighborhood streets.
Spreading the joy of engineering. With a spark of knowledge, the smoke is clearing. Call the firefighters, their passion is searing.

This team’s robot is sturdy in the field and certainly can’t be startled and tipped. Equipped with pneumatic grip and a powerful climber, it will be a long time before you put this bot out to pasture!

Traveling far and wide, this team remains prepared for anything. Despite being fierce creatures, they are balanced with their nature to lend a paw. Their generosity and Aloha spirit is felt with every action.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: With a robust sleek robot and arm design rare Printed materials zooming by fast like a hare, Spline funnel collection shows creativity at its peak!

Quality has been FIRST and foremost in this robotz long adventure. Quickly sailing through troubled waters, collecting coral and removing algae throughout the journey. This legendary team is more than good, more than great.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: When the challenge is to negotiate the Reefscape, few creatures will have what it takes to tame coral reefs and algae nets. So, it should come as no surprise that a team of dolphins pass the test of innovation and control just fine.
Their auto ranks above the rest, Three corals in fifteen seconds is their quest, Their scorpion tail strikes above the rest.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: With a streamlined coral hooking design, this team is hard to miss. Taking a walk on the wild side, their striking green and gold attire hippo-notized the competition.

This Impact Award team believes that every student in their state needs STEAM and puts funding to their passion. They translate FIRST projects into resources for all in their country. They are roaring with FIRST to "cer"tainly be a compassionate and collaborative team.

This team strikes with impact by building FLL teams, hosting an FLL tournament, and running free robotics workshops at their local library. With outreach spanning 25 community events and 20 schools, they don't just inspire - they take action. Their dedication to STEM continues year-round, hosting numerous off-season events in their own robotics league, leading the charge like true commanders indeed!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: FIRST robots can often look pretty intimidating, and this one brought to mind an ancient monster. Its wagging head to place coral really captured the imagination of the judges, especially in how well it cleverly made a nest of the rest of its robot to make a scoring package. We are glad this atomic dinosaur crossed oceans to rampage on our fields here!

This team is a team that is hard to miss. Their professionalism, creativity, and branding helps them to soar to new heights. Bringing a new meaning to "CAD", their primary colors help them fly high. This team's trading card gives us everything we need to present the Judges Award.
This team had to overcome building their robot in pieces to accommodate flying to this competition. Their robust robot incorporated excellent design elements.

When faced with a labyrinth of challenges, this team refused to be trapped. With determination and hand drawn artistry, they rebuilt their journey from the ground up, crafting a story of ancient legends. Soaring once more, they are the Rising All Stars!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: It’s hard to create a robot that makes as small an impact on the planet as possible. This team decided to treat the planet with the care the inhabitants of a big island might lavish on their home. They not only create a well-performing robot out of parts of a boat, a gate, and some wood, but have been nuturing fellow sharks and real coral. For being a beacon of sustainability,

All FIRST teams have great team spirit, but this team eliminated the competition. Their spirit sines out from the rotunda to all over California and beyond. They ses-tymatically built a robo-alliance to support their community.

Part of the FIRST experience is creating impressive robots with limited time and resources. This team, faced with a season shortened by two weeks by outside circumstances, decided to focus on algae as a niche but later added on coral scoring and climb. Their six schools came together to keep their red flame alive even in the face of historic fires.

This team's mission is clear and bright / To spread goodwill with all their might. / With helping hands and wisdom shared / They show all teams how much they care. / Through inclusion, they take a stand / For equity strong and justice grand. / With nerves of iron, bold and true, / They lift up others in all they do.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Teams make many decisions when they design a robot. This team used a rainbow of techniques to create its robot, with an integrated package with a lot of attention to driver interface and access to electronics. The judges were particularly impressed by their innovative pneumatic climb mechanism that captured the cage as if it were grasped by the hand of a Titan.

This clean and simple design was clever and well executed. Their robot could reach great heights even though it had to fit in a suitcase. These bears built a great robot that let them show off their true colors.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team grabbed control, gave it a spin, and yelled ‘Yippee!’ while making their robot a Superstar! With slick swerve moves they crafted a robot that flips machine states like a champ! For their dazzling smarts and a legacy of viral videos, they earned the Innovation in Control Award.
I overheard that the autonomous award goes to a California team that scored high. This team likes to name their robots after ripples.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team's vision was as bright as their colors. The displays in their pit, robot, and uniforms created a striking, unified presence. They soar above the crowd in orange and purple.

Since its inception, this team has demonstrated resilience, never backing down from a single challenge; AGAIN and AGAIN they transform obstacles into opportunities they can use to their advantage. The judges were particular impressed by the lengths they went through to design the entire team around financial accessibility. They ignite a spark by inspiring young minds in their community through partnerships with a diverse group of organizations. This team stood out as STARS with their effective use of assessment surveys and the engineering design process to find members of their community who might not otherwise be exposed to STEM opportunities. It was clear how they identified a problem, collected quantitative data and made strategic decisions to achieve maximum impact with continuous feedback cycles. This team is also building alliances in their community to strengthen the FIRST bond to unite the FRC teams in their district into one cohesive, functioning SYSTEM. Their SYSTEMATIC approach at self improvement and expanding FIRST footprint operates in perfect harmony like parts of a CIRCUIT BOARD to create meaningful impact for many years to come.

In addition to sustaining their long-lasting initiatives that impact their local FIRST community, this team has found creative ways to plan and execute several new initiatives this season. At a local and global scale, they sought to understand the needs of the underserved communities they help; focused on building a solid foundation for a meaningful education. This included both students and teachers. Having had so many of their members to through their programs has sent RIPPLES throughout their community, growing into WAVES across the world. Utilizing these DEOTHS across their team, they help everyone to SWIM FORWARD.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team made stability their priority, Shimming their gears to perfect balance between their elegance and functionality. Working with their limited resources, their design is intentional - to shoot, place, and climb. With Their 3-sided intake and sleek design, this team quickly FLUSHED the coral and the competition. Their focus on programming allows a single driver strategy to be hard to defeat

This team is on a trajectory that really impressed the judges, delivering concrete impact in their community that was well defined and clearly articulated. Their numbers are simple and show effectiveness; students who join this team attend college at fully twice the rate of their non-robotics peers. Iterating and expanding on their outreach each year they increase the pool of applicants and produce a pipeline of qualified students to feed the bigger FIRST project A short poem….. Their drone initiative flew to skies BLUE. The Judges Award for an inspiring trajectory goes to the numerically named Project 2 - 1 - 2.

(a poem) This team began their very first YEAR, With curious minds and no hint of FEAR. They quickly learned the biggest TRICK: A full system’s not built up QUICK. They’re learning systems, building FAST, Their FIRST steps strong—and built to LAST. Light on weight but big on HEART, They’ve shown they’re ready for the START.

While this team isn't a rookie, they are a young team that is really starting to take off. Despite losing 9 seniors, they've grown their freshmen as replacements. They've expanded their outreach and fundraising to avoid relying on member fees as their only budget mechanism, and for the first time this year they used the magic of CAD to invent their own design. We look forward to seeing what they'll grow next in their ROBOT GARDEN -

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Illustrating their belief that much like the vast universe, there are endless possibilities for success when individuals come together with a common purpose. Over the past 3 years, this team’s recruiting efforts have led to an astonishing growth of nearly 500%. This team is dedicated to expanding its reach within the community and growing its team, recognizing the GRAVITATIONAL PULL of collaboration and shared goals.

(a poem) From pits to the field, their pride is LOUD, A team that stands out in any CROWD. Toys in hand and spirit to SHARE, Their love for FIRST is EVERYWHERE! Two bots built, with wiring CLEAN, Their teamwork shows in every SCENE. The vibes they bring are off the CHARTS, With bubbles and fun and purple HEARTS!

(a poem) Between events, they never REST, They tune their bot to be its BEST. They tweak, they test, they OPTIMIZE, With every match, they ANALYZE. A funnel fixed, a claw REFINED, Their build shows off an engineer’s MIND. No fixes needed, no tools to DEPLOY— The pit crew got bored… and jumped for JOY! They track the field with VR FLAIR, A Quest headset? Now that’s RARE!

(a poem) From the very beginning, this team jumped right IN taking the helm, helping with planning, and worked from WITHIN. Regardless of the ask, they never COMPLAINED. Their helpfulness and support never WAINED One thing for sure, if we were out on a PLANK This team would rescue us, so we never SANK

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: When off-the-shelf options wouldn’t work for their bot, they VENTURED into the world of fabrication. Their creative solutions won’t pull the WOOL over your eyes. This winning team is leading their nation’s robotics program forward.

(a poem) They ditched the plastic, went full SEND, SRPP gives them that lightweight BEND. Their build is clean, their bot is TIGHT, With powder blue, it’s quite the SIGHT! From a pivoting elevator to gearboxes SPUN, Their pride and joy: ETR 21.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team is on their own QUEST to master the depths of V-Slam and sensor fusion. With highly automated scoring and path planning, the drive team is in full control of the reef, coral, and algae. Breaking away from the pack, we know detecting algae will help them clean reefs beyond the shores of Reefscape.

Decked out in RED HATS, this team worked all year long on improving their autonomous operations. They studied hard in the offseason to improve their capabilities and put their hard work into action this season. With help from teammates JULIE and JAZZ, they made GOLD in autonomous maneuvers. We’re not “JANKING” your chain….

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team took an obvious DEEP DIVE into the season. Their theme invites you UNDER THE REEF into a bright and calming place to escape. They eliminated unrecyclable powder-coated metal, wear eco-friendly shirts, and recycle everything they can. Dedicated to keeping it GREEN and protect these little sea creatures,

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: To help bring STEM to more students, this team developed a new curriculum to meet their school time constraints. They focused on lowering the barrier to entry by teaching core robotics principles with a simplified bot. They expanded their tools and teachings to other school districts across grades K-12. Over a few short years, they’ve proactively started multiple FLL & FTC teams, and shared technical and financial know-how with fellow FRC competitors. Their name may be a game, but they make a serious impact.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This team is ready for WAR. They – wait a minute, I need to tweak this script. Take two: this team went above and beyond to expand their local and global horizons. With their CADathons and curriculum integration with their school district, they clock in all year-round.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Unique climbs, innovative funnels, and a comprehensive tech binder were all part of this team’s competitive advantages. Linear algebra provided the insights they needed to not get confused by any directional cosigns. From reef to jungle, this hippo has made a huge splash.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: When the pressure was on, this team found a novel solution. They approached the reef like a gentle monster, and their robot truly sucks! This robotic creature vacuumed up the Judges’ Award.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This rookie team went looking for anyone that was interested in building something together. By collaborating across many classrooms, this team gathered its mentors to lead their charge. When it comes to competition these rookies are ready to brawl.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: Waddling out of the frigid zone, this team showcased excellence in both performance and innovation. Despite space constraints (and limited arms and legs to do all their tasks), they developed a cutting-edge vision system alongside a powerful scouting app, which regenerated their ability to compete. For their resilience, ingenuity, and technical prowess, we proudly honor these cephalopods as Rising All-Stars!

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team uses a practice robot to train rookies and expand community awareness and support for robotics. They funnel future students into their program by visiting all the middle schools in their area, and stage a hybrid FTC/FRC event to “Celebrate the Music.” They’re always hard at work preparing for the spring, so you’ll never catch these cubs hibernating.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This team embodies the spirit of FIRST. They share their enthusiasm with their school, their sponsors, and here at the San Diego Regional. You may know them as the laughing team – let’s celebrate the form, the function, and the joy of these “Sapiens!”

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This team’s design approach focused on modularity and resilience, which tipped the scales. Multisensor integration and quickly-swappable units kept this team moo-ving on the field, not stuck in the pit. They were udderly impressive!

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: All weekend long, the pits have been buzzing about the outstanding support that this team provides. We heard about their kindness, generosity, and Gracious Professionalism from nearly every other team. We know them for their stellar robots, but you should never underestimate that their robotics domination is rooted in how well they serve others.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: These competitors took a novel approach for funneling new ideas into their robot’s design. Turning one part into two was the key. Don’t get Messy with Nessy, and

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: When it came to solid field performance and stuning looks, this team had it all. Their design had depth, their execution was flawless, and their robot design was slick and clean: Mariana’s quality certainly stood out from the crowd.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Sensing a need for better vision, this team took camera control and execution to a new level, yet simplified it down to a button. With an adaptive navigation system, they always knew where they were; it all came down to seeing clearly.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: Navigating around the reef showed off this team’s exceptional control abilities. By automatically releasing their climber, it was always ready when needed. Echolocating in search of coral, this sea creature's prowess earned them this award.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This year’s water game was brought to you by Poseidon, king of the sea. The winning team didn’t let the Reefscape turn them to stone. When they had to leave their sword behind, they were quick on their feet and used their shield to thwart the competition. Congratulations to Perseus and Team 6695!

Like a vibrant coral reef, this team provides safety to many FIRST students. From the shallows of FLL to the depths of FRC, they provide critical year-round support to start and sustain FIRST teams. This team decided that achieving 100% adoption of their equity initiative across FRC events was not enough and is now expanding this meaningful work to other FIRST programs. We're awestruck by how fast support of their community field has bloomed. Their outreach recipe requires all ingredients—every member tags along to BAKE a better future.

Diversity and sustainability are at the core of this team’s many programs, ensuring equitable access across their home district for underrepresented groups in STEM through internal training, workshops, and industry panels. They FIGHT for STEM access in low income areas with limited opportunities all around the world, with programs ranging from their local elementary schools to active and in-person outreach in India, Taiwan, and Nigeria. With branding levels rivaling the Warner Bros, the BRIDGES they’ve BUILT are bound to BEAT the issues with the brain, the heart, and much much more in the future.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team has crafted a robot that is not only elegant in its structure and appearance, with thoughtfully chosen LED colors, but also proves its effectiveness on the field. With an illuminating LED system that’s more than just for looks, their robot guides its driver like a beacon in the HIGHLANDS, enhancing efficiency and control. For their seamless fusion of design and performance, the Industrial Design Award goes to… Team 8033 Highlander Robotics!

When the waters got rough, this team knew exactly how to adapt. By reviving and running their school's STEM classes, this team revitalized their classmates' love for STEM and literally rebuilt part of their school. Even with a majority-freshman class, we know this team can survive any storm that RAGES at sea.

This rookie team proved that GOOD is just the beginning. They lit up social media with powerful Women in STEM content, amplifying voices and connecting their country to the global FIRST community through meaningful partnerships. From a robotics club to a full-fledged FIRST team, they’re building a future that’s local, regional, and global — proving they’re not just good… they’re GOOGIRLS great.

This rising team knows that innovation has no borders. Uniting homeschooled students from the U.S. with teammates in China, they built a global team—and a robot named Quasar that shines just as bright. With scalable mechanisms and custom CPU code that isolates each component for performance, they’re not just building robots—they’re building practical technology for our future!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team is digging deep for a greener future and proving that sustainability is no FOSSILIZED idea—it’s ROARING to life! They’re growing more than just robots—they’re recycling plastics, mentoring young minds, and planting the seeds for a brighter tomorrow. It’s clear, they’re harvesting success in both their team and the environment. It’s clear they’re not EXTINCT but instinctively eco-friendly, harvesting success for both their team and the planet.

When it comes to spirit, this team leaves NOTHING TO WASTE! They recycle their energy into nonstop enthusiasm, supporting their team and dancing through the competition. You could feel their passion anywhere on this one planet.

Coral, Algae, Cage…this robot ROSE to meet every challenge the game could toss at it. It wasn’t easy as this team worked to refine their RECIPE as they sought to be the best. Their effort showed as this team BAKED their ingredients into a savory robot.

This team is making WAVES by breaking down barriers and riding the tide of teamwork. Whether it’s lending a hand with parts or offering up their machines, they always go above and beyond to help out other teams. Their positive attitude and sportsmanship are unmatched, both on and off the field, making them a true example of Gracious Professionalism. So, let’s give a round of applause to the team that embodies teamwork and support – Team 5104, the Breakerbots!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Scrubbing the floor for coral is commonplace Even into the gripper is first base Where others would add a motor Their arm's it's own rotor Their chain synchronized four-bar linkage flips with grace The award for creativity goes to Team 840, Aragon Robotics

From flawless wiring to expertly machined components, every detail of this team reflected durability and efficiency. Their robot delivered smooth, consistent performance with powerful DYNAMIC drivetrain control and precision scoring mechanisms that never faltered under pressure.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team’s achievements can’t be COMPRESSED into just a few lines. They engineer one-of-a-kind solutions, with the math to prove it. When field elements get FUNKY, they know exactly how to react. For their expert application of control principles to every challenge, we proudly present the Innovation in Control Award to Team 846: The Funky Monkeys!

Circling the reef with the speed of a great white shark but like... a shark with a full self driving package? They've brought the arctic ocean to San Francisco with their use of "polar" coordinates. At the push of a button, this robot sticks out in the Bay like a peninsula, congratulations 6036 Peninsula Robotics!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: When engineering meets artistry, this team makes magic. They don't just build—they STEAL the show. And when it comes to style, they’re not DRAGIN' their feet! For their integrated team theme and eye-catching robot design, we proudly present the Imagery Award to Team 5700: The SOTA Cyberdragons!

This team empowers girls and other underrepresented groups through workshops, summer camps, and robot demos, showing them what’s possible and paving their way to join the FRC community. Their work to expand STEM curriculum at their school has opened opportunities for every student and including both AP classes and industry certifications as educational options ensures that their graduates are fully equipped for college, trade school, or the workforce. Perhaps it is fitting that this team works out of a woodshop, since their impact is TREE-mendous and they are nailing it! Keep striving for the summit and mahalo for your impact on your community. Congratulations to the Tiki Techs Team 3880!

This team has been ROARING with creativity shaping future STEM leaders for over two decades. They've CLAWED their way through challenges and shown younger CUBS the BEAR necessities of robotics and engineering. They've left TRACKS across the FIRST community with an open-source scouting app that paws-itively benefits teams everywhere through crowd-sourced data. And speaking of rookies, their wildly successful rookie training competition has brought mechanical mayhem in the best possible way. Their enthusiasm and dedication are simply un-bear-able. Please join me in congratulating Team 766, the M-A Bears!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: In a shop where students make everything bright, Repeated 3D printing makes every design right. With student designed swerve, And ball slides that don't curve, They teach others to build with delight!

This team had everyone on the edge of their seat in every match they played. That's in addition to their extensive outreach efforts which, like their shooter, GEAR UP to give students a boost. This team was a bright spot on the field this year!

This rookie team has POUNCED on every opportunity—mentoring FLL teams, refurbishing laptops, running FTC and FLL events, and even tackling plastic waste and scrap metal recycling. They worked hard to engage sponsors, proving they’re no CUBS when it comes to impact. The Rookie All-Star Award goes to Team 10252, MechaLions!

This year’s Rising All-Star team is building a strong foundation—literally! Working out of a construction company, they’ve been hard at work laying the groundwork for STEM in their city, even starting an FTC team to expand their impact. Though they may be a small team, their ambitions are anything but—raising a GOURD-geous $60,000 this year to fuel their mission. With a vision as bright as a JACK-O’-LANTERN and a commitment to CARVING out a future in STEM, we are thrilled to present the Rising All-Star Award to… The Pumpkin Bots! 🎃

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team is SWINGING ahead in both robotics and environmental action! They've MONKEYED around rivers and gardens, cleaning up creeks, restoring rose gardens, and planting trees to prove sustainability isn't just APE business—it's their mission. With over 600 volunteer hours mentoring FLL teams, and hosting an annual FRC Kickoff event, this team's impact branches out WILDLY. Congratulations to the team that truly apes no one—Team 668, Apes of Wrath!

This colorful and consistent team shows amazing spirit, pride, and positivity that allows them to FACE the competition HEAD on. With iconic giveaways and enthusiastic energy they always show up in force to support their alliance. Please give a round of applause to the winner of the team spirit award, the team of bows and ties, team 1967!

This team had a structured approach to multi-tasking during the season. They scheduled slots to build multiple robots, allowing programming and mechanical to COOK side-by-side. Their end effector is SLICED perfectly to carry coral and algae simultaneously, and their dominant performance in this game shows that TOAST doesn't get Soggy under the sea...

This award winner has truly revolutionized kindness into their orbit. Ready to lend a wrench—or even an entire workspace—this team LOOPS others into their success. Their pit stop isn't just a place for robots; it's home to a wheel-y inspiring pledge to gracious professionalism, signed by every team member. They CURVE expectations by empowering rookies to prototype ideas, no matter how ELLIPTICAL they may seem. Always there to help teams swerve smoothly through technical twists and turns, they've made gracious professionalism their GRAVITATIONAL pull. Congratulations, Team 6814, Ellipse!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Robots use lots of axels for drive wheels, arm and elevator joints and climbers. Some axels are driven by motors while some just provide a pivot point. To reduce the weight of their grabber and lower the center of gravity they created a clever, three-element, coaxial unit where only two of the elements are driven.
A monster with many faces so rare, Built to last and easy to repair. But the team, with care, Gives a welcoming stare, Scylla’s charm is beyond compare!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: What sets this team apart is their DOGGED commitment to sound software practices, including unit testing, logging, and data-driven performance optimization. All of this seamlessly integrated with their clean robot build and strategic gameplay, proving that when it comes to innovation in control, this team is on FIRE!

They say genius teeters on the edge of MADNESS, and one team proved it with a robot that mastered the reef. With pinpoint localization and game piece detection, their robot executed coral transfers with the grace of a ballet dancer. Let's cheer for the unstoppable winners of the autonomous award, MadTown Robotics!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team made a SPLASH with their stunning visual identity! Their deep dive into the reefscape inspired their outreach, apparel, and pit display. Their original community-created mural SWIMS seamlessly with their signature color. You’ll SEA them coming in their vibrant shirts and unmistakable fish tails. With a look that’s both FIN-tastic and SHORE to impress, congratulations to this year’s Imagery Award winner: Armour Robotics!

This team met every criterion of the FIRST Impact Award. They made incredible contributions by steering the ship toward substantial growth of FIRST programs and raising the tide in their local area in a sustainable way. They also developed resources that are broadly used by the FIRST community around the globe. They paint STEM in a positive light and are anchoring FIRST in Europe.

The judges appreciated hearing how this team took disadvantage and turned it into advantage. Great initiatives, strong data and sharing their field while offering open workshops and a published book raised the odds. They rolled the dice with the Bot Swap Shop and hit the jackpot.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: When this small team of industrial designers leaped into action, Their expertise in CAD, software and advantage scope climbed higher than all the rest. These big cats won with consistent balance and team principles.
Publishing books is just one small step for this team. Their commitment to their community in all aspects is out of this world. Soaring to new heights into space.

New to FIRST and new to the floor, they hit the ground running, and opened the door. Traveling with their robot in tow did not impact this team's mojo, Their bot is creative, excitement is catching near and far.

Rising above the challenges, these warriors tried something new. Organizational structure made all the difference, with 2 strong presidents and 24 outreach events, this desert team will show us the way.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team's core values are sustainable, from local to global their impact is notable. With the focus on building the skills of their members, this community really minimalizes their carbon footprint. Their ohana stand out as they strive for the summit.
We heard you in the crowd ROAR, Lifting our spirits to SOAR, We see a sea of ORANGE ........ and BLUE and we knew it was you!

This team used an iterative process, along with a large team, testing multiple robots to get their best design. Their goal was to score quickly and consistently, which they accomplished throughout the matches. Their printing design and two drive trains gave them an edge in match play, and their robot did it all while wearing printed cat ears.

Helping teams is a core value of FIRST. From raising funds to sharing space, to building a field, these FIRSTers are showing us how to go to competition in print. You can find them in four across in the super pit in the corner.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team's unique design blew the judges away with an out of the BLOCK idea. Their versatile arm could throw a spear in any direction. And with their HEADS together, showed creativity in design.

The level of workmanship of this robot cannot be OVER-stated. Deliberate engineering design, precise manufacturing of parts and outstanding wire management achieve a level that is HEADS above the rest. Quality is not just an undercurrent for this team.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: They are the soldiers of unique solutions. They assimilated a whole different world and mapped it into their vision. They are warriors of true innovation in control.
From the moment the hunt begins, this team prowls and pounces on instinct alone ..... They'll be feasting on the Autonomous Award tonight.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Through this pit, take a dive into the ocean blue. Swimming with excitement, this team makes engineering an enjoyable adventure. Soaring over the ocean, their bright blue wings shimmering, this team creates a splash of imagery wherever they go.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This team’s impact journey has carried them to the upper stratosphere. Their longstanding efforts in championing FIRST values has been felt by FLL teams, underserved community schools, local summer camps, and the halls of the Commonwealth legislature. With a three-pronged approach focused on Advocate, Advance, and Advise, this team’s impact scales well beyond the norm.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This team's passion for growing FIRST programs is truly remarkable. They mentor and assist FLL, FTC, and FRC teams AND run 2 weeks of LEGO Robotics camp every summer. They focus on prioritizing underserved communities and spreading the love for STEM and FIRST through their incredible initiatives. Their mission to make STEM education accessible to all has led them to establish the STEM+C Competition Team Grant Program, which is now a PERMANENT part of the Code of Virginia. And that's not all – their creation of the FIRST Robotics Pathway has led to 73% of schools in their county having a FIRST team. That is truly a BRIE-lliant achievement!

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.script: You can really count on this team to inspire students to engineering. They have reached tens of thousands of elementary students using simple and effective Lego designs to demonstrate basic engineering concepts. Their intuitive engineering lessons will really STICK with you.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This team has put engineering inspiration into the claws of underserved schools. Their summer camp curriculum teaches block-diagram coding and has been translated into other languages to expand their reach. We’re happy to put this award into their talons.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: From the start, this team defined clear design constraints and goals, laying out a solid foundation for success. Through rigorous testing and iteration, they built a robot designed not just to play the game but to endure it. This machine is both practical and elegant as these TIGERS POUNCE onto the reef.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.script: We were magnetically drawn to this team’s system modeling. This team could accurately test code before having access to the robot, allowing them to simulate the code and conquer the competition. With modeling skills that were simply out of this world, the Judges Award for Simulation proves these knights are ready to launch.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: This rookie team put in a big effort to soar above the rest. They’ve learned to find joy in difficult challenges, pushing themselves to the limits of possibility & sharing their successes with other teams by building tactical partnerships. This high-performing rookie team is TOP GUN.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.script: Like their namesake, this team blasted back onto the scene this year. With new growth came a new mindset, prioritizing diversity, inclusivity in leadership, and new methods to achieve FIRST goals. This litter of kittens certainly pounced on the opportunity for a new future.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team demonstrated a strong team structure and sustainable growth through the reuse of parts and materials. They also have well-documented plans for passing down knowledge to the next generation of students. This team has the power to SWIM UP RIVER or SOAR ABOVE for years to come.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.script: From the moment this team enters the venue, their presence is unmistakable. Their exuberant array of color signifies unity and diversity within the FIRST community. Although this team is small, their heart is mighty, which is reflected in their team motto, “Do Better”.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This team’s design included just about everything: scoring on all levels, algae manipulation, and the elusive floor pick-up. Their robot SWARMED the field, and they articulated their manipulators with unBEElievable speed and grace. Most of all, these students shared their design and manufacturing process and left the judges BUZZING with excitement.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.script: When your team is having problems, this team’s SAILS are the ones you want to see on the horizon. They’ll pick up the pieces and help you code your autonomous routines. This SEA SERPENT is here to help, not to pillage!

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: In the heat of the battle, this team used creativity to adapt old designs to solve new challenges. Their multi-axial wrist allowed them to manipulate game pieces to provide creative advantages. Like the Statue of Liberty, their wrist held the Torch high!

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This team RIPS APART the competition when it comes to design simplicity. Their design ideals lead the path through a JUNGLE of challenges to have them end up KING. This team certainly AIN’T LION about their quality.

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: When it comes to control, you can SPOT this team zipping around the field with minimal human interaction. By creating their own virtual control board, their robot is able to autonomously generate paths to and from the reef while following preset priorities. When this team turns on their “SMART MODE” operations, you better MOOO-VE out of their way!

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This team's sensing capabilities truly stood out in this year’s ARENA of competition. In particular, their method of odometry estimation through Kalman Filtering truly made them a STAR. Their autonomous capabilities made them an OVERALL great team (just like their OVERALLS).

records.eventName: FIRST Chesapeake District Championship presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team is very comfortable in this splashy competition. With their strong color selection, this team is all about inclusion and having fun. These fish make waves with their strong brand and infectious kindness.

This team has a rich history of over ten years, committed to actively promoting the FRC culture. Their open-minded and inclusive approach, with senior members guiding newcomers, reflects the spirit of gracious professionalism. Through the OpenAlliance project in the open-source community, they have provided technical support to over 20 outstanding teams by offering CAD structures and manual/visual coding. For them, the robot is more than just code and metal, it is a bridge to the future, a driving force for technological innovation. Their creativity and influence extend beyond the competition field, serving as a role model to peers, schools, and the broader FRC community. May they continue to uphold the spirit of innovation and collaboration, spreading FRC culture and helping more young people embrace technology to realize their dreams! The FIRST Impact Award goes to Team 5449 from Beijing! 他们是一只拥有十多年成长历程，致力于积极推广FRC文化的战队。积极开放与包容的心态，以老带新的传承纽带体现出高尚的专业精神。通过开源社区OpenAlliance项目将搭建结构CAD和手动/视觉代码，为20多个优秀团队提供技术支持。机器人不仅是代码与金属，更是连接未来世界的桥梁，是推动科技创新的新动能。团队的创新才智和影响力超越了赛场边界，为激励同龄人、学校乃至FRC社区做出榜样。愿你们继续秉持创新与协作精神，致力于FRC文化的广泛传播，帮助更多年轻人热爱科技实现梦想！影响力奖颁发给来自北京的5449

This team from Shenzhen exemplifies their respect and admiration for engineering. Over the past two years, they have open-sourced their technology on GitHub, with over 300 international teams downloading their resources. Also, they’ve met with thousands of children in Manila, Philippines, showcasing the FIRST Robotics Competition, an initiative recognized by the Metropolitan Children’s Foundation and broadcasted on over 20 television stations. The Engineering Inspiration Award goes to Team 5516 from Shenzhen! 这是来自深圳的一支队伍，他们充分体现了对工程的尊重和欣赏。在过去两年里，他们在“Github”上开源了自己的技术，一共有300多支国际队伍下载。同时，他们与上千名菲律宾马尼拉的儿童见面，向他们展示了FIRST机器人比赛，这一活动获得了大都会儿童基金会的认可，并在20多家电视台播放，工程启发奖颁发给来自深圳的5516

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Hailing from a southern city renowned for its spirit of innovation, this team has prioritized control in their design approach. By adopting a modular architecture, incorporating advanced nylon-carbon fiber materials, and optimizing lightweight structural design, they have significantly enhanced their robot’s reliability. The Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors goes to Team 8214! 这是一只来自充满创新活力的南方城市的队伍，他们将控制放在设计首位，采用模块化设计，通过尼龙碳纤维新材料的创新使用以及轻量化的结构设计，有效提升了机器人的可靠性。“通用汽车”赞助的工业设计奖颁发给8214

This team from Zhenjiang Vocational and Technical College has gone above and beyond in promoting the spirit of FRC. Over the past few years, they have organized more than 50 events, opened over 20 vocational experience centers in their local community, and established partnerships with 20 local businesses, reflecting the concept of integrating industry and education. Moreover, they hold over 100 patents, showing their passion, professionalism, and influence within FRC. The Judge’s Award goes to Team 6304 from Zhenjiang! 这是一支来自中国镇江职业技术学校的队伍，在过去几年中，他们为宣传FRC精神，做了超过50场活动，在当地社区开放了20多次职业体验中心。同时，这支队伍与当地20家企业建立了合作，充分体现了产教融合的理念。此外，这支队伍还有100多项专利，充分体现了他们对FRC的热情、专业和影响力。评委奖颁发给来自镇江的6304

This is an incredibly young team that has built an outstanding team structure in just six months. Their robot boasts perfect L4 projection capabilities, helping them achieve the goals of FIRST. The Rookie All Star Award goes to Team 10479 from Shanghai! 这是一支非常年轻的队伍，在短短半年时间里，建立了出色的团队架构，他们的机器人拥有完美的L4投射能力，帮助他们完成了FIRST的目标。新秀全明星奖颁发给来自上海的10479

This is a team that has embarked on a journey of resurgence. Due to various circumstances, they were unable to participate in FRC for the past few years. Yet, with unwavering determination, they successfully convinced their teachers and principal, secured school support, and even raised their own funds. Despite limited access to machining equipment, they crafted robot components by hand using the simplest tools and completed their robot’s design and manufacturing. Now, they have returned to the FRC stage. While their robot may not be flawless, their confidence and ambition shine brightly. The Rising All Star Award goes to Team 8810 from Suzhou! 这是一支重新启航的队伍。过去的几年，他们因种种原因未能参加FRC比赛，但今年，他们凭借坚定的信念和不懈的努力，成功说服了老师和校长，获得了学校的支持，并自筹经费。尽管加工设备简陋，条件有限，但他们用最简单的工具，亲手加工零件，完成了机器的设计与制造，终于重返FRC赛场。虽然他们的机器并非完美无缺，但他们满怀信心，决心再创辉煌。崛起之星奖颁发给来自苏州的8810

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Hailing from the entrepreneurial hub of Shenzhen, this team adheres to the principles of creativity, inclusivity, and environmental sustainability. They continue to grow and evolve, with over 700 students from their school and community signing up to join the team, providing a steady stream of talent to support their 40-member core team. The Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow goes to Team 6414 from Shenzhen! 这是来自充满机遇的创业热土——深圳的队伍。这支队伍秉持创意、包容、环保的理念，持续进步，并且在学校和社区拥有700多名学生报名参加队伍，为40多人的常规队伍提供了源源不断的人才供应。“陶氏化学”赞助的团队可持续发展奖颁发给来自深圳的6414

This team exemplifies the true spirit of teamwork. Despite facing challenges such as limited resources and a lack of technical mentorship, they assembled a 32-member team and made their way to the competition. Their members are self-taught, and they actively promote the FIRST spirit through social media. May this invaluable perseverance help them grow even stronger! The Team Spirit Award goes to Team 7002 from Taiyuan! 这是一支让我们深深感受到团队精神的队伍，在缺乏资源与导师技术支持的情形下，仍然组建起一支32人的队伍参赛，并且组员到现场参赛。团队成员自学技术，同时在自媒体踊跃宣传FIRST精神，希望这种可贵的精神可以让你们快速成长起来，团队精神奖颁发给来自太原的7002

This team from "China’s Silicon Valley" has embraced the "keep it simple, stupid" philosophy in their design. They innovatively created a flexible rotating launcher head, coupled with a “herringbone” track structure, to achieve more precise and long-range projection. The Excellence in Engineering Award goes to Team 6766 from Shenzhen! 这支队伍来自“中国的硅谷”，他们用“keep it simple, stupid”的概念，创新地设计了灵活的旋转发射头部，结合“人字形”的轨道结构，实现了更精准和远距离投射。卓越工程奖颁发给来自深圳的6766

Hailing from Shanghai, this team has demonstrated remarkable dedication. Their "Starlight SAGA" program not only supports the growth of new team members but also extends guidance and companionship to students from remote areas, even to those battling leukemia, through online mentoring. The Gracious Professionalism Award goes to Team 6907 from Shanghai! 这位是来自魔都上海的一支队伍，这支队伍的星光SAGA课程，不仅给团队新成员的成长提供助力，也在线上为来自边远地区的学生，甚至白血病学生进行了指导和陪伴。最佳风尚奖颁发给来自上海的6907

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Hailing from the dynamic and vibrant city of Eastern China, this team has demonstrated remarkable ingenuity. Their intake system utilizes tape for positioning constraints, while dual TOF sensors and ultrasonic measurements ensure precise placement. Inspired by computer networking equipment, their lifting and securing mechanism creatively bridges the gap between technological application and engineering practice. The Creative Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation goes to Team 6487! 这支队伍来自中国东方、具有独特的都市风情和无限活力的城市。他们的intake采用胶带进行限位，通过双侧TOF传感器和超声波进行位置测量，起吊固定装置的设计灵感来自计算机网络设备，创新地解决了技术运用与工程实践的需求结合。由Rockwell Automation赞助的最佳创意奖颁发给6487

This team from Shenzhen has set a high standard for reliability, safety, and aesthetics in their robot’s wiring. Their coral collection mechanism features a curved entrance design, ensuring smooth and stable collection. Throughout the competition, their robot maintained excellent performance without any major malfunctions. The Quality Award goes to Golem 6706! 这是一支来自深圳的队伍，他们的机器人接线可靠，安全且美观。珊瑚收集装置的入口采用曲面设计，有效保障珊瑚的稳定收集。机器人整体运行稳定，没有发生重大故障。最佳质量奖颁发给Golem 6706

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team comes from a renowned bilingual school in Shanghai. Their robot features an innovative deployment mechanism with a two-way structure, which centralizes the wheels, enhancing stability. Throughout the competition, their machine’s flexible design allowed them to maintain consistent performance. They focused on creating a pipeline of talent starting with FLL. They demonstrate laser-like focus on all the right things. They walk in Woodies shoes, literally every day.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team described their elegant and practical robot design with ease, highlighting form, fit and function. Beginning with their robust elevator to their cam system protecting their snow blower motor, their functionality is unmatched. Shifting into “high-gear”, this team is “red-hot”.

Their Engineering focus and inclusion impact doesn’t stop there. Whether presenting at the FIRST Championship or meeting with lawmakers, they’re proving that engineering inspiration can travel far and wide. Congratulations Team 2486 - Coconuts

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Emerging from the heart of nature's wild beauty, this team has navigated through challenges with remarkable precision and artistic prowess. You might say they have a unique affinity for thriving in environments that others might find daunting. Indeed, their journey reflects a blend of creativity, ingenuity, and a bit of that daring spirit that one only finds in the most unexpected places. Your creativity and hard work have inspired us all. Congratulations Team 179 - Children of the Swamp

This team faced a season full of plot twists with many organizational challenges. But instead of giving up, they regrouped, rebuilt, and kept moving forward — with the support of determined students and rockstar parents. They found a new home, demonstrating strong and joyful team collaboration, and showed up ready to compete — proving that grit, heart, and teamwork can overcome just about anything. You have truly inspired us! We would like to give the Resiliance Award to Team 10017 - GPS Robotics

When it comes to creativity, this team served up something truly delicious. With a piping-hot theme and plenty of cheesy charm, this team brought the ingredients and flair to power their community. Please join me in congratulating the team that delivered a slice of brilliance—Team 10154, PizzaByte 2.0!

They forged success through teamwork, family, drive, and impressive fundraising power. Nine schools united, forging a bold, diverse team of engineers. With strong support and spirit—congrats Team Forge 9404!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team dove deep into sustainability, making waves in their community through apprenticeships and impactful outreach. By partnering with a coral restoration company for environmental stewardship, they helped rebuild the very reefs that inspired this year’s Reefscape theme. Congratulations to Team 1744—Robo-Rays Robotics!
This team’s got more pep than a double espresso shot. From bleachers to Slack, their spirit lights up in every connection. Let’s hear it loud for the unstoppable Team 6722 LED Robotics!
They roam the jungle searching for a problem to solve Engineering Excellence is not Greek to them They may not be the "Alpha" but they are the SigmaCats Congratulations Team 108 - Sigma Cats
Cleanliness may not be their greatest virtue But gracious professionalism is their hallmark The mechanics on call for all your robot needs Congratulations Team 3932 - Dirty Mechanics

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Creativity is the essence of innovation, and this team scaled the steep cliffs of competition and grabbed each challenge by the horns. Their robot was a unique masterpiece, showing off clever engineering and standout imagination – able to multi-task with great agility. Let’s hear it for the team that truly charged ahead with creativity— Team 59, Ram Tech!

By understanding their limitations, these mammals made a plan that set them up for success. Through simplification and iteration, they created a robust machine that paddles its way to reliability and continuous improvement. They really come OTTER the sea. Congratulations Team 8841 - OTTER

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team took control innovation to the next level—merging reality with the virtual to enhance precision and performance. By integrating a META VR headset into their system, they gave drivers a whole new way to command the field. Even better, they open-sourced their work so others could follow in their footsteps. Congratulations to Team 2383 —the Ninjineers!

This team’s autonomous routine was anything but fishy. It was precise, reliable, and scored a consistent four points time and time again. Hailing from a coastal town, their robot moved with the grace of a sea creature navigating its reef. Their clever control systems made this “anemone” a force to be reckoned with. Congratulations to Team 180 —S.P.A.M.!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Instead of flying, they dove down deep on this year’s theme. By involving other school programs, they put the A in STEAM. This team hammered home the appearance throughout. Congratulations, Team 5410!

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.script: If you know cryptogram, this team’s name adds up to 67. They have demonstrated extraordinary ability to connect with their community with STEM days, summer camps, and Stem nights. They even droned the vision of FIRST by spending countless hours mentoring and sponsoring FLL, FTC and even inspired a couple of FRC teams. Their innovativeness is unparalleled and on show in their community. Back to the cryptogram, 2 is A, 3 is B, and 4 is C! Get it? . It did not take a C64 to break this code. This team wrote the code for FIRST’s success! Congratulations Team 6919, The Commodores.

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.script: This team has worked both inside and outside their home track to expand the reach and impact of STEM. They have committed to running toward every Opportunity and UPlifting others, while showcasing innovation. A high-energy current of inspiration runs through their circuits. Congratulations, Team 1002—the Circuit Runners Robotics!

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: When the challenge was revealed, this team got to work right away. Masters of agile development, they rapidly built, tested, and refined their designs—ready to awe the world. Their approach to industrial design stood above the rest. Congratulations, Team 3329—the Wildbots!

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.script: When the need arose to promote STEM in a community obsessed with “THE SPORTS,” this team stepped up. They gained local support, showed off their robot, and even became a rising social media star. They recycled their scrap and donated materials to programs for students with special needs. Congratulations, Team 7470 the iRamBots!

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.script: When this team decided to make a comeback after their robotics program was sidelined, they were not horsing around. Just two years into their rebuild, their energy has been hard to corral—they have been stampeding forward ever since. In the true spirit of this award, this team shows a sustainable and promising future with FIRST. But let us not stall any longer— Give it up for Team 5074—the Meadowcreek Mustangs!

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has made a positive impact on both their community and the environment. Their ocean “shiver” has grown tremendously over the past year. They are not afraid to take a shark bite out of sustainability! Congratulations, Team 6905—Raiders of the ARC-TEAR-A-BYTE!

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.script: Whose cheers echoed loud and clear? This team drove over three hours to bring their spirit here. Their energy is fierce, their pride even more— Listen closely… and you will hear them roar! Congratulations, Team 4459—the LeoTechs!

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.script: Engineering is not just about solving problems—it is about designing creative solutions that spark new ideas. This team brought their innovative concepts to life with an intake system that excelled on the field. With determination, creativity, and a few well-placed precision sensors, they are proving that anything is possible. Congratulations, Team 2415—the WiredCats!

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.script: This team knows how to hit hard—with KINDNESS Whether it is helping others drive, build, or code. They bring the energy of the game and the heart of the Eagles. Their sportsmanship is unmatched, and their professionalism? Pure gold. Please give it up for the team behind Saquan Botley... Team 6023—the DISCBOTS!

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team was “Chief” among others, impressing everyone with a solution that was as imaginative as it was effective—showing clear thought and intentional planning. Whether they are competing here at FIRST or 3D-printing prosthetic devices for those in need, they do not just think outside the box—they rebuild the box to match their strategy. With elegant design and purposeful innovation, they transformed a creative idea into a competitive advantage. Please join me in congratulating the winner of the Creativity in Strategy Award... Team 8080, Sequoyah Robotics!

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.script: Where precision meets resilience, one team stands apart— Their commitment to quality is nothing short of an art. With every weld, wire, and rivet in place, their design is built to endure and sets the pace. Through the heat of battle, their machine holds tight— engineered for excellence, forged for the fight. Ladies and gentlemen, give it up for Team 6925—Woodward Academy Robotics!

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: When the reef called for help, this team answered. They built a system that could search, recognize, and scoop coral—working to save the reef. Their control system was the most innovative we saw. Congratulations, Team 1261—the Robo Lions!

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.script: This award goes to a team whose robot is so independent that it might be just one software update away from applying for a job. While others were busy controlling their bots, this one was making its own decisions—probably even questioning ours. With precision, reliability, and just the right amount of rebellious spirit to take over the world, this team has truly mastered autonomy. Congratulations, Team 1771—North Gwinnett Robotics!

records.eventName: PCH District Albany Event presented by Procter & Gamble
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team demonstrates a cohesive and well-executed brand—from their robot to their pit. Their primary team color reflects the passion, creativity, and kindness they bring to the competition. DJ 24 would be extremely proud of this impressive group of young women. Congratulations, Team 7514—EVE Robotics!

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.script: This team came swashbuckling into the 2025 season wanting to make a huge impact, and they did just that! By sharing and caring they emulated the values of FIRST not only in their community but with others throughout the state of Georgia. Poised with professionalism and forward thinking this team plotted a new course even though it was mid-season. They saw a need and sailed ahead, mapped the solution, engaged leadership and went to work immediately. They embody everything that FIRST stands for and will represent Georgia well at Worlds! Congratulations Team 2974, Walton robotics.

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.script: This team exemplifies the values of FIRST in every way, charging beyond the call of action – not only do they mentor local FLL and FTC teams, but also have given light to a dozen global teams, and have hosted many local STEM events, reminding us that the arts are still very relevant in a growing technological world. This team also guaranteed funding for thousands of students by securing state grants that help recharge access towards STEM education. Energizing the pits with a radiant presence, this team has shown us what it means to turn potential into kinetic. Congratulations to team 1002, Circuit Runners Robotics.

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.script: Some teams build robots. This team builds something even more powerful — a movement. They’ve carved a path with inclusive summer camps, adapted STEM fairs, and a reading program where kids learn literacy alongside robots — and they’re not climbing alone. With no cost to join, a multilingual team, and outreach designed to lift voices often left unheard, their impact flows from base to summit and ripples well beyond the reef. Congratulations to Team 7538, Metal Mountain.

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This year's Industrial Design Award recognizes a team whose machine exemplifies the perfect balance of form, function, and aesthetics. Their sleek, purposeful design is not only visually striking but also a testament to their dedication to efficiency and practicality. From the use of 3D parts in their unique vibrant colors to the overall function of the robot, every element has been crafted with precision and intention. With a logo that proudly represents their identity and creative touches sprouted throughout their build, this team has truly engineered excellence. Congratulations team 1833, Team BEAN!

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.script: From deep in the southern coast, this team has built a program grounded in persistence, technical grit, and a spirit as untamed as their name suggests. Whether facing geographic distance or limited access, they continue to rise, proving that even in isolation, excellence echoes loud and clear. Congratulations to Team 3329, the Wildbots, winners of this year’s Judges’ Award: The Untamed Spirit Award

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: This award celebrates the rookie team exemplifying a young but strong partnership effort, as well as implementing the mission of FIRST to inspire students to learn more about science and technology. From the start, this team created quite a buzz with their energy, enthusiasm, and collaboration. Their hive-minded teamwork and sweet dedication to STEM has kids in elementary and middle school buzzing with excitement, as they mentor and coach the next generation of First participants. It's clear that this rookie squad is gliding to success while building a foundation that will keep the team skating for seasons to come! Congratulations to team 10482, the Buzz Bots!

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.script: The Rising All-Star Award is a new award that FIRST introduced this year. This award celebrates the spark of something special—the team that rises despite the odds, showing promise, persistence, and the drive to grow even while being young and facing the struggles that can come with that. This student-led crew turned scarcity into strategy, proving resourcefulness was their lightening in a bottle, even in the wake of not having STEM coaches. Despite this, this team has shown that accountability, a garage and a willingness to shift with the tides are the keys towards becoming our next star. You might say their impact on their community has been electric, and their energy? Like raging thunder. Please give it up for none other than… Team 8849, Storm Robotics!

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: When hearing that FIRST is "More Than Robots" this year's Sustainability Award Winner took that to heart. Soaring with purpose, this team embodies that mantra by building not only robots, but by building a strong flock around their team. From mentoring their future eaglets in both FLL and VEX, to a unique open-door high school recruitment strategy in both Summer and Fall months, this team is working around the clock to give members a change to take flight and empower STEAM in the community. They have proven that their flight plan is a success, in the last 4 years this team has over tripled the women on their team and plan to keep on growing. Raising FIRST up on the wings of an eagle, give it up for the EAGLEBOTS TEAM 4112!!

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.script: This award celebrates extraordinary enthusiasm and spirit through exceptional partnership and teamwork furthering the objectives of FIRST. The enthusiasm this newbie team has shown for robotics has been as sweet as honey. Their presence at First competitions bears noting everywhere, from their pit to their robot. They proudly represent their school’s brand and image.They care deeply about mentoring younger students in the schools around them, inspiring the next generations of robotics teams. Congratulations to team 9480, The Flowery Branch Gear Bears

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.script: Some teams talk about innovation… this one put it right in their name. By lightening their grip and doubling their payload, they proved that smart engineering is more than just shell-deep. And with a design binder thick enough to anchor a ship, their commitment to documentation set the gold standard. Join me in congratulating Team 8866, Innovation Robotics.

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.script: The Gracious Professionalism Award demonstrates a team’s sportsmanship, working together on and off the field of play. This team is fierce when in battle, but embrace everyone as their own flesh and blood. The impact they have has helped not only the local community, but also ones on the other side of the world. Guiding young new members to embrace their warrior ethos. Congratulations to Team 5109- The Gladiators

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: While most bots scoop, grab, or claw, this one spiraled into action. With an intake powered by a clever twist on ancient screw mechanics, custom 3D-printed belts, and a climb that balances like a gymnast on a beam, this team engineered a truly unique trifecta. Add in a sensor suite to navigate the reef with ease, and you’ve got a design that didn’t just think outside the box — it redesigned the whole thing. Congratulations to Team 1648, G3 Robotics.

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.script: From the depths of the ocean to the resilience of a thriving reef, this team’s robot is built to endure, adapt, and dominate. With unmatched craftsmanship, rock-solid construction, and a design as strong as the tides, their robot weathers every challenge with ease. Congratulations Team 1683, the Techno Titans.

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: With multiple subsystems working in harmony and vision processing sharp enough to spot coral in a crowded reef, this team’s robot moved with purpose and instinct. Their thoughtful integration of controls and protection of key electronics showed experience, and the kind of discipline you’d expect from a well-led pride. Whether navigating the reef or stalking the next scoring chance, this team showed they were in command — kings both on land and sea. Congratulations to Team 1261, the Robo Lions.

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.script: From sensing surroundings to precise positioning, this team's robot moves autonomously with consistent and purposeful control. In both the autonomous and human game play, this robot determines its position, calculates the best scoring solution and then generates a path to score the coral.. Just look around—you'll see this ROBOTICS team steering NORTH toward excellence! Congratulations Team 1771, North Gwinnett Robotics

records.eventName: Peachtree District Championship presented by Mercer University
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team gathered together to swim to the top. Their Journey through the ocean is a prime example of their sustainable pipeline initiative. With their distinct blue color and Hawaiian shirts it's no wonder that this jubilee is for the Manatees. Congratulations team 6340, the Marist Manatees!

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.script: Using their past to grow a better future, this team has their map in hand to chart their new course to inspire others and build FIRST in their region. With a treasure box full of resources from videos, summer camps, mentoring sessions and their scouting app, these students are charting their way to success to inspire others. If you are on a quest to inspire and spread the message of FIRST the forensics is clear – X marks the spot at 1590 Bill Murdock Road. Ahoy Mateys – Congratulations Team 2974 Walton Robotics. Arrrrrr

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.script: They’ve not only excelled in the ocean competition but have also inspired a deep appreciation for engineering in their school and beyond with their FISHING efforts. Please join me in celebrating this year’s Engineering Inspiration Award winners: Team 6919, The Commodores

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: With a robot that combines elegance and efficiency, this team is blazing a trail with its stylish good looks. Their sleek black and orange design sparks everyone’s interest…. Congratulations Team 6829, Ignite Robotics

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.script: Not only did they build a robot that could barely be contained, they’ve also helped other schools get their own bots off the ground. Clearly, these wild creators are spreading chaos and robotics everywhere. The Judges Award goes to the Wildbots!

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.script: Beginning without experience this team learned to solve problems not only with building a robot but also with students coming together to form a team. Parts had to be inventoried and then re-inventoried in figuring out how their wheels, motors, and computer would come together to form a robot, but also how different student interests in art, design, computers and mechanics would come together to form a team. The Rookie All-Star Award goes to: Team 10376, The Plutonium Panthers

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.script: Against all odds, this team has overcome great adversity to stay in the competition. They clawed their way back despite losing all but 2 members and their mentor. These cats still have all nine lives, congratulations to the hometown winner – Catabots!

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Through their ongoing efforts, this team has shown unwavering dedication to preserving the health of our oceans and shores. These future engineers from all over the seven seas that call their home port Georgia, are not only designing cutting-edge robots, but they are also actively dedicated to ensuring a positive environmental impact in their community through their ongoing efforts, including their participation in the Tybee Island Beach Cleanup, they are resolute in preserving the health of our oceans and shores. We give a 21-Pistol Shrimp salute to the Sustainability Award winners: Team 4701, Warriors “Team W.I.R.E”

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.script: This award goes to a team that stands out from the pack for their energy and look. Decked out in yellow and black everyone can hear them roar. Bringing the heart of a lion to every match is the winner for Team Spirit. Congratulations Team 4459 LeoTechs

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.script: Meticulous attention to detail and creative problem solving are always an important part of FIRST Robotics. Designing a robot that is easy to improve and update goes above and beyond the normal engineering process. This team has modular all figured out, which is engineering excellence at its core, giving them a great edge on the field. Congratulations Team 4112, EagleBots

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.teamName: Career Blazer Robotics - The Fighting Mongooses
records.script: The Gracious Professionalism Award recognizes the team who showed an immense dedication to supporting others, lifting them up, and fostering an environment where all can succeed and grow. This team was always willing to share their knowledge, resources, and their time offering guidance, troubleshooting assistance and encouragement. They understand robotics isn’t just about the robot, it’s about building relationships and creating a culture of mutual respect and support, exemplified by their assistance to other teams, key role in starting three other independent robotics teams and encouraging those in their community that want to learn more about robotics. Congratulations Team 5900, The Fighting Mongooses

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team had a creative “twist” when designing their robot. Their strategy had them sweeping the floor in this competition. They were not “screwing” around with their intake mechanism. Congratulations Team 1648, G3 Robotics

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.script: Whenever this robot is on the field, you can be sure their high-quality design is helping them “spin towards success”. We are proud to give the Quality Award to this team who is showing all of FIRST what DISC can do. Congratulations Team 6023, DISCBOTS

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team has officially taken control of the competition. Who knew that a robot with a little “wrist action” could make such a big impact? The Innovation in Control Award goes to: Team 4026, Decatur Robotics

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.script: Through advanced automation, including vision that would make Medusa jealous, their system seamlessly guides the robot to success. Like the legendary nymph Calypso, who skillfully flies through the sea; this team’s robot charts its own course. For their mastery of automation and strategic execution, we are proud to present the Automous Award to: Team 3635, The Flying Legion!

records.eventName: PCH District Dalton Event presented by Shaw Industries
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
