records.script: We want to recognize an incredible team for their outstanding efforts in creating a truly memorable and inspiring purple presence. This team can be found engineering vigorously every day. The Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen goes to: Team 7514 Eve Robotics

This team made it their goal to expand outreach and introduce STEM to more students in their community. The results for the last three years speak for themselves with almost all of their county schools now having a FTC or FLL team. They have also reached over 50 low income families and have partnered with the junior ROTC program. In addition they have assisted teams a partial orbit around the globe. They have clearly strengthened their REEF! But don’t be Green with Envy, and don’t be Blue…with a clear goal and team dedication, every team both domestic and global can have the same impact as our winner, Blast off with Team 4188 Columbus Space Program.

This team has climbed to new heights with their commitment to science and technology education. Their dedication to coaching FTC and FLL teams, along with hosting FLL events, has fortified curiosity and growth within their community. Through their STEM events for special needs students and their "Reading with Robots" events, they have made STEM education accessible to all. This teams' efforts, as strong as iron, exemplify the principles of FIRST's mission. Congratulations Team 7538, Metal Mountain.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team detailed a meticulous design process as they crafted this year's bot. Due to growing their team four-fold, a sub-team was created to ensure training was provided to new members as they learned skills for fabrication. The result was an elegant and linear bot to help deliver the heard to the competition. Congratulations Team 9477, Lambda.

These Siblings of STEM demonstrated exceptional teamwork to overcome fundraising obstacles outside of their control. Leveraging their unique talents, discipline, and drive, they marched their way to a solution. For designing and building a go-cart for a community raffle, the Judges would like to present “The Drive for a Cause “ award to Team 7104, Benedictine Military School – Bot Brothers.

This year's Rising All Star award goes to a team that has hit some roadblocks while trying to build outreach programs in their community Despite working with a tight budget, their drive and spirit have shone through. They have built plans for sustaining their team to ensure a bright future with FIRST just like their neon hats! Please join me in congratulating Team 9260, Built4Bibb!.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This metro Atlanta team sets the bar when it comes to sustainability. Their outreach efforts result in new recruits and their loyal sponsors help this team charge into battle against any competition. If you like to play Plinko, be sure to check out their HULK of a can bot! Congratulations to Team 7451, AvengerRobotics.

Outstanding team that can always be heard in the stands. Students yelling and screaming to support their team. Creating a contagious energy in the stands. Awesome environment for all. Robotics is the key. We just told you the acronym for their name!…OSCAR, congratulations Team 832, Oscar.

Great engineering doesn't just happen - it takes brainpower, blueprinting and a whole lot of innovation. This team didn't just build a robot; they engineered a masterpiece with rock solid prototype testing and documentation so detailed, even HAS would be jealous! This team proved that when you innovate with intention, document like detectives, and test with precision of a submarine navigating unchartered waters, the result is engineering excellence. Give it up for Team 8866, Innovation Robotics.

This metro Atlanta team has exemplified Gracious Professionalism throughput their FRC journey, embodying respect and collaboration in every aspect of competition. Helping others learn and overcome challenges is part of their voyage. Through teamwork and integrity, they navigated the seas to make a lasting impact both on and off the field. Congratulations Team 6340 Marist Manatees.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Like a well-oiled machine shifting gears at just the right moment, this team has engineered a mechanism that brings precision and control to every move. Their innovative “stick-shift” system seamlessly moves through present levels with control and smooth execution. With bold design and inventive thinking, they have shifted creativity into high gear! Congratulations Team 8736, the Mechanisms

This team from the north is dedicated to precision and attention to detail. Pride in craftmanship and design is reflected in their bot, pit and team. They'll be dancing the night away to electronic music as they come down from the stands to receive this award. Congratulations Team 1683, Techno Titans.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: When it comes to control, some teams push buttons - but this team pushes boundaries! This award celebrates teams that take electrical, mechanical, or software control to the next level, unlocking new possibilities for their machines. This team didn't just navigate the field - they sailed smoothly around the reef with precision, proving their control system was built for the high seas for competition! And let's talk about those LEDs - not just for style (though they are fine) but also delivering real time status updates like a robotics lighthouse guiding the way. Congratulations to Team 9496, LYNK.

This team doesn't just "stick" around - they've built a robot that moves with purpose and precision. Forged in fire, it commands the field with autonomous moves that are sharp and swift. Like a dragon navigating the battlefield with calculated intent, they strike with perfect execution. Congratulations Team 3318, RoboDragons.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This year’s Imagery Award recognizes a team whose machine and theme are seamlessly intertwined. Their exceptional visuals and original theme are not only a sight to behold but also a testament to their dedication to the principles of FIRST core values. For their distinctive logo sprouting up all over the venue to their creative touches that have been woven into every aspect, this team has truly grown to stand out. Congratulations Team 1833, Team Bean.

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.script: This team hasn't overlooked anyone on their climb to the top. Their targeted approach to outreach has allowed them to identify and address the gaps in STEM access they saw in their own backyard. When they're not reading with robots, supporting students in foster care, or dancing the night away at a sensory-friendly prom, this team is resurrecting FLL in their community and bringing a bit of calm to FRC events. Proving that you don't need to travel far to move mountains, Team 7538 builds belonging into everything they do. Congratulations Metal Mountain - Gwinnett Qualifier Impact Award winners!

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.script: Rising up through the Engineering tide, this team leads giantly, with inspiring energy. Gliding through the reefs mythically, diving into the community to build a bridge into the world of STEM. Their dedication to engineering, science, community, team building, and ongoing off-season involvement highlights their commitment to Science and Technology education. Congratulations to Team 1683, the Techno Titans, winners of the Engineering Inspiration award!

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Like any great super group, this team balanced multiple design elements to achieve a heroic result. And with a Mascot named Landshark, could this team have aligned any better to the competitions theme? These Avenging heroes brought the whole package from form to function to aesthetics. Of course we are talking about Team 7451, Congratulations Alliance Academy for Innovation, Avenger Robotics!

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.script: The Deep Dive Judges Award – Given to a team that demonstrated excellence at every level, from the surface to the ocean floor of competition. This crew made waves across the board! Whether navigating the deep waters of engineering, innovation, or community outreach, they showed that when they hit the water, they don’t short out, they shine. Their well-rounded excellence kept them afloat at the highest level of competition. Congratulations to Team 2415, the WiredCats, winners of the Judges Award.

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.script: This rookie team entered the competition with a working bot and a can-do attitude. Spreading STEM through creative fundraising and artwork, this Baker’s dozen is laying a strong foundation for the future. Led by a mentor who inspires like Kirby Smart, please help us congratulate the winner of the Rookie All Star Award, Team 10482, Buzz Robotics.

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.script: Funding is a “wild” challenge for many teams including this one. Facing limited financial support, they “clawed” together a plan, creating sub-teams to manage budgets and promote their team to sponsors. Addressing their challenges, they are ensuring future seasons will feel as easy as a “tropical” breeze. Congratulations Team 9086, Wildcat Robotics.

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Like a noir apparatus, synchronizing consistent sustainable movement, this team has merged the world of STEM and sustainability with ribbiting success. They are leading with a mechanical unyielding in innovative mentorship and environmental dedication. Congratulations to Team 8736, The Mechanisms.

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.script: This team showcases spirit on the field, across the FIRST community, & within their school. They have surfed technical oceans to share best practices with other FIRST teams to build talent and excitement for STEM. Have you Reddit? Through their love of FIRST & fun energy on all things STEM, this team increased their team from 15 members to 40 in a few short years. They are not Squidding or Sea Horsing around! Please congratulate Team 8865, Dacula Droids on the Team Spirit Award!

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.script: This year’s Excellence in Engineering Award goes to a team that has wrangled their design process with the precision of a rodeo cowboy. By using a Design Matrix to evaluate their game strategy and each component of their robot, this lassoed key factors like efficiency, durability, and functionality, ensuring that every choice was made with skill and care. Their methodical approach was an example of an excellent engineering approach. Congratulations Team 4509, the Mechanical Bulls.

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.script: Living FIRST’s core values is a driving force for this team. By working with underserved populations, both domestically and internationally, this team builds relationships within and outside of the FIRST community. Their fighting spirit shines a light in their community with their bot Nathan leading the charge. Congratulations Team 5109 Gladiator Robotics.

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team didn’t just think outside the box-they built one and climbed right in! with a unique “cage” climbing mechanism, they cracked the code on controlled, reliable ascension, proving that creative engineering can be both effective and eye-catching. Their innovative approach turned heads and lifted their performance to new heights. Congratulations to Team 1833, Team Bean

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.script: This team engineered a machine with the strength to thrive in the wild. With a ground intake that pounces on coral and a lightning-fast elevator, their machine swims through the reef like a hunter. Their sensor reinforcements let them sail even the roughest seas. Congratulations to Team 1261, the RoboLions, winners of the Quality Award.

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team didn’t just see the field-they saw the future of innovation. With a sophisticated multi-camera system, their robot maintained precise field awareness throughput the entire match, ensuring every move was calculated and controlled. Paired with a custom input device that tracked scored pieces, their machine seamlessly optimized its path, autonomously swimming between the human player and the reef with efficiency that left the competition in their wake. Congratulations to Team 1771, North Gwinnett robotics.

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.script: Moving strategically, this team has built a robot that tackles a challenge with precision and control. With an autonomous system that executes multi-level scoring, their machine moves with confidence before the first driver takes command. Pedal to the metal, these Crusaders have put scoring into high gear! Congratulations to Team 5293, the Metal Crusaders!!

records.eventName: PCH District Gwinnett Event presented by Gwinnett County Public Schools
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: We saw many impressive robots, but one team truly charged our imaginations with their exceptional visual design. They masterfully crafted a robot that wasn’t just functional, but a compelling visual story. This team, hailing from a town that shares its name with a famous architect of vision, really showed us what it means to build with purpose and artistry. For their ability to translate ideas into a striking, memorable presentation, the judges are proud to present the Imagery Award to Team 4189, the Chargers.

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Medtronic
records.script: This team has done an outstanding job in advancing respect and appreciation for engineering in their community. So many projects have been done to help so many from the learning impaired to the elderly. Gears only work when together— and this team has gotten it together. Congratulations, Team number 6429

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Medtronic
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team proves that mythical creatures exist and can come in black. Their robot uses a clever combination of materials to make an elegant machine. There is no mysticism about this team and robot; they are ready for the world. Congratulations, Team number 8214

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Medtronic
records.script: Every so often, a team comes along that truly embodies the heart of FIRST — not just through what they build, but how they bring people together. This season, one team stood out for going the distance — figuratively and literally — to unite individuals under a shared vision of teamwork, perseverance, and innovation… all while piloting a robot with a name that’s just as unforgettable as their journey Spongebot Square Drive. Congratulations, Team number 9692

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Medtronic
records.script: This remarkable community team has not only built an impressive robot capable of navigating the grid, but they've also deeply engaged their local community, inspiring future STEM leaders. The judges can not be more excited to see their future. The Rookie All-Star Award is presented to: 10011

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Medtronic
records.script: This team’s innovative robot, and community events, as well as partnership to translate documentation has demonstrated exceptional drive. This team has soared to new heights this season! Congratulations, Team number 9008

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Medtronic
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: The judges found this team’s sustainability practices empowering. Their visibility has risen from their environmentally focused work across developing STEM education in their school and community. Let us hear the Yeti roar! Congratulations, Team number 3506

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Medtronic
records.script: This team has reached the summit of team spirit. Across the Appalachians, they reach out to help other teams, and yet remain grounded in within their community. This team is well known to have reached the peak with their spirit. Congratulations, Team number 2614

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Medtronic
records.script: Forged in the fires of competition, this team builds like warriors and thinks like engineers. Powered by custom circuit boards and controllers, their robot has the match dancing to their tune and their wiring is locked in. Shielded by discipline and driven by design, Engineering excellence isn’t just their goal – it’s their standard. Congratulations, Team number 971

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Medtronic
records.script: This team demonstrates the full spectrum of FIRST core values. From sharing their robot to their in-person assistance this teams embodies gracious professionalism. Watching the shift in their colors is a boost to all around them. Congratulations, Team number 4039

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Medtronic
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Some teams build arms. Others build intakes. This team combined both. With a lightning-fast intake and multi-purpose arm, they skipped the perfect alignment dance and shaved seconds with smart design. With dual degree of freedom and travel-ready design, they turned constraints into innovation. From half-way around the world, their creative force elevates the game. Congratulations, Team number 7539

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Medtronic
records.script: Just like a mountain goat this team has scaled to great heights. When the alliance faced adversity they didn’t flinch. With human inspired intuition driving every action, this robot stepped up and delivered. There is nothing redundant in its parts or in its construction, this robot is all quality. Congratulations, Team number 190

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Medtronic
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Some bots are driven. This one is orchestrated. With motion profiles that do not “jump the shark”, and motion smoother than maple syrup, their robot is dialed in from intake to alignment. Scoring as quickly as you can press a button, this team turned chaos into choreography. Congratulations, Team number 7558

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Medtronic
records.script: Before the buzzer finishes its breath, this team is already making moves. Whether in auto or tele-op, game pieces can’t hide. Scoring four in a flash during auto, this robot flows right into tele-op like nothing changed. Their smart controls, sharp interfaces, and routines blur the line between human and machine. This robot doesn’t just move – it decides. From a coast town with a flavorful name… Congratulations, Team number 180

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Galileo Division presented by Medtronic
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Their cohesive and memorable aesthetic extends beyond their robot, reflecting a strong team identity which they carry forward to their outreach events. With a visually striking robot bathed in vibrant orange and adorned with a distinctive hexagonal motif, this team has captured our attention and imagination. Congratulations, Team number 8708

With its intelligent eagle eyes, this team is relentless in the pursuit of its mission. With a large wingspan, this team is going the distance by building inwardly, outwardly, and soaring to new heights. The sky is the limit as to where this team will go in the future, as they help build the future workforce at Robins Air Force Base. Congratulations to Team 3635, Flying Legion.

This team learned to soar to new heights. This year they loved having the sea in their feathers. Through their multiple STEM events and their mentoring initiatives, they are inspiring others in Forsyth County to have an appreciation for engineering. Congratulations Team 4112, EagleBots

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team's design captured attention not only with its striking visual appeal but also with its impressive functionality and engineering excellence. They couldn't bear to stay in the pits, instead showcasing their purple bioluminescent glow with pride, a true reflection of their innovation and determination. Every aspect of their design radiated a sense of purpose and creativity. Congratulations Team 9480, Gear Bears.

This team has taken the charge to find new sources of funding. With their student initiative they are engineering a way forward. Ramming their way into the local market the judges are excited to award the "Enterprise Award" to team 8100, Grayson Robotics.

This team has been re-generated and shown a desire to grow. They are a marvel to see. Willing to help out other new teams, they are becoming a vital part of our ecosystem. Congratulations Team 6944, Wolverines.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.teamName: Career Blazer Robotics - The Fighting Mongooses
records.script: This tight knit group has demonstrated valiant efforts in their recycling abilities and team continuation. Their continual fight for our environment is apparent. We are not weaseling around with this team. Congratulations Team 5900, The Fighting Mongooses.

Even though this team has not been a resident of the reef long, they have made their mark with their unforgettable spirit. This team at its core shows atomic energy and passion that is unstoppable. Congratulations Team 10376, Plutonium Panther

As this team explored the depths of the reef, they expertly selected their prey through a precise targeting and seamless real time navigation. Once their quarry was captured by their Kraken-like claw, they would release their air tanks, swiftly surfacing to deliver their treasure to the barge. The engineering brilliance of this team is nothing short of legendary, rivaling that of the ancient Greeks. Congratulations Team 9477, Lambda

This student led team built a machine that would have made Archimedes proud with their screw design. Even though they are super busy they always found time to help other teams. Who says midtown Atlanta only has great restaurants. This team lives it’s gears for the greater good name! Congratulations Team 1648, G3 Robotics.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Get ready to blast off into a world of creativity and innovation as we announce the winner of this award! This team dazzled us with their alien-themed team unity, green antennas, and truly out-of-this-world creative robot design. And now, let’s give a thunderous space rocket cheer for the Columbus Space Program, congratulations team 4188.

Great engineering conceptualization can come to you at any time…even while swimming quietly in Atlanta, Ga. With a focus on ease-of-assembly, modularity to support quick modifications and high reliability to handle the rigors of game play, the byproduct is a robust design that delivers. Congratulations Team 6340, Marist Manatees.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: With exceptional precision, this team showcased remarkable speed and efficiency, executing repetitive strikes on their target with flawless consistency. They meticulously defined the optimal angle of attack, delivering their payload with accuracy while seamlessly sweeping away the adversary in a single motion. This innovative control system enabled them to approach challenges with unmatched finesse. Congratulations Team 2974, Walton Robotics.

This award goes to a team whose work stands out for its brilliance and ingenuity. Their innovation is undeniably Magnetic, attracting everyone’s attention with their precision and creativity. Congratulations Team 8866, Innovation Robotics.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team was simmering hot from the start. Their intensity was matched only by their flair and style with a matching theme that came together right down to the earrings. Their robot is an orange beauty. “Orange” you happy for the Orange team? Congratulations Team 6829, Ignite Robotics.

Showing up RED-y and raring to go, this team hacks away year-by-year: innovating, volunteering, and uplifting the FIRST community around them. The Impact Award goes to the team forged in fire, and built in magma: Team 3008!

This team didn’t just spark interest—they lit a wildfire of inspiration, going door to door to ignite passion for STEM and the FIRST community. With documentation so polished it could stop, drop, and roll into an engineering manual, and outreach tools as creative as cardboard cords and a ukulele, their dedication is truly on fire. They’ve turned every ember of effort into a blaze of innovation — team 3501, Firebots, is fanning the flames of future engineers everywhere!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Fine tuning their bot, helped get their scores to the top. Their well through out design, kept the whole reef's health in mind. Emerging victorious in their CRUSADE to win, the Industrial Design Award goes to Team 4270, The Crusaders!

This team has truly shocked us with their commitment to excellence both on and off the field. Their outreach is electrifying, sparking interest in STEM from the ground up—whether it’s hosting VEX IQ events or engaging with future innovators in their community. They’ve created a storm of legacy, staying tightly connected with their alumni who continue to generate momentum for the program. Their robot showcases high-voltage performance with autonomous operations that leave others in the dust, and they never stop iterating, proving that continuous current really is the secret to success. From impactful projects to a charged-up social media presence, this team keeps their community informed, inspired, and plugged in. With thunderous determination, lightning-fast innovation, and outreach that strikes just the right chord—this year’s Judges’ Award goes to… Blue Thunder, team 2443.

This year, the judges were inspired by a team that demonstrated remarkable resilience and potential with limited resources. Their dedication to learning and rapid development set them apart as a team to watch in the future. For their outstanding promise and perseverance, the Rising All-Star Award is presented to 9012, Team Waffles of Assets School.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This year, the judges were impressed by many team's commitment to environmental sustainability, but one team stood out with their This team didn’t just go with the flow—they made waves of change with their deep commitment to sustainability! From reef-safe innovations to current solutions like water filtration efforts in Kenya, they’re proving that true impact goes beyond the surf-ace. They’ve sea-zed every opportunity to protect our planet, and now it’s time to shell-ebrate their fin-tastic efforts! Team 6317, Disruptive Innovation!

To this small team, their robotics workshop is the reed they call home. Working as a family, each member is a vital component of their ecosystems as they come together to solve problems and celebrate successes. For exemplifying Team Spirit, this five-member team is the pearl of their city -- congratulations to team 3721, Charger Robotics!

1. These kids from Hawaii designed a fast and efficient robot. 2. Their robot provided physical stability and operational redundancy with a simple, robust design. 3. The winner is team 359, Hawaiian Kids from Waialua High School.

This team, bar none, exemplifies their positive attitude despite challenges. Their actions are displayed both on and off the field: translating manuals, advocating for STEM in their elementary schools, and using the Tech Cube in the community. For their exemplary conduct and dedication, the Gracious Professionalism Award goes to Team 4253, Raid Zero, of the Taipei American School.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: 1. This team holds the torch for creating a robot for collecting both coral and algae. 2. Their creative robot uses a rotating arm with an elevator. 3. The winner is team 3880, Tiki Techs from Kealakehe High School.

When the pressure was on and the competition heated up, this teams' robot never broke a sweat. With a modular design, making repairs quick, this team's robot demonstrated robustness and performed well under pressure. This team brings the heat to the Quality Award: Team 2853, Hot Spot Robotics, from Mililani, Hawaii!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This FIRST team came over the ocean with a weighty load. With push button control, they were able to put coral on different levels of the reef with ease. Controlling is their game. The winner of this year's Innovation in Control is team 7632, An Kang Robotics Maker!

As soon as the match ignited, this team's robot sparked into action. Their impressive autonomous routine navigated the field with consistency and accuracy. This team lights the way in autonomous. Congratulations team 2438, `Iobotics, from Honolulu, Hawaii!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Touching down in Honolulu, this team took in the culture of Hawaii while letting everyone know who they are. Armed with a beautiful magazine and an enduring passion for their homeland, they commanded our attention with stunning visuals. The image of this team's yellow logo connects grit with future innovation: an astronaut helmet with spartan feathers. Hailing from Alberta, the Imagery Award goes to Team 9277, The Sparkans!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division presented by PwC
records.script: Green with innovation this team has the FIRST mission in the bottle. Their low cost STEM kit proves they are thinking “out of the box” to reach underserved communities. These PIRATES are “Working in New Technologies”! Congratulations, Team number 3794 Prepa Tecmilenio WinT

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division presented by PwC
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: The design of this robot is the NIRVANA of maintainers. The ability to remove and replace components quickly is essential to any team’s success. The Judges were really impressed by the modular design this team implemented. Congratulations, Team number 1038 Team Lakota Robotics

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division presented by PwC
records.script: This team concentrates their talents on women in STEAM initiatives. Their creation of an innovative female STEAM Olympics has really SPLIT THE BRIDGE. Their THEORY is that STEAM is a way to connect new immigrants to their community. Congratulations, Team number 1241 THEORY6

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division presented by PwC
records.script: Even though they are rookies, this team gives back and makes everyone better, helping other teams achieve their maximum potential. They advocated for funding from their local government, borrowed and recycled parts from other teams, and shared everything they received. This small team feels “the need, the need for speed”. The Rookie All-Star Award is presented to:10224 MAV MECHANICS (NASA)

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division presented by PwC
records.script: We could go on FOREVER AND EVER about this team. They had a “VEX”ing problem when they lost their head coach and 60% of their team. They lobbied their school administration to hire a new coach, quickly fundraised for their team and shared it with others to allow participation in FIRST. They en-CIRCLED many counties and school districts to spread the FIRST ethos. Congratulations, Team number 3814 PiBotics

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division presented by PwC
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team is on the trail, continuing to sustain FIRST at home and abroad. They SPARK curiosity in leadership development across their many initiatives. They SIZZLE as they bring home the BACON! Congratulations, Team number: 1902 Exploding Bacon

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division presented by PwC
records.script: This team brings in members from far and wide. Their area may be void of other FIRST teams, but they are not void of spirit… or CHOCOALTE. You can see them in the stands cheering on their alliances with hammer and trident. “Let’s release the Kraken”! Congratulations, Team number 2539 The Krypton Cougars!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division presented by PwC
records.script: This team has made a SWEET robot that can do it all. They FLY around the field scoring algae and corals on all levels. Through constant innovation, this team creates a BUZZ whenever they take the field. Congratulations, Team number 33, The Killer Bees!

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division presented by PwC
records.script: They took on a “GRU”ling job driven by a desire to serve others. They created a sub team whose sole purpose is to seek out and assist teams who need help at competitions. This team is “STEALING THE MOON” and Gracious Professionalism with their MINIONS. Congratulations, Team number 8177 Vector

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division presented by PwC
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team STRUCK a very unique and creative design element. They effectively VACUUMED up algae off the reef. You could say this team is so successful that they always follow LIGHTNING. Congratulations, Team number 4907 The Thunder Stamps

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division presented by PwC
records.script: This great robot team is an amazing collaboration of 3 towns, proving the phrase “the THIRD Time is the charm”. This team really understands the importance of having great gears as well as keeping the battery down low. One can say this team really RATCHETS up the competition. Congratulations, Team number 4728-ROCORI Ratcheteers

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division presented by PwC
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team kept their eyes on the target, just like their bot which is constantly looking at tags on the field. They found their way to champs with their custom dashboard and simulator. Their robot moves as slick as a SNAKE and stings like a BEE. Congratulations, Team number 3339, BumbleB *Note: Judge from region is hoping that the Emcee will read the team number in Hebrew as well: shalosh shalosh shalosh tesha

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division presented by PwC
records.script: This team’s bot performed so well in autonomous, you’d think they had skills in MAGIC! Using camera guidance, their finely-tuned routine consistently scored three corals at level 4 and acquired a fourth. Don’t try to put these CATS on a LEASH—you’d need BAT WINGS to keep up! Congratulations, Team number 2877 (LigerBots)

records.eventName: FIRST Championship - FIRST Robotics Competition - Hopper Division presented by PwC
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s rebrand is pushing the limit to emphasize FIRST core values. SHIFTING GEARS, they desired to go above and beyond. From their pages of black and gold, their efforts in the community are OVER-CLOCKED. Congratulations, Team number 2485 Overclocked

The work that this team has done will be felt by teams from river to river, for generations to come. They found a unique story to tell that reached kids in every state in the country. Their vision and pleasant persistence paid off with publications and legislation, definitely winning the judge's vote.

Not only do they donate their time and experience, they also donate supplies to other teams. This team holds camps, conducts science experiments, and organized MINI BOTS DAYS. Follow the rows of corn to get to these events. Congratulations to the Engineering Inspiration winner - Team 167 - Children of the Corn

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team exemplifies the core principles of robust and durable design. Their custom belt elevator and reliable climber made a lasting impact on the competition. Just like a dark storm cloud, their all black robot weathered every challenge that came its way! Congratulations to team 9576 - Loretto Lightning!
Inclusion COLORS everything they do. When the status quo wouldn't do, they rewrote the code. If you're on this team, prepare to be sprayed.

This team impressed the judges with their clean robot design. They WIRED together the team, mentors and the community. They ignited a spark and made connections for an electrifying future. The Rookie All Star goes to Team 10739 - Wild Wires
This team more than tripled the number of returning team members. Weathering the tide to rebuild their team, they are programming toward a bright future. They are collecting rising stars.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Through bonfires and camps they grow. In pool days and Olympics, they bond. With each new design, their skills they refine and LEVIATHON rose bold to show. Congratulations Team 3928 - Team Neutrino

This team is clear in all they do and complementary, not just because of their colors orange and blue. Their enthusiasm is consistently displayed as a unified front with sponsors, judges, and other teams. Among the chaos of the season, they keep the positive, spirited energy up.

In the world of robotics, where design meets functionality, one team has truly stood out with their complete documentation and outstanding engineering. The team showed exceptional skills in tracing their designs from conception to completion. Their custom coral intake wheels, algae lure, and dropping flapper system gives access to their CAGE FLIPPERS that securely allows them to hang in the end game. After hanging out, you can find “Guppy” chilling at the “Doghouse”! Congratulations to team 525 – Swartgdogs on winning the Excellence in Engineering Award.

This team uses robots as a tool to help everyone become their best. Coalitions build teams that build students that succeed. Even small towns can do great things, if you get THE drift. Congratulations Team 4859. THE CyBears.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team had a unique perspective on the field. By utilizing multiple cameras, they clawed their way to success. Their use of a VR headset was a creative solution to a fundamental challenge! Congratulations to team 6391 - Ursuline Bearbotics

This team decided to mitigate risks in their robot design and strategy. Their super simple robot could be counted on to get the job done. The team TOWERED over the competition by pressing all the right buttons.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team BOLTED ahead of the competition. Their multi functional robot ROCKED the play field with its dual purpose intake. They took things to the next level and RATCHETED our hearts. The Innovation in Control Award goes to team 1706 Ratchet Rockers.

ARRRRR.... the sails automatically deploy, cannons are aimed for success. This team not only knows where they're at on the field, but even after the match. Let's welcome Black Beard to the field. Congratulations to Team 4646 - Wildcard Robotics for winning the Autonomous Award

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team fearlessly goes where other teams may not. They very deliberately integrated their school Halloween colors throughout their equipment, robot, and décor. Their brave bot's name, Ursula, clearly embraced this year's ocean theme.

Finding a need to spread the mission of FIRST in their community and beyond, this team operated on a different level. With volunteering as a core value, they’ve started and mentored countless FLL, FTC, and FRC teams. This team’s passion for robotics has Engineered the Change in Idaho.
This team identified a gap in their community that needed to be addressed. They are bridging the gap by bring STEM to the kids that are easily over looked.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: When it comes to elegance, this team never misses a cog. Their carbon fiber arm caught the judges attention in multiple ways. This team arrived on time from across the seas.

The Grit Award During this competition, this team showcased their drive and true Grit to earn their stripes. We hope they are inspired as much as they inspire us, and continue to build their new team for many years to come.
This team took flight to their first season with a sharp focus and high energy. With eyes on the horizon, they’ve soared into success, advocating for STEM in their community.

Despite being a young team, they have found a treasure chest of confidence. Building on the lessons of their maiden voyage, they navigated this season with collaboration and clear growth on the horizon. It will be hard not to notice this time on the field next year.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Forged with purpose and pride, this team blends strength and strategy every season. They’ve cultivated a program that grows stronger each year—mentoring, maintaining, and marching ever forward. Their legacy is no accident—it’s crafted for the long haul.
This team shoots high in all aspects. Aiming to grow their team, they have great enthusiasm. Their team spirit burns red hot. We are pleased to award one of FIRST’s first teams
This team sparked innovation with their build this year. They flipped the switch on conventional design with an arm capable of unlimited degrees of rotation. The current of creativity runs strong.

This modern council’s reach spreads far beyond the horizon. They can always be relied upon to provide support on and off the field. Their gracious professionalism shines bright enough to withstand even the sun.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.teamName: Victorian Engineered Robotic Nation or V.E.R.N.
records.script: This team doesn’t want to be in the “limelight.” Their creative take on vision has sent them on a quest. Let’s hear it for the team with the hats and the vests.

A team steeped in cultural history. With redundant systems, a bevy of unused spares due to a clean and robust design process that is driving top performance. Adding to the collection of Frequent Flyer miles

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This teams use of scoring task automation, combined with its innovative robot design and effective control features, makes this robot a true standout. And of course, with its signature googly eyes, it’s clearly recognizable from across the stands.

This team didn’t just plant the seeds of success; they programmed them to grow on their own. Their autonomous routine is crisp, well-seasoned, and executed with precision. Smooth, smart, and spud-tacular…

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team soars high with colorful style on and off the field. They integrated their team colors into all aspects of their design and outreach. Color me purple and take me to the RoboProm!

This team has exemplified and demonstrated characteristics of the “IMPACT” award as follows: “I” – International support for visiting teams to the Midwest Regional “M” – Mentoring the next generation of FLL to FTC and FRC “P” – Partnering with local municipal leaders and representatives to promote FIRST across the State “A” – Adapting technology and materials in creative and useful applications “C” – Collaboration with local community, youth clubs, and organizations promoting STEM and FIRST values “T” – Technical support through open alliance, programming libraries, and custom public scouting apps. After all of this, you too would be DOG tired!

This team has traveled far to inspire with their passion, knowledge, and commitment to engineering. They have mentored teams, conducted Lego Leagues, held webinars and expos to provide further access to FIRST. With an enthusiastic, “I’m Ready,” as SpongeBob would say, this team inspires others.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team has demonstrated the ability to ensure their robot holds up to the rigor of competition. Their consistent barge scoring is definitely GOLDEN. Hopefully, they aren’t too TAXING for their opponents.
Thirty members standing wall to wall in honor. This team is the definition of inclusivity, curiosity, and teamwork. This team will show their pastel colors this Spring!
In competition, we saw this team put up a spirited defense. They traveled a along way to push their CHIPS into our game. Small but mighty, they are “all that and a bag of chips!”

This team persisted through many challenges and started a rebuild of their numbers and balance. They evolved significantly, increasing women on the team and in their pit. In their toolbox was a titanic crash course for sustaining new membership as they try to CATCH THEM ALL!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team provides support for other teams in an effort to expand their resources. They have traveled far and are not afraid to expand beyond their domestic BUBBLE. They go out of their way to stick their NECKS out to help others.
Their spirit was strong, in the pits and in the field. They showed their true spirit with another team when they took the wheel. They have two Rosie’s, a safety shark, and a band of pirates.

When other teams were crossing wires, this high scoring team stayed aligned and organized. They methodically pieced together their goals and ambitions to engineer and clean robot. They GEARED their designs to fruition with excellence in engineering.

This Chicago-based team loves their Saturday pizza nights. They graciously help others throughout the year, playing together, machining parts, and even today assisting an opponent on the field to be the best they could be to keep the match exciting and fair. Watch out--this collaborative team will take you under their wing. They electrify all of us…

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team tried to solve the challenge from every angle possible. They designed a mechanism to differentiate their range of motion. This allowed them to score coral from L1 to L4 with the same EXCEPTIONAL wrist.

This small but mighty group shows quality through both robot and team. Keeping it all in house, they can do it all, climbing to success. They gather the brightest minds from miles around to design with simple geometry and play the whole game. Most teams want to keep the lights on, but this one wants to play lights out…

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team are specialists in the AREA of controls. They impressed the Judges with their data collection and analysis. Using April tags, they got into the ZONE…or multiple ZONES
Autonomous programming is based on a series of zeros and ones. Scoring coral is done with speed and accuracy by their robot. This team consistently scores ONE…and ONE…and ONE.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: From the highest high to the depths below, their, iconic imagery and attention to detail are hallmarks of this team. This team has successfully met their challenge to AIM HIGHER. Their identify is clearly integrated into name, logo, programs, and color. They have shown their true color, pantone number.

The FIRST Impact Award is presented to the team judged to have the most significant measurable impact of its partnerships among its participants and community over a sustained period, not just a single build season. The winner is able to demonstrate progress towards FIRST’s mission of transforming our culture. The recipient team will be invited to the FIRST Championship where it will compete for the FIRST Impact Award against winners from other qualifying events. This team’s mentoring and community outreach impressed the judges with a commitment to all ages. They have volunteered thousands of hours at FIRST events, fundraised to donate STEM kits, shared 3D printed items, and trained hundreds of students for a future in STEM. With a twist and a yell, they have forged ahead to increase diversity in STEM, both locally and across the state. They use Coopertition to create fun events and share analytic tools with opposing teams. Bringing STEM to their doorstep and toys to the kids, they have spearheaded their outreach to make a real impact. When it comes to fighting for STEM’s future, the judges want these Warriors on their side.

Through outreach, mentorship, and innovation, they inspire their school and community to embrace the possibilities of STEAM. Soaring to new heights, this team doesn’t just build robots, they build a passion for engineering. Rounding the bases with teamwork and knocking inspiration out of the park, they are the Eagles of Engineering Inspiration!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: The philosophy of this team was attention to detail. Their democratic process bolted them to an elegant design with flying finesse. They dropped the hammer on Industrial Design.

This team goes beyond the competition, making an unforgettable experience. Through their detailed robot design and extensive outreach, they have displayed dedication to FIRST Robotics and their overall community. This team is leaving their mark with a cyborg-like blend of grit and determination.

This team may be young, but they are already making valuable investments in their future. Through perseverance and determination, they have overcome every audit of their abilities, proving that dedication pays dividends. With a rock solid foundation and no exemptions for hard work, this team is a true Rookie All-Star!

FIRST is more than coming in first. FIRST is about teamwork and passion and inclusion and perseverance. This team forded the streams f adversity to rebuild a robotics team on the rock of the principles of FIRST.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team isn’t just flying high, they are charting a course for a sustainable future. With innovation solutions and sustainable practices, they reduce their environmental footprint while ensuring long-term success for their team and community. Harnessing the power of the sun, with the precision of a bomber, they are dropping sustainability initiatives that will have a lasting impact.

This well-structured team embodies the spirit of FIRST principles as they work together across various communities. They provide outstanding community support, teaching local Lego camps and reaching across the ocean to bring the spirit of FIRST to international students. They are showing their mettle and moooooving FIRST Robotics forward across the globe.
This team wore the hat for a stellar design process. They cooked up a recipe for reliable play on the field. They stirred in some excellence in their engineering.

This team knows that true success is not just about winning, it’s about lifting others up along the way. Whether offering a helping hand in the pits, Or fostering collaboration, they are constantly shifting their mindsets towards supporting others. By setting a new paradigm for teamwork and generosity, they exemplify the true spirit of Gracious Professionalism!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: By sailing their robot smoothly through autonomous, the points were scored. Creating solutions to move their robot and shooter floated them to the top. These pirates found the treasure trove of creative solutions.
This team removed their Achilles heel. Their highly robust design thrived despite all their clashes. Their strength was their Titan-like quality.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team has such control, you almost don’t realize they’re doing anything at all. With a feedback loop that allows continuous innovation, they have created controls that would rival those of a NASA rover.
This Team's vision gave them navigational clarity. Their Tel-Op was consistently above the line. The state of this team is synonymous with autonomous!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s theme was seeded deep and a head above the rest. Everywhere this team or robot went, it was obvious which team they represent. This pink flock is here to be seen!

A large portion of the state has benefited from this team showing how wide their impact is. Working to grow their impact with their local library, they also decided they could grow FIRST more outside of their pipeline. Supporting more than 40 various FIRST teams, this team has definitely rose to the CHALLENGE!

This team helps their local community by supporting a summer STEM camp, incorporating FIRST into the curriculum. Using multilingual language skills, they helped unlock more potential for those outside of their team to be involved with FIRST. Recognizing nearby FLL teams they support didn't have a future pipeline, they decided to start TWO additional FRC teams this year.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: The first thing you'll notice with this team is bright colors, but their design is just as nice. They've made a list, and before each match, they are checking it twice. When they spring their trap, you will feel the strength of the shark BYTE.

Winding their way through data, these cats are on the prowl. Developing a neural network to guide their game plan, the legacy of this app has begun. Stormy seas does not thwart this Tiger Shark The judges would like to award the Neural Shark award.

records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: This team cast their net far and wide to obtain sponsors who were SMITTEN with their potential. To get the cogs rolling for the season, they did CAD workshops over the summer and researched many programming libraries. They are GEARed up to represent Indiana at the World Championship!

With minimal resources, this team was able to dive into the season with excitement, optimism, and determination. They charged ahead to continually innovate not just upon their robot, but their culture. Their outreach efforts in-between competitions electrified the judges, and paves a bright path for the future.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has navigated through rough seas, dealing with several location changes. With significant efforts and fund raising, they were able to bring their shop on the road. Expanding their area of impact, they are creating a sustainable PACK in their community.

This team is always seen and definitely heard. With bright colors, enthusiasm, and classic chants, the judges could not miss them. You will feel their purple glow no matter where they are, on and off the field. GO “TEAM NUMBER”!

This team will leave the competition green with envy. Using Monte Carlo simulations they effectively developed their strategy. After hundreds of hours of investment, their 3D prints are out of this world.

When there is work to be done, this team puts on their helmets. With a focus on helping others in need, they are leaving a legacy of improving the coding process for all. Even though their armor is black, these Knights shine bright with Gracious Professionalism.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team has established an all-time legacy of greatness. Picking up from through ground, they score from side to side, with a twist. With style and uniforms as creative as their bot, they get the other teams GOATs.

This team doesn't just meet a standard, they shattered it...Literally. But no worries, they had plenty backups ready. Representing an unstoppable force from the WEST, give it up for a team that builds with next-level precision.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team has an unquenchable need for speed. While other teams took a more hands on approach, this team found success at the push of a button. Like a bull in a china shop, the real Swim Shady has stood up to the competition.
This team has shown they have a golden touch when it comes to autonomous. They may not even need drivers due to their sensors and code. They just continue to score and score...with SUPER speed.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team's vibrant colors can be seen from the robot, through the pits, and in the stands. They definitely sunk their claws into a brand worthy of the tin can. The judges think that their image is Tuna-tastic!

This team’s story explores the vast ocean and reaches beyond borders Their trophy case is filled with activities like there are grains of sand on the beach Don’t take it from us, Ryan and Benji will tell you that this team has oceans of IMPACT

This team is a pack leader in all that they do. From mentoring rookies, supporting STEM education to international connections, they race to make an impact. Their bark of excitement for STEM is contagious.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Through mathematical analysis and simulation, this team created a robot that is elegant, yet efficient. Operating on the same wavelength, they strive to separate themselves from the competition. Their robust and swappable mechanisms show their strategy is angled for long term success.
This team has been talked about throughout the pit. It’s not their first rodeo. Dr. Doofenshmirtz would want to steal their “Arm-e-vay-Tore”
This team got their gears turning. Coming in for their first year, they had lots to learn, but now these kids are golden!

Coming out of last years season this team was faced with many challenges. Through rigorous outreach for students and mentors they re-established their future for years to come. These student's horns are as sharp as their spirit.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Despite their shirts, this team doesn't turn blue under pressure. Student's take an active role in writing grants and even mentoring their own teammates. Every fiber fears the cyber.
This team packed the high school all night long. At every event, they have a howling good time. Their bark is just as big as their bite.

Starting from the beginning, this team PNEU they wanted to challenge themselves to climb to new heights. Their commitment to pushing boundaries, while consistently maintaining engineering and design processes helped us become PHYXATED. Their strong approach has them gearing up for a greener future.

This team has exemplified the principles of FIRST core values on and off the field. Even under pressure, they keep a cool head within the jungle and are always willing to help out. With the heart of a tiger they take every opportunity to support others.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This colorful team brought their out-of-the box thinking. They were faced with three technical challenges and solved them with Novak and elegant solutions. Like a cat chasing a laser dot, this team was focused on creative solutions to give them a competitive advantage.

This team made it a mission to build a robot that can withstand the rigors of the battleground while ensuring complete functionality. With elegant failure prevention mechanisms and elaborate plans to ensure redundancy, this team took reliability to a new high. This team can take one more thing off their "checklist".

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team was sky high above the competition Their use of sensors and tracking landed them in our top spot Their piloting of their robot jetted them past the competition

This team has been on the prowl this weekend. With an efficient auto and efficient control system, their autonomous actions consistently perform. They've really sunk their teeth into this years challenge.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team stands out in the pits. With clever posters, names and style they are wanted all around. You know who they are from a mile away like a train coming around the tracks.

This team is ready to Dive into Deep connections They constantly adapt to opportunities to connect with youth in their community. From starting FLL teams to hosting FIRST Robotics events, these Knights are ready to SUIT UP!

This team is taking off without leaving anyone behind. Their partnership with the community and rookie teams are all PART of sharing FIRST’s mission. Across Indiana this team’s THUNDER can be heard making FIRST loud.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team caught our attention with their futuristic design. With almost 20 iterations of their intake they pivot and rise to every occasion. This team is out of this world.

This team VIBES with FIRST’s core values. They bring a unique blend of precision and enthusiasm to create an unforgettable experience for their team and their alliances. It is clear their success isn’t just GUESSWORK

This rookie team came ready to PLAY taking THE FIELD with determination and strategy. they started strong on the OFFENSIVE LINE, working hard to recruit TEAMMATES and secure sponsorship from their community. Their PLAYBOOK was impressive and well documented in their engineering JOURNALS. With as strong GAME PLAN and passion for FIRST this team is destined for the END ZONE.
This team battled robot code like learning a foreign language and sometimes English too. Their wiring was “No Problema!”. And their “Determenacíon” is a role model for all.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Pay attention and stay alert. Have a plan for the worst, train your members as early as you can. SWOTs down adversity before it stings them. Living their mantra, Challenge accepted.
This roaring team is more than a machine, it’s a home for all. Where their beastly spirit stands tall. Release the Beast!
This team met obstacles and made early decisions to design a unique robot. With a smooth rotating arm made in Teal. When creating “Lamda” they are never accused of being SQUARE
This team is a beacon of support to the FRC community. Helping teams on and off the field to find great support is at their core. Just look for their KILLER colors in the pits.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team square dances outside the box. Their actuator mechanism is “Rollin, Rollin, Rollin” with no wires getting in the way with a unique coaxial configuration. Would the real SWIM SHADY please stand up?

This team used this event to shift into gear. Rewiring their robot for consistency this team takes flight with the help of their pre-flight checklist. Despite this being their second event ever, this team is geared for gold. Congrats to 10021

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team really went the distance letting their robot find its way on the field. Using time of flight sensors to align to each level, they benefited from the precision of their machine. Hats off to team 3176.
This team has a smooth take off and soft landing. They are able to score many pieces and climb with a push of a single button. Their single driver operated robot, Golden Coral, takes flight.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: When it comes to imagery its safe to say this team is the GREATEST OF ALL TIME. They sounded the HORNS on their robot, pit, brochures and even their hats. Everyone say Happy Birthday and Congratulations to Team 829

Through their outreach efforts with scouts, FLL, FTC, and camps for students in their districts, future engineers flow through their FIRST pipeline like WATER. Their enthusiasm for spreading the FIRST message is BOILING over.

This energetic team did a phenomenal job reaching out to the community. Their spirit of volunteerism was chivalrous and bountiful. Their commitment to the community gives these black knights a seat at the round table.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team used their evolutionary design process to swallow their competition. Their thoroughness in prototyping and design was out of this world.

The judges were impressed by this team's goal to develop servant leadership. Persistently standing at the door of every organization in the county fundraising, cajoling, and inviting others. So join in and follow the Axolotl Waddle.
This rookie team embodies a true partnership between their members and sponsors. Their aim and precision were hitting the mark. They pulled an arrow from their quiver and hit the bullseye.
This first year team has persisted through many trials and adversity. They have a strong plan for outreach and growth for the future and we can't wait to see them continue to grow.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow

This team demonstrated FIRST Core values in relation to not only themselves but to other teams. With an emphasis on fun, they consider each other family.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This robotics team played on their past experience to come up with a unique lift design leading them to CHECKMATE the competition.

In a sea of quality robots this team was "GOLDEN". Their untarnished dedication to craftsmanship gleamed through out the competition. They dove "SUPER" deep and can treasure what they have accomplished.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This teams use of a revolutionary controls system set the judges in a hunt. Though their quest to innovate the meta of FRC controls this team created a new method for FRC vision. This team's future is not virtual, its reality.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: You can tell this team put a lot of thought into their image. They had an aesthetically pleasing design all around from their robot and colorful organized tools to their specific t-shirts for each day. They really hit their mark with an arrow...or 3.

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University
records.script: This team impressed us with their ability to rise above adversity. From diverse backgrounds to diverse skillsets, they've built back their program that's now as sharp as a pitchfork. There definitely aren't any idle hands in this devil's workshop.

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University
records.script: This team showed up with energy that lit up the entire room! Their streak of enthusiasm continued to ignite excitement throughout the competition. Win or lose, they kept their fire burning bright.

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University
records.script: This southern team uses their radar to offer maritime aid. While taking rookie teams under their wing, they display gracious professionalism. Their bot was "super" when it thundered over the reef.

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team took an out of the box approach to functionality and form. Using a modular set up and multi-purpose mechanism, this team left the competition green with envy.

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team is so in control of their robot documentation. Their system requirements document has more than 400 tasks! Even NASA’s jealous, they’re Classified: out of this world!

records.eventName: FIN District Washington Event presented by Toyota Indiana and Vincennes University
records.script: This team spun their wheels for improved performance. With their 4 coral auto, this robot bubbled to the surface. Their team had to outrun a greyhound to conquer the reef.
