records.eventName: CHS District Severn MD Event presented by Ball Corp
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team stands out from the PACK with a well-balanced approach With the versatility of their controls, they were propelled to win after win. Their MAGNETIC cage capture helps SHARKBAIT give them PRIDE

records.eventName: CHS District Severn MD Event presented by Ball Corp
records.script: This teams approach to autonomous fetches the win They consistently score hands-off and don't settle for SCRAPS their coding is top tier and DOGONE great

records.eventName: CHS District Severn MD Event presented by Ball Corp
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team came barging in with a rebrand. By recruiting artists as a way of improving their aesthetics, they also broadened their reach of STEM Their HAND-PAINTED imagery can be seen in their pit, on their robot, and PUUR-haps even in Space.

The winner of our FIRST Impact Award does many of the things we expect from a top-tier team. They sponsor multiple FLL teams, run robotics events, and hold a multitude of outreach events at fairs, schools, and community locations. However, this team is further distinguished by the amount and variety of their initiatives, and the extent to which they are member-led. They have even designed STEM curricula for classes that are now used in their high school. The students have worked with local institutions and found a grant donor to help fund STEM activities at a local museum. The students helped drive the effort to initiate state legislation to fund robotics and other STEAM learning activities for all of Maine. Our choice did not just come out of the BLUE. The winner of the 2025 FIRST IMPACT AWARD is Team 6153, the Blue Crew!

This team is fueling the STEAM growth. With a three year vision in hand, they create new FLL teams, hold multiple STEAM days and multi-week programs, beach cleanup, and college STEM nights, resulting in BREW-TI-FUL community growth. Through all of this involvement, students can earn varsity letters. For DRIVING Engineering Inspiration, this award goes to team 166, the Chop Shop.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: When it comes to blending function with finesse, this team leads the CHARGE. They prepare like professionals: running off-season training, iterating through countless prototypes, and ensuring the modularity of their mechanisms. Their use of simulation and advanced tracking software proves their commitment to smart, efficient design. For a machine as polished as their process, the Industrial Design Award goes to Team 190, Gompei and the HERD!

For the Judges award this year, the judges would like to recognize a team of strong leaders that set an example for us all. This team is proactive in seeking out opportunities to support people with specific challenges and develops custom assistive technology. Additionally, this team was contacted by a local autism support group and have worked with them for the last two years to create robotics programs designed for Neurodivergent people. For their outstanding efforts to expand inclusion and assist those in their community, the Judges award goes to team 61, The Intimidators from BVT Robotics.

This team was very small last year, only to get smaller by the summer. But they GALLOPED back to a very healthy membership by engaging with their school though engineering classes at multiple levels, raising their visibility and finally getting people to GO WILD for the team. Congratulations to team 3314 Mechanical Mustangs!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: The winner of this years Team Sustainability Award has struggled in the past with recruiting new members. In recent years, they have taken proactive steps to address this issue by starting FLL and FTC teams. But where this team really shines is by addressing their environmental impact. This team reuses parts from previous years robots, they recycle their metal, they recycle their plastic, and they seek donated material such as fire truck parts to incorporate into their robot. The winner of this years Team Sustainability award is team 1729, Team Inconceivable!

This team encourages each other with positive attitude, smiles, songs, and humor. No matter what obstacles or problems they face, they know they are already winners by bringing 6 schools together to build a working robot in a few short weeks. Whether sending stickers to their proud sponsors, building ping pong shooters, playing Mario Cart or floating down-river, they are always bringing endless spirit, fun and good cheer. Congratulations team 2648 Infinite Loop!

When the competition heats up, this team stays cool under pressure, using a BLIZZARD of precision and design to engineer their way to success. Their meticulous design process leaves no detail to chance. From initial sketches to CAD models, they carefully chart their course, refining functionality at every step. With detailed flowcharts, problem statements, and a disciplined revision process, they showcase a professional approach to engineering. For their commitment to an exceptional design process and measurable engineering success, the Excellence in Engineering Award goes to Team 172, Northern Force!

This team consistently demonstrates Gracious Professionalism on a global scale. As a COG in the wheel of FIRST global, From Botswana to the Maldives, They took this competition by STORM. The winner of the Gracious Professionalism Award is Team 5422 Storm Gears!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Clanking its way through competition, this team's creativity rose above everyone else. The unique and creative coral handling mechanism JUMPS right out at you when you see this robot. Congratulation to team 95 - Grasshoppers

This team dove to great depths to assure quality on this mission. A low center of mass, hidden drive belts, and autonomous controls helped them place coral with ease. Their robust design assured that the mission would be free of CHAOS. Congratulations to team 131!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: We like to see creative uses of off-the-shelf commercial parts, and this team is transforming the field of ocular odometry. For their work in making the VIRTUAL a reality, The innovation in control award goes to team 5687, the Outliers.

This team SEES their way around the reef with ease. Their robot quickly and accurately places coral when it comes to autonomous navigation; at all depths, this team is no DEER in headlights. For their ability to navigate with precision, adapt to challenges, and execute autonomous tasks with unwavering reliability, the Autonomous Award goes to Team 6329, The Buck's Wrath!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Branding is what ties this team together all the way down to their color selection. This team has a uniform design throughout their shirts, robot, pit, and logo, with stenciling to seal the deal. They do not need Mister J for this master design. This team is a standout in the dark of night. The imagery award goes to Team 238, the Crusaders.

This team brings engineering discipline to their community outreach program with thoughtful planning and extensive documentation. In addition to starting and mentoring teams at every level, they developed detailed STEM classroom lessons for Kindergarten through 6th grade. Thanks to their peanut butter and jelly system, this team makes elementary education a top priority. They run a STEM Fair that is so electrifying you need a passport to navigate it all. This team believes that everyone should celebrate with kits that cover both robots and birthday cakes. From their Unified team to their structured curriculum, this team shows no IMPEDENCE. The FIRST Impact Award goes to Team #4925, The Resistance!

This team puts the community in their community-based program. Whether recruiting new mentors from local businesses, presenting to educators and state government, hosting twelve summer camps, or quadrupling the number of FLL and FTC teams, they share the joy of engineering with everyone around. They have made it clear that with the energy of a MONSTER and a steady focus on STEM, there is no MOUNTAIN they will not climb. The Engineering Inspiration Award goes to Team 9101, Green Mountain Robotics.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team’s deceptively wooden robot stood out vividly on the field. With a thorough engineering approach involving a game rules worksheet, maximum points analysis, a digital twin, and a careful revisioning process, this system FORCEs the team to leave no detail unaddressed. And it shows, with a machine that elegantly brings solid functionality with their signature PINK hue. Congratulations to Team 172, Northern Force!

The judges would like to call this the “Changing the Game” Award. This team is driving research and development for improving the FIRST game. They thoroughly studied the cost and resource impact of current bumper materials and developed and tested a cost-effective and eco-friendly solution, and plan to share their results to FIRST HQ. While the bumpers may be in red, we think this CREW would prefer them in BLUE.

Despite being a new team, this squad showed up ready to get KRAKEN! Their pit showed its true colors with their over-the-top decoration and unique swag Who knew, that 150 miles from the ocean, you would find a sea creature like the CephaloSquad!

Reduced to nothing, this team persevered. Memberships rocketed and sponsorships RAINED down The challenges faced by the team were not just BREEZES, and this season welcomes their THUNDEROUS return!! Congratulations team 2523, Tech Storm!!!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team SPEEDS through their efforts for their team and environmental sustainability. Not only do they have a FIRST pipeline and summer camps, but they have gone from ZERO to 100 by rallying other FRC teams to clean up the coastal community. This team certainly SHIFTED INTO GEAR towards an impactful future. Congratulations to Team 166, Chop Shop!

This team has a lot of spirit for community outreach. The excited cheering of the team and their supporters might even be heard back in their home state of New Hampshire. We hope to be invited to one of their movie KNIGHTS! Congratulations to Team 501, the PowerKnights!

This team applied the ideals of agile development to both their hardware and software systems. The resulting robot is a robust and efficient union of optimized mechanisms, state machines and innovative manipulators. This combination has led the team to create a great example of cybernetic success. Congratulations to team 4909, Bionics.

This team exemplifies Gracious Professionalism through their STEM outreach, supplying equipment for their local FLL and FTC teams and “Making it fun for All” attitude. Their efforts SOAR above the rest with their sharing of scouting information. The judges are proud to present the Gracious Professionalism Award to Team 2713, Red Hawk Robotics!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: The essence of creativity is facing a big risk and using teamwork to succeed. This team knew they needed too many degrees of freedom to achieve their goals in the game. They used an articulated mechanical design with an innovative software algorithm to avoid self-collision. Their robot can POSE, but this team is no poser. The Creativity Award goes to Team 5813, Morpheus.

This robot exemplifies excellent craftsmanship, reliability, and performance. The team's group-based design and development process has resulted in a high quality robot. Their approach has allowed them to respond to challenges instead of passing the BUCK. Congratulations to team 6329, Buck’s Wrath!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: We all know that the BOTTOM feeders are a key part of any marine ecosystem, and this team built a real down to earth robot. Its system for a loading coral from the back of its fiberglass shell is innovative, efficient and effective! Congratulations to team 9055, Knights of Katahdin (Ka TAH din)!

This team has set the standard for precision and innovation, with a robot demonstrating unmatched efficiency in the rapid placement of coral. Their flawless execution allows them to score well OUTSIDE THE NORM. Congratulations to team 5687, the Outliers!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s colors might seem a day early and definitely leave other teams GREEN with envy. Their robot’s nickname is so funny, it’s almost too much to BEAR. The Team Imagery award goes to the Tardigrade and Bear.ly functioning!

records.eventName: FIM District Battle Creek Event presented by BlueOval Battery Park Michigan
records.script: In a world increasingly split into good and evil, they have risen above. Providing even younger youth in their community with tech knowledge to help them grow. Where did they come from? Were they heaven sent, quite possibly. Congratulations, Team number 4422 Twisted Angels

records.eventName: FIM District Battle Creek Event presented by BlueOval Battery Park Michigan
records.script: Leading summer programs to inspire others they have given aspiring engineers the tools they need to brave the storm. They spread their engineering skills across the seven seas succeeding in motivating the upcoming generation to parrot their enthusiasm. Red sky day or night, it’s Engineering Delight. Qualifying to compete for the Engineering Inspiration Award at the District Championship is: Team number 3875 Red Storm Robotics

records.eventName: FIM District Battle Creek Event presented by BlueOval Battery Park Michigan
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team’s combining of design with artistic flare was Grand. With effective pops from 3D prints and powder coated parts for a sleek effective design. Their team and robot are Eastbound and down. Congratulations, Team number 5980 East Grand Rapids Robotics

records.eventName: FIM District Battle Creek Event presented by BlueOval Battery Park Michigan
records.script: There was no need to scavenge the depths. This team’s clever robot design and community partnerships rose to the surface. I found the Chili Man; he’s on the Crimson Pearl! Congratulations, Team number 4453 The Red Hot Chili Bots

records.eventName: FIM District Battle Creek Event presented by BlueOval Battery Park Michigan
records.script: This team pounced into action early and fast. These Rookies aren’t just spinning their gears as they work to develop not just a robot, but a team exemplifying FIRST. These fresh faces are the cat’s meow. Qualifying to compete for the Rookie All-Star Award at the District Championship is: Team Number: 10651 Gear Cats

records.eventName: FIM District Battle Creek Event presented by BlueOval Battery Park Michigan
records.script: Standing tall like a “Colossus”, They’ve made waves with their positive attitude and collaborative coding. Their Titanic effort has made a big splash. Congratulations, Team number 9743 MV Titans

records.eventName: FIM District Battle Creek Event presented by BlueOval Battery Park Michigan
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Who are they that keeps their team pipeline fresh while taking advantage of reusing components? Sparking an interest in STEM and FIRST with a summer camp for girls, they keep their sponsors engaged with frequent status updates. When asked if they are human or machine, they answered – I am Robot. Congratulations, Team number 4810 I AM Robot

records.eventName: FIM District Battle Creek Event presented by BlueOval Battery Park Michigan
records.script: In a challenging and competitive “rat race” this team managed to stand out. Their enthusiasm and positivity surely got the judge’s attention. Their style and aesthetic was nothing short of magical. Congratulations, Team number 7658 MagiTech

records.eventName: FIM District Battle Creek Event presented by BlueOval Battery Park Michigan
records.script: This team was like a perfectly welded joint—strong, seamless, and built to last! They shocked the judges with their current tech skills, wired communication, and a spark of passion for all things engineering! No need to keep twisting in your seats. Congratulations, Team number 4381 Twisted Devils

records.eventName: FIM District Battle Creek Event presented by BlueOval Battery Park Michigan
records.script: For more than a decade this team has been cultivating a “Robotics Nation” in a rural Michigan. Their promotion of STEM throughout the community has taken root and no student will be left behind. Their eager willingness to help other teams by sharing their onsite equipment has gained much “Traction”. Congratulations, Team number 3655 Tractor Technicians

records.eventName: FIM District Battle Creek Event presented by BlueOval Battery Park Michigan
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team was in Control of their Creativity at design and at play. Their innovation didn’t just climb the ranks, it harpooned success and reeled in results. This team’s bold creativity isn’t meant to freak you out. Congratulations, Team number 8126 Control Freaks

records.eventName: FIM District Battle Creek Event presented by BlueOval Battery Park Michigan
records.script: Achieving quality can be a “bear”. This team’s iterative process for improving reliability won’t leave their robot to the wolves. Failing forward for a robust design is the motto at the Zoo. Congratulations, Team number 6002 Zoobotics

records.eventName: FIM District Battle Creek Event presented by BlueOval Battery Park Michigan
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team “Swerves” to stay in control. With the aid of “Occulus” they keep their eye on the prize of going over the top. Their controls keep them steady in Reefscape while breaking “Alotta” waves. Congratulations, Team number 5152 Alotobots

records.eventName: FIM District Battle Creek Event presented by BlueOval Battery Park Michigan
records.script: The Autonomy of this team is in the “Limelight”. They have such “Summer” fun but sometimes “drain their batteries” and “scorched the carpet” while “spinning their wheels.” Their “Manta Joe” does the work allowing them to sit back and enjoy the results. Congratulations, Team number 8608 AlphaBots

records.eventName: FIM District Battle Creek Event presented by BlueOval Battery Park Michigan
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Through waves of competition, this team surfaces with a striking imagery. Their machine, apparel, and pits are a black-and-white masterpiece, hunting like a pod in sync. We will set Willy free to celebrate! Congratulations, Team number 7197 Mountie Megabots

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Main LLC
records.script: This team LIGHTS the way with their energy, mentoring an impressive cluster of FLL and FTC teams. They engage with the global FIRST community, their local community leaders and educators. They reach out to students with varying abilities, and share their resources freely. It is hard to miss the impact of this LIGHTNING STRIKE. Congratulations to Team 862 Lightning Robotics

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Main LLC
records.script: After losing a large number of seniors, this team is now BREATHING easy. This team is PUMPING life into its community, mentoring multiple FTC and FLL teams, and helping girls find a love for STEM careers. They have unlocked the CODE for team success. Qualifying to compete for the Engineering Inspiration Award at the District Championship is: Team 5567, Code Red

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Main LLC
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: They take FLIGHT and SOAR, “PREYING” on their competitors. Their motto of TRUST BUT VERIFY helps to confirm continued optimal mechanical performance of a well designed robot on the field. THIS BRAVE LITTLE TEAM didn’t leave any CRUMBS behind for the other teams. Congratulations to Team 3641, The Flying Toasters

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Main LLC
records.script: This year the judges award is for finding their robot’s STRENGTH WITHIN. Everything in this team’s design is handled with exacting precision, enabling the drive team to focus their attention on strategy during the match. Despite the design of their coral placement mechanism, this team does not take a PASSIVE approach to engineering. Like a BARRACUDA, they are always on the PROWL for high scores. Congratulations to Team 247, Da Bears

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Main LLC
records.script: This team is DRIVEN to succeed. They make full use of their resources, embodying FIRST principles and will make an impact for years to come For a young team, they are on FIRE Congratulations to Team 10349 Pontiac Firebirds

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Main LLC
records.script: After its rookie year, this team lost most of its members, The following year, they rebuilt their TRIBE by integrating middle schoolers as part of the team, including the core programming team. They engage local businesses and nonprofits and are building FIRST from the top down. Congratulations to Team 9182, Tech Tr1be

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Main LLC
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team is on a quest to elevate itself into the history books and to set a standard of GOLD. They are working with their community to clean up the environment, on both land and SEA. Many arms (all eight of them) make light work. Congratulations to Team 8728, The Argonauts.

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Main LLC
records.script: This team can really be FIRED UP at times and demonstrates strong energy through the entire competition. Their infectious spirit and playful sense of humor has proven to these judges they could even FLY if they put their mind to it. Kings and Queens have worn the color purple for centuries. This team proudly wears it as a symbol of their royal FRC heritage. You can’t miss this team in the stands or the pits. Congratulations to Team 51 Wings of Fire

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Main LLC
records.script: This team understands that the details make the difference. With their sketch-to-work-order process they integrate lessons-learned with student feedback. They won't need to make any ‘DEALS WITH THE DEVIL’ to get ahead in this competition. Congratulations to Team 5498, the Wired Devils

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Main LLC
records.script: This team was nominated by multiple teams not only for helping teams with coding and communication issues but extending and sharing robotics to the benefit of their community. Always ready to take a BYTE out of any problem as presented to themselves or other teams. They exemplified kindness, sportsmanship and a positive attitude rather than striking TERROR in their competition. Congratulations to Team 6528, Terror Bytes.

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Main LLC
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team SAILED through the game with a creative solution for 3D printed design that enables high consistency in coral scoring. Further, this team demonstrated a unique and creative OUTSIDE-THE-BOX strategy for ground intake algae handling and scoring. This VIKING tribe and their robot soaks up competitors like a SPONGE. Congratulations team 5167 VI BOTS

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Main LLC
records.script: The quality of this robot BLUE the judges away and turned them GREEN with envy. Starting with goals, proceeding to CAD, then prototyping resulted in a cleanly executed machine. They HARPOONED the competition and became the WHITE WHALE of this event. Congratulations to Team 7769, The CREW

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Main LLC
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: At the press of a button this team took to new HEIGHTS, If you FLEW over the reef you were able to watch as they SOARED through the competition. Controlling a TSUNAMI is an impressive feat, Congratulations to Team 5695 The Heavy Duty Eagles

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Main LLC
records.script: With a nautical name and a positively charged environment. This team has ACCELERATED its alliance members to the top of the board with a SNAPPY autonomous mode. Their FUSION of creativity and speed allows them to score three coral almost every time, Congratulations to Team 4405 The Atom’s Family

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Main LLC
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team may be ahead of their TIME in many aspects, starting as a 4-H robotics team. Clearly, FRC was their destiny. Their consistent use of props, wild hair, and custom art inspired by a movie. Fan-favorite event pins and pit signage completes the playful and humor-filled narrative. Time waits for no one, and the FUTURE is bright for this team. Congratulations to team 6344 Yale Jiggawattz

records.eventName: FIM District Berrien Springs Event presented by Edgewater Automation
records.script: This crew has conquered the HIGH SEAS of innovation, proving sustainability and outreach be at the heart of their voyage. Whether they’re bringing the circus to STEM or proving the world is not flat, their impact is no mere mirage. These Buccaneers be claimin’ SHARKNADO to be their finest treasure!

records.eventName: FIM District Berrien Springs Event presented by Edgewater Automation
records.script: Through mentorship, founding an FRC league, and expanding STEM access – especially for young women – this team has become a true powerhouse of influence. In a city where engineering meets innovation, one team is CHARGING ahead, lighting the way for the next generation of STEM leaders. They are ELECTRYFING the spirit of Engineering Inspiration!

records.eventName: FIM District Berrien Springs Event presented by Edgewater Automation
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: With a streamlined robot and attention to detail, this team’s commitment to the design process is evident. BRIDGING safety and aesthetics with rounded and capped edges to protect themselves and their electronics. This BUZZING bot really STUNG the competition.

records.eventName: FIM District Berrien Springs Event presented by Edgewater Automation
records.script: With determination to overcome unique supply chain issues they impressed the judges. They ZAP each challenge they face like a BUG. These busy BEAVERS can weather any storm.

records.eventName: FIM District Berrien Springs Event presented by Edgewater Automation
records.script: With passion and teamwork, they rise up with pride, In a classroom where knowledge and skill coincide. They BLEED GREEN with spirit, they work and they strive, Selling shirts to fund dreams, keeping hopes alive. ROCK NATION stands strong, and with LAMP as their guide!

records.eventName: FIM District Berrien Springs Event presented by Edgewater Automation
records.script: Being young and small does not hold this team back. With the help of a MICROSOFT assistant, they could teach a SCHOOL course. That CLIPPY is neat and ELITE

records.eventName: FIM District Mason Event presented by LIFT
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: They’re at the beginning, not the end. Their Coded Simulation and a raising lever for climbing made for a very creative solution and amazed the judges. Ho-Ho-No, that robot is not Santa, it’s “Manta-Joe”.

records.eventName: FIM District Mason Event presented by LIFT
records.script: Did you see it? Did you feel it? That’s Quality. Constantly calculating and calibrating, this team aligned their flight path. One could say they kept an “Eagle Eye on it”.

records.eventName: FIM District Mason Event presented by LIFT
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This well calculated & crafted bot from Down Under, whirls in action amidst the storm. With precision retention, their hardware is designed to hold the product - this robot really bites down! Guided by Python, they have proven that even in chaos , there is beauty in control.

records.eventName: FIM District Mason Event presented by LIFT
records.script: The autonomy of this team treats coral and reef like a pick and place machine. Their ability to auto path is making strong tie dye waves on the game floor. If you meet up at the barge, you may get caught in their “Freeze Frame”.

records.eventName: FIM District Mason Event presented by LIFT
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This species of robot does not normally operate in packs. The site of their fins send prey running through the reef. They are here to Chomp the competition.

records.eventName: FIM District Macomb Event presented by DTE
records.script: Today’s winning IMPACT team has had an immeasurable impact on FIRST students and their community. With a VAST array of outreach activities at major fairs, expos, and shows, this team successfully introduces thousands to FIRST robotics year after year. Their social media provides powerful resources for all teams in FIRST. This team won’t back down from a challenge—their commitment to promote future FIRST leaders is evident in their hosting FIRST events and serving as youth mentors. Within their program they continually INNOVATE to engage their students through “Lunch and Learns” and fun STEM activities. Their powerful advocacy efforts have created countless partnerships with their school, other FIRST teams, and civic leaders to improve funding for FIRST programs in Michigan and beyond. Their NEVER ENDING efforts to promote STEM extend well beyond their own team to grant INFINITE possibilities for all FIRST robotics teams.

records.eventName: FIM District Macomb Event presented by DTE
records.script: This team has become a standout in their community through their ongoing activities to promote FIRST robotics and STEM. Their PASSION and ENTHUSIASM for STEM is clear as they have successfully promoted all levels of FIRST robotics by partnering with their school to secure a grant, mentor and organize FLL teams, and host events. They help students LEARN by providing videos to be used in the classroom as well as developing summer activities to help students DREAM and explore STEM. They put their entire SOUL into their community through community service, school partnership, social media and summer camps. LEARN, DREAM, GROW, INSPIRE

records.eventName: FIM District Macomb Event presented by DTE
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This robot is a top performer, optimally filling the reef at the highest level. From autonomous to tele-op, their design shows great SYNERGY between hardware, electrical, and software. Ask any judge and they will say, “I AM impressed.”

records.eventName: FIM District Macomb Event presented by DTE
records.script: FIRST CORE VALUES award: There is nothing PLASTIC about this team. These ODANTRA ZIBETHICUS exude FIRST class core values. This team of ALLOYED SEMI-AQUATIC RODENTS really impressed the judges.

records.eventName: FIM District Macomb Event presented by DTE

records.eventName: FIM District Macomb Event presented by DTE
records.script: This team STEALS their way through the competition, BOLDLY building from the ground up, while moving forward MECHANICALLY. MARAUDING as they improve their game.

records.eventName: FIM District Macomb Event presented by DTE
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow

They CLAW to build FTC and FLL and DIG to help their city and neighboring towns while spreading the message of FIRST. Continued growth of sponsorship makes it possible to include all students free of charge while veteran students SCURRY to mentor younger team members. By the way, the robot is not bad either, with carbon fiber and STEEL!

records.eventName: FIM District Macomb Event presented by DTE

records.eventName: FIM District Macomb Event presented by DTE
records.script: This team came to compete with STEELY resolve. This one arm bot can do it all and excels in ENGINEERING principles. This bot is green like a frog but does not say ‘ribbit.’ Instead, it prefers to be called RIVET.

records.eventName: FIM District Macomb Event presented by DTE
records.script: This team is not AFRAID to help others. While SPREADING THEIR WINGS for food drives, FLL Competitions, making greeting cards, they graciously impact their community. They have “ ENGINEERED A BETTER WAY TO CROSS THE ROAD.”

records.eventName: FIM District Macomb Event presented by DTE

records.eventName: FIM District Macomb Event presented by DTE

records.eventName: FIM District Macomb Event presented by DTE

Tesla would be SHOCKED at the amount of support this team provided to their communities, including disadvantaged groups. Edison would be impressed with how they POWERED all levels of FIRST through mentoring and hosting events. Ohm would applaud the RESISTANCE they overcame helping teams in Nigeria "UNLEASH THEIR POTENTIAL!"

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow

They build the robotics KINGDOM by teaching programming to their subjects, young and old. Even the local fire department knows this team is KING when it comes to creative solutions.

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow
records.script: In the stormy sea of sports, FIRST came to the rescue. This team's ability to build robots quickly despite being new show the strength of the PACK. Starting with the young PUPS, these WOLVES will continue to excel as an outstanding team.

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow
records.script: All the gods are smiling on this team as they are building pillars for their future. This team's TRANSFORMATION has them performing at a level worthy of their ancestors. The network of younger teams they have helped create ensures their legacy will live on.

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow
records.script: The judges had a great FEELING about this team. They're always LOOKING FOR CLUES for team that need help, parts, or a sweet break from the pressure of competition. Their true COLORS show through as AGENTS by recognizing the great work of other teams at every competition.

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow
records.script: This well built, sleek robot with quality 3D printed ear, is the QUICKER, PICKER, UPPER. They were able to absorb points, leaving no mess on field. From the start of the year, this team put a BOUNTY on quality and coral.

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Using April tags to line up on their target, this team obliterated their competition at the push of a button. Redundancies allow them to be responsive to changing in-game conditions. No proton torpedo can take down this design.

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow
records.script: This team's FOCUS was clear on scoring with pin POINTE precision. Their ARMOR-CLAD guidance system navigated with ease through the competition. These brave KNIGHTS displayed keen VISION on the battlefield of play.

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Milford Proving Grounds
records.script: This team has ventured beyond the ordinary, charting courses through innovative ideas, groundbreaking technology, and unorthodox strategies. They have shown us that the most exciting destinations often lie in the places we least expect. They have fully documented their journey to places where curiosity in STEM and the FIRST community is ignited. Their sustained dedication and determination have been nothing short of a galloping success. This team has shown that when faced with hurdles, they don't just trot over them, they soar like a thoroughbred. The voyage has been a race well run, with each stride bringing you to victory this derby season. Good night and safe travels.

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Milford Proving Grounds
records.script: This team BLAZED a path through the STEM JUNGLE by bringing safety awareness to the community. Their magnificent triple C camp inspired LIONESSES to strengthen their pride. Their CROWNING achievement is assisting Fire Fighters with performing their duties.

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Milford Proving Grounds

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Milford Proving Grounds

A RIP TIDE of outreach efforts have made a huge IMPACT, creating a strong CURRENT of support within their community and we can’t wait to see them moving into the future with hurricane force.

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Milford Proving Grounds

records.script: Charting a course to weather any STORM, this RED fleet brings new sailors aboard for their green mission. Hoist the colors and sound the THUNDER, this team has struck gold with their sustainability efforts.

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Milford Proving Grounds
records.script: Losing their home did not CHILL their team spirit. They came out of the stands with an AVALANCHE of energy. It’s a team you want on your side in a BLIZZARD or to keep your drink cold.

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Milford Proving Grounds
records.script: These EARLY BIRDS excellently communicated their five-step design process which allowed the robot to SOAR to new heights. Competing in all aspects of the ocean by swimming, diving, or ascending, they were able to navigate the coral reefs with the accuracy of a “TERRI-DACTYL.” This team proved with their direct drive approach they can FLY with the best.

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Milford Proving Grounds
records.script: With no lack of coral to offer others, they GRACIOUSLY opened their facilities to let MONSTERS and BIGFOOT in. They were able to work through scheduling conflicts and limited resources to give them a home SWEET home.

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Milford Proving Grounds
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation

Extending across their RAILS, they creatively cruised through the competition from CAB to CABOOSE. Coming into the STATION for the creativity award their LOCOMOTIVE is on time.

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Milford Proving Grounds
records.script: This teams algae-picking machine is really taking FLIGHT proving it’s not a FEATHERweight when it comes to cleaning up the reef. Their controls allow them to SOAR across the field scoring coral quickly and precisely. Truly, they exercised EAGLE-tastic practices when designing their robot.

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Milford Proving Grounds
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Never getting lost at sea, this team’s custom vision and software systems allow them to SAIL past their competitors. They FEAR nothing as their robot can navigate port or starboard to bring their armament to bear on the reef, scoping through the coral. This teams controls allow them to DREAD nothing!

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Milford Proving Grounds
records.script: A double-sided design gives this robot BLISTERING cycle times. Cameras looking forward and back are optimized for BURNING a trail between the coral station and reef. With a flip of the arm and flick of the wrist this team BLAZES to the top in autonomous.

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Milford Proving Grounds
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Some robots just get the job done but this one feels like it’s ready to DRIVE THROUGH HISTORY. With a team imagery that combines FUTURISTIC flair and a touch of nostalgia, this team has created something FROM THE FUTURE.

This team is Fully, Engaged, Determined, and Strategic when it comes to expanding the reach of FIRST and creating lasting impact. Overseeing one of the largest networks of FIRST teams in Michigan, they work tirelessly to foster inclusion, particularly through their efforts to support hearing-impaired students in STEM. Their OPERATIONS extend beyond borders, partnering to start new FIRST teams in Mexico and mentoring teams in communities both near and far. With a focus on sustainability and community development, they share INTEL like their sponsor scouting tool, operation manual, and ASL FRC library with the FIRST community to help others BE A GOOD PERSON. Their commitment to outreach, inclusion, and innovation has set a powerful example of what it means to be true AGENTS OF CHANGE.

This team’s MIND was on inspiring others. They brought new students to STEM by recruiting members from outside of their school. They KNOW that their coding camps and STEM Dust days MATTER to the community. Sharing their MEMORIES about their 2 outreach events per month showed their CONSCIOUS effort to GROW STEM awareness. Their GRAY CELLS were FOCUSED on finely tuning the minds of youth in their K-6 outreach program.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This winning team demonstrated exceptional creativity, craftsmanship, and the ability to seamlessly score both coral and algae. These TYCOONS have a design that enhances user experience while addressing practical challenges in manufacturing and production. The Judges recognize these BARRONS’ excellence in design. Their innovative solutions combine functionality, aesthetics and sustainability easily, for an impressive DERRICK.

The Judges create a unique Advocacy Award. This first year team came SPINNING onto the scene ready to help everyone. They cut out the noise to help CONTROL the entropy of the day with their sensory kits. They build advocates to raise awareness of the unique needs of ASD students within robotics. They are spreading the CONTROLLED CHAOS around the globe.

From small ideas, big things can come! SOARING from a simple STEM class into a comprehensive robotics program, to learning how to use tools to place coral in autonomous, this team is learning FIRST is “More than Robots!”
This team came DOGGY paddling into view quickly, catching the eye of the judges. This small team has goals for growth as they expand their PACK. From YouTube to the field, these DOGS are RISING up.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team’s commitment to sustainability is SHORE-ly steadfast. Who knew Sustainability could be a work of ART? By combing through grains of sand and TIDEying up over 20 beaches, these KNIGHTS have SHORED up their future and ours.

This team had spirit from their heads to their SHOES. They lent a helping CLAW at their Saturday kid’s events, inspiring kids in STEM. Their spirit hasn’t become a FOSSIL and their shouts are DINO-myte.

Within the competition, this team is able to TRIANGULATE their location for optimal scoring. Their toggle switches on their swerve drive modules show that they are always thinking THREE steps ahead. With unbelievably detailed CAD drawings for each robot component, and a quality review process, this team’s engineering process guarantees them success at super-SONIC speed!

These AGENTS are always on the CASE! They show unmatched dedication to gracious professionalism. They not only created 3D-printed pit awards, but their AGENTS are always on a MISSION. They impressed the judges on Friday when they traveled back to their shop to retrieve a crucial GADGET another team needed.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Their creative design for grabbing coral BELTED the judges’ attention. With a smart sensor-controlled mechanism along with their unique deep climb, this team brought GREEN ELECTRIC ENERGY and clearer engineering to the field.

This team has a long history with the SEA. They built a robot to WEATHER it all! By BRAVING the Reef, their robot CAPTIVATED the judges with its dependability. You won’t find this team in RUINS, they’re sailing home with an EPIC tale. This team has a long history with the SEA. They built a robot to WEATHER it all! By BRAVING the Reef, their robot CAPTIVATED the judges with its dependability. You won’t find this team in RUINS, they’re sailing home with an EPIC tale.

Throughout the weekend, MOVING AT LIGHT SPEED, this team had some incredibly controlled and fluid plays, utilizing many autonomous actions. During the autonomous phase, they were able to CONSISTENTLY place 3 coral onto the top level, using navigation skills that rival those of the Millenium Falcon. The Force was clear with this team.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: By steering the SHIP of these young HUNTERS, they seek empirical control. Black and RED-iculously cool to its core, this team’s imagery would make Boba Fett proud.

records.eventName: FIM District Muskegon Event presented by RENK
records.teamName: Code Red Robotics the Stray Dogs

Their many WAVES of team building activities build hands-on skills that help float their boat. Supporting and developing team members through all levels of FIRST programs, their mantra is “building better people the entire time”. They've brought a lot of youngsters into the robotics world from their community and beyond, picking up STRAYs along the way.

records.eventName: FIM District Muskegon Event presented by RENK
records.script: Logging THOUSANDS of hours to prepare for the future, this team is thinking ahead. Traveling to Lansing and setting examples for younger teams, they are full “STEM” ahead! Ready to PUNCHOUT all obstacles for a brighter future.

records.eventName: FIM District Muskegon Event presented by RENK
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Climbing from the depths with a well-crafted machine that is both a mystery and a masterpiece Its sleek design and meticulous engineering come together like the perfect solution to a complex PUZZLE. Every element of their robot showcases a seamless fusion of form and function, leaving no QUESTION.

records.eventName: FIM District Muskegon Event presented by RENK
records.script: Judges’ Award for DEMONSTRATING REMARKABLE CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT. Not afraid to re-engineer their approach and chart a new course they ingeniously integrated systems to optimize navigating the reef akin to a masterful deep-sea diver. Their processes allow them to press forward, with a clear view of the horizon on their QUEST for a perfect robot.

records.eventName: FIM District Muskegon Event presented by RENK
records.script: BURNING up the competition with their performance, ingenuity, spirit and teamwork, they are more than just a FLASH in the pan. They have demonstrated they are not just a SPARK but a full-blown INFERNO of FIRST inspiration. Ignite the fuse and follow their bright flare.

records.eventName: FIM District Muskegon Event presented by RENK
records.script: With their ULTRA welcoming atmosphere, custom name tags, and bold colors, they’ve built a community where everyone feels at home, and their drivers DANCE their way through every challenge. Punctual in the pits, they’re always working '9 to 5' and beyond - come late nights or SUMMER RAIN! For their relentless spirit, vibrant teamwork, and bright future, they are truly A BREATH OF SPRING and deserving of the Rising All-Star award!"

records.eventName: FIM District Muskegon Event presented by RENK

Let’s talk about REPUTATION—because this team’s alumni don’t just move on; they STAY, STAY, STAY involved, mentoring, cheering, and even helping build and share practice spaces and sponsorships. With 80% of this teams members being introduced through FTC and FLL and a 100% STEM education rate for recent grads, they’re proving they can stay on the CHARTS all year long. To foster interest in STEM and FIRST, they design and run a variety of creatively themed camps year-round that appeal to multiple age groups and skill levels. Their passionate commitment to equity, diversity, and inclusion shows up not only in their team, but also in their outreach to rural youth, disadvantaged kids, and women. When this team unexpectedly lost their lab space, true to their mascot, they were tough and resilient. They applied their skills in communication, persuasion and relationship management to locate a new space and secure financial backing. records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: An agile team focused on continuous improvement, building a positive and persistent culture and community. Supporting multiple teams as if there are one, ensuring knowledge is passed for members to come. Like cattle and bison, they stampede along, making sure their team is sustained life long.

There's no doubt that teamwork really make the dream work for this crew. Countless members were thrilled to tell us their role in the team's week zero event. Talking about FIRST clearly ignites their spirits.

Beneath the reef's surface, deep under, lurks a marvel that's truly a wonder. With a might arm, instead of a tail, it snatches coral, flashing it's metal scales. Swimming so fast, as gears and belts mesh, This denizen of the deep, who's name is Jignesh.
With LGBTQ+ and mental health at the top of mind, This team with a TWIST has great drivers in line. Their gumption shows in their alliance of scouting, With unicorn hats, you can hear them shouting.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: While climbing a cage, there are many ways to conquer. Instead of following the pack, this team chose to hunt on their own. A twisting lock caught their prey. A mechanism as unique as a tiger's claw. Congratulations "Timmy Rhubarb" - team 2227.
This team crashed into the top of the rankings. From electrical panels to mechanisms, their robot is truly built to last. The judges were impressed with their space-grad construction.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team had a clear recipe for success. Start with a coop full of autonomous during and scoring routines. Mix in 5000 lines of custom path planning software, and finish it all off with a generous helping of chicken.
Through coral and currents this bot takes aim. Scoring up to 4 corals in auto - what a game. Tracking, turning, smooth and free, A master of autonomy!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: From their T-shirts to their booth, this team brought a sea theme into all design aspects. Even their robot was designed to take on the appearance of a sea slug. When they hit the field, they caused a storm.

When other teams need help, they don’t hesitate to go the distance. Bedazzling the world with the power of STEM, one robot at a time. The impact of this team truly has no borders. Congratulations to Team 2883, Team FRED

With a flood of excitement on the way to the Reef, this unit doesn’t fall flat in inspiring growth in their team and impacting students and sponsors in their community. Their four captains guide the Torrent through a sea of ones and zeros. Congratulations team 7028, Binary Battalion

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team took the mystery out of the ocean depths. They captained their design without going overboard. They know that lobsters are better than dinosaurs and clawed their way to win this award. Congratulations Team 6175, EVW Mystery Machine.

From the valley to the reef this team’s independent systems work together and the judges recognize the endless options that these students can achieve. Bringing matter and energy together, they forge a path to the future. Congrats Team 7578, Quantum Mechanics

Small team size and budget cuts didn't keep them down. They found new sponsors in their quiet, little town. With creative new approaches, they inspired their community, like youth programs, meat raffles, and dinners of spaghetti. Hard times are behind them, and their future looks great. Congrats to these Rising All-Stars, the Anndroids, Team 3058.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: There once was a team by the river, with aluminum traded for metal delivered. With Niron they schemed and sustainability dreamed, congrats to Team 6045, the great giver!

Duct tape and zip ties bond this team with their community. Team members stand out in a crowd, especially a big parade. They really know how to celebrate with fruit salad and pop. Congratulations Team 3026, Orange Crush
When traveling the ocean on a three-story ship, you want to have reliable wiring under you for your trip. If you get caught in this riptide, it is not a blip. Congrats to Team 4607, C.I.S.

This team in green made quite a splash, helping others in a flash! With code, a clamp, a guiding hand, they kept the pits safe and happy as planned. They mentor kids and sign hubcaps too - Terabytes, this one’s for you! Congrats to Team 6749 from Hopkins, MN, and their robot, Orca!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Designing a bot to mitigate risk and support their alliance. This team specifically prioritized a niche many other teams made a second thought. These howlers clean the reef like a shrimp in Finding Nemo. Congrats Team 8422, Husky Howlers

When choosing this award and who we tap on the head, the team with the 80 inch bot is sure to wrench ahead. Wrench, wrench, grey wrench - you’re it! Congratulations to Team 4728, the ROCORI Ratcheteers.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.teamName: Robo Remedy @ Manitowoc Lutheran High School
records.script: When it comes to practical control innovations, this team experiments. Their study of sensors fulfill their alliances’ needs and is exactly what the doctor prescribed. Their control system is so clinical, it makes our hair stand on end. Congrats Team 7103, Robo Remedy!

Three piece coral is no problem for this team. Their ground intake help their alliance jump out to a fast start. This team was able to score both coral and algea in auto with some great tools. More than just dogs are scared of these black and yellow cats. Congrats Team 3276, the TOOLCATS

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has truly brought the beauty of the ocean to life in their robot design. Their heartfelt reefscape theme features handmade artwork and vibrant colors, celebrating the spirit of the sea. With a touch of creativity, they turned their robot into a vessel of support, reminding us that even when things got a bit “janky,” there’s always something to celebrate! With an ocean of creativity, we proudly award the Imagery Award to Team 4656, Rock Solid!

This team is a big fish in their small community. They have saturated their elementary and middle schools with FLL teams. They are ever-present at community events and festivals and have even started their own community event to celebrate STEM with pancakes. They lobbied for the use of referendum funds to provide STEM and manufacturing facilities in their school. They host coding camps, and other events directed to attract girls to STEM. They have truly made an impact on their community. This team hounded their way to change STEM culture in their town.

This team has a leg up on their competition with a flamboyant passion for STEM. They are not just their robot, always ready to step up to bat for their community. This is one pink feather they should be proud to wear.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Like a vessel charting through reefs with grace. Every component is in its proper place, arranged with true precision. And electronics protected with a thoughtful decision. Form meets function in this clean machine. That's the elegant design of Nautilus we've seen.

Small but mighty, proud in diversity, complimenting others on the REEF scene. With back up plans when swerve faced the test, they crafted designs that proved their best, Placing coral on levels two and three shows what determined heroes they can be!

In just 60 seconds, this team proved that consistency, passion, and purpose can make waves. They make every dollar count, and bring novel design to life with unique parts. They really minute (mean-it) when they say they are ready for the next challenge

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: With a focus on inclusivity, longevity, and joy of life, this team has their head in the zone! They take being green to the next level by promoting sustainability and recycling. This decision was a piece of cake.

The shipmates on this team filled the arena with their cheers. Instead of stealing gold, these pirates spread excitement, energy, and extraordinary enthusiasm. The attitude of this fleet commands the spirit of still water.

This team was thoughtful and considerate about their design process, down to the document handoffs and part quality control. We were left googly eyed by their professional approach. To a team that is passionate about their inventory control spreadsheet.

This award goes to someone who leads with sharp vision, steady grace and respect for all - just like the spirit of FIRST. This high-flying team demonstrated swift generosity by sharing batteries, parts and support with teams in need - showing once again that kindness powers more than robots. With the quiet confidence of a raptor and a humble heart, they showed that coopertition is part of who they are.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This group embraces all aspects of STEAM. From their robot's many degrees of freedom, and their work as a team. A scoring system designed after a flexible fish, this team can score anywhere as they wish. Their mission was perceivable, believable, and achievable.

With intentional designs and a sturdy machine, this team's reliability stands tall despite having a short robot. Using a led screw and 2x4, they rose to a higher altitude of performance. Like a summit challenging their competition to strive for excellence, this team has powdered through their matches.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team may look like they are on vacation, but their robot shows nothing but dedication, with encoders that don't skip, this team's robot refuses to tip. Their aided controls improve their alignment, this team and their robot understand the assignment. Please put your sunglasses on and your hands together as we welcome our winner.

One team stood out bright and clear. They bulldozed our expectations - scoring a staggering three and even four L4 corals with literally in-human speed. Not to be outdone, their drivers utilized their autonomous tools with grace and their custom trajectory engine to pave their road to victory!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team is breaking barriers. With a robot built to dive, their perseverance and compassion will take them far. They will tell you what to ask, and they're not all talk. She says 'no' to keep their team pink. And with every matching robot, they're growing the 14%

With a consistent legacy of developing and sharing team resources and engaging with younger students, this team has supported the growth of FIRST and STEM in their community... and beyond. Expanding their impact in new ways this year, they are now… HOLDIN' … hands with new teams.

Students enter the FIRST pipeline through numerous camps, events, and an FTC team, then continue with a structured one-on-one training program. They invite other teams and the community to view kickoff for a pancake-flipping good time. With a comprehensive action plan to advocate for state funding, they certainly aren’t horsing around.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Robust materials and assembly come together to create a professional aesthetic. With new fabrication capabilities, this team shows that good design is knowing which corners to cut and when its better to BEND AND NOT BREAK. This robot might be black, blue, and “broken” all over, but its construction ensures this team is never down for the count.
From a small-town reef, this team has surely grown. Like David vs. Goliath, this team has shown: believe in yourself and be a dragon of your own!

This team is planting seeds for the future. Their FLL pipeline, camps, and outreach are CORE to their ability to inspire future engineers. Like their robot, they browse the highest branches of each apple tree.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team dove right in to build up STEAM. Through outreach, advocacy, and community, they’ve caught the judges in their web.
They came across a deep blue sea, To share their spirit and energy. This team is electric!

The professional design and bright colors of this team really shine on the field. Their tilting elevator effectively collected coral from the ground and human player. This Grim Reaper is an Inspiration to all they align.
When this team got the notification, they rose to the challenge. Their roar to help was loud and clear. These hosts showed us their Gracious Professionalism with purple hospitality.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Their distinctive headgear isn’t the only thing that catches ones eye on the reef. Their button box controls a coral system that inspires collaboration among team and alliance. There is no limit to what this gun-slinging sharp shooter can design.
This team speeds around the reef like a red-yellow blur. Their robot’s modular design lets them perform like a quick-change artist. In this game of liquids, this team simply melts the competition.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team’s on-field navigation system makes On-Star look like an amateur. Their four-eyed vision system eats pixels for breakfast as they fly to each April Tag and align for the win. These Top Guns can run simulated matches in the Matrix without any glitches to improve their performance on the field.

On the rough waves of FRC, a good lookout is key. This team coupled their limelight lookout with a high perch to place coral. This simple yet effective strategy meant they were always well armed when teleop began.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: A true REEFSCAPE DREAM, this team surely sets the scene. A lighthouse gleams as their robot’s guide, sailor hats and jackets are worn with pride. All hands on deck for this TIGER team.

• This team has expanded their reach not only to local communities and individuals, but also to state officials and global partners. • This team exemplifies the FIRST foundations of Gracious Professionalism and Coopertition by pioneering programs to serve underrepresented groups, support of individual challenges, and STEM awareness. • Come soar with them as they fly high and inspire others through their many initiatives

• This team is very visibly advancing STEM within their community through summer camps and mentoring. • Their electrically charged metrics substantiated their success. • Young Sheldon would approve of this winner …3..2..1..blastoff.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: • This team’s silky-smooth design bucked them to the top of the judge’s list. • Their coral & algae shooter rode side saddle on their elevator to protect it from outlaws on the open field. • This team’s high scoring robot will efficiently ride off into glory.
• This team’s innovative design and helpful demeanor truly set them apart. • Elevating other teams to a higher level by sharing their expertise. • Thank You for Inspiring us all.

• This team rebuilt themselves from the street up. • They are the “A” in steAm and they persevered with a broken leg/robot. • Using the field as their stage, they celebrated every part of their performance.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: • This world class team has a vision for the future. • They bring the bling to their community by nurturing a fresh batch of FIRST teams as well as transforming the landscape around them. • No doubt we will hear their thunderous roar for years to come.

• Sounding the horn, this team exhibits enthusiasm both at their competitions and in excellent partnerships at their school. • They don’t pass the buck on having fun even as they focus on volunteerism. • From building a fantastic robot, to 3D printing a memorable hat, you can certainly say that they solve problems.
• This team fused simplicity with sophistication to bite the cage. • They used their thunderous hammer to place delicate coral. • In the end, this CAT…or should I say DOG…pawed its way to the top.

• This team plants the core values of FIRST all around the globe. • They enjoy building connections as they promote growth in their community. • They not only talk the talk, but walk the walk both on and off the field.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: • This team kept an EYE out for a unique solution to an overlooked problem. • They wrapped their tentacles around past successes to fill a niche on the field. • They have had TOP SUCCESS in algae manipulation using their fish finder mounted intake.

• The robustness of this robot kept all of their nine lives. • They maintained functionality with maintenance plans, spare parts kits and extensive logging. • They have made jumbo strides and kept themselves out of hot water.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: • This team was popping around the field. • They wrote predictive navigation to help their driver align to the reef. • Iron Man would be jealous of how well this team’s repulsors helped them to fly.
• This team overcame a low tide. • They took a gamble and stayed with a pair. • The team navigated the reef to a winning hand.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: • The scent of victory follows this team on every adventure they embark upon. • They are celebrating 20 years of cohesively working together to serve their community. • This Team has cooked up the recipe for success and sailed heir way into winning this award.

This team is a champion for science, technology and student empowerment. They advance the mission of FIRST by uplifting an array of teams from FLL to FTC to FRC. They host, support, and mentor teams locally and globally, providing tools for success through coaching workshops. They also advocate specifically for STEM education for children with disabilities through a wealth of resources accessible on their custom made website. At the state level, the team lobbied lawmakers to share the value of providing financial investment in STEM education for underserved communities through legislation. Join them in April at the Capitol for the STEM Educational Innovation and Advocacy Day. This team's strategic focus in on a sustainable future for FIRST - an ultimate objective for a team with nine lives.

The Engineering Inspiration Award is basically a badge of honor for turning engineering into an epic adventure. This year's winner, known for rocking caps and feathers outside of competition, their robot took up golf and had pilot training from the Blue Angels. Hailing from St. Peters, MO, they've reached 60,000 people, including kids, during Christmas across the world. Congratulations to 4329 - Lutheran Roboteers.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team's robot was constructed to be bold, efficient, and stand out. Their waving arm is iconic, effective, and methodical. The extensive use of industrial design practices helped this team RUSH to new heights. Congratulations to team 27 - Team RUSH.

In just two short years, this team has built a wide base of support by hosting corporate presentations, creating FLL teams and hosting STEM camps, FTC kickoffs and tournaments. This team's connections stateside and beyond, including a trip to NASA, have been foundational to their growth. If you are in southwest Missouri, ask them out for their favorite nutty poultry dish. Congratulations to Team 9428 - The Cashew Chickens.

Robotics is based in science, but creating a new robotics team is an art. This team is it's renaissance, flourishing in its rebirth, developing presence in its community, and creating several connections with its partners. Look to this team's orange and green 3D printed parts if you want an example of how to fabricate a new beginning. Congratulations to Team 10317 - CIA Robotics.

This team faced the challenge of losing their build space but refused to fade. With the instinct of an ant, they found a new home and flourished. Their relentless spirit spread FIRST ideas to rural and underprivileged communities, igniting a movement. Like a true army, their resilience and commitment made them a Rising All Star. Congratulations to team 3792 - Army Ants.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: When they heard the vibrations from far below the water's surface, they took action. By building habitats and forging partnerships, they enhanced the environment and inspired others. They were fishing around for sustainable practices. Congratulations to Team 4330 - Rambunction.

This team is driven through their rebranded look and logo and commitment to younger teams. They exuded sophistication and swerve when talking to the judges. These enthusiastic Men in Black are bright flashes of light to all who encounter them. Congratulations to Team 6744 - Melville RC.

This team attacked the design process with feline precision. Their CAD models, prototypes, and drawings created a robot that struck fear in their competition. They understood that "failing fast" is the best way to avoid extinction. Congratulations to Team 2506 - Saber Robotics.

This team represents the best in all of us. From mentoring aspiring team members in their small school, to lending a helping hand to over 15 teams at this event alone, teamwork and collaboration are always the mission. This team is in complete command of the FIRST core values that guide their exciting journey. Congratulations to Team 5889 - Commandobots.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team stung the judges with the highly reliable, and remarkably simple feature, which stood out for its elegance and functionality. Watching this system perform, you may become unhinged. This team creates quite a buzz in their community, in the pits and on the field. Congratulations to Team 8069 - Super Hornets.

This team really *shocked* us with their top-tier electronics package, neatly wired for reliability and ease of maintenance. Their custom truss rod system bolted down a strong yet lightweight foundation, keeping their robot rock solid on the field. We are ratcheting up the excitement to present the Quality Award to Team 1706, The Ratchet Rockers!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team has a nose for precision, always tracking the right balance between power and control. Their use of physics-based stability calculations, real-time diagnostics, and data driven simulations has set a new standard for intelligent automation. No matter how fast they push forward, they never lose their footing - true to their name, they always hound down the perfect solution. Congratulations to Team 4500 - the RoboHounds.

Successful auto OPS starts with defined path planning and is augmented with video sensed deviation correction. Relying on computed trust factors, this team's golden touch consistently scored multiple autonomous coral placements. Congratulations to Team 9401 - Midas' Mayhem.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team beautifully reflects the spirit of FIRST from the FORCE and style of their robot, which aligns with the HEART of the team's fashion. Their interactive game and energetic team members reeled fellow reef dwellers to their attractive pink and red pit. With waves of gratitude, we grant the imagery award to Team 7472 - R2 ESU Robotics.

This team has been finding innovative ways to bring FIRST and STEM to their community for many years. They create lasting waves of impact by partnering with colleges, schools and charitable organizations. They’re preparing students for college, securing internships and creating adaptive devices to assist those with disabilities. This team swims with ease and flies high.

This team doesn’t stop at county, state or country lines, but continues to grow FIRST in new countries. Their beacon of light shines throughout the community with continual fundraising and outreach events. Just like ‘PI’, their impact is limitless (goes on forever).

This team connects people of all ages and abilities with technology. They are ‘bill – ding’ a foundation with their state for a stronger FIRST program. Having hosted their first district FRC event, this team shows no end to their enthusiasm and commitment to STEAM!

This team has created a GREEN environmental sustainability program to recycle plastics and other materials. The objects they make from their recycling are used to promote their outreach programs - especially with girls. Collect all their cards and learn more about FIRST Mid-Atlantic Robotics.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This robot jousts its way to the top with its dynamic arm and climber. It was able to effectively complete all aspects of the game. It is almost like they are on a crusade.

From the Delaware Valley to the great blue seas, this team reaches out to all of FMA. By including students far and wide, they have created a team for those who could otherwise not compete. Whether in person or via a virtual meet, MORT and Gamma are a judge’s treat. The Judge's Award for FMA's first hybrid team

records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: These rookies have grown from within through existing STEM activities. Forget “see you in September” – we’ll see you at STEM summer camp. As gladiators in the Colosseum, this team fights like Romans.

Overcoming obstacles and performing at this championship is a major accomplishment. With graduation and retention creating a Chaotic situation, this team reorganized and came back stronger. With a vice on the robot, this team is looking to defend its way to success with simplicity and reliability.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Growing like a school of fish, this team’s feeder program of FLL and FTC impressed the judges. Hosting a summer camp that serves double duty of engaging kids in STEAM as well as raising money for the program, their focus on the future extends beyond the reef. This team has STEM - Ascended to the highest level.
Two reasons the judges love this team are their enthusiasm and their passion Too many cheers to count, and almost too much joy. Cheering for everyone, these cats in stripes roar the loudest.
This team’s robot is a lean mean coral machine. Their optimized claw rises to wash away the competition. It’s no surprise their building process led to a robot with the beauty of a daisy.

This team’s focus this year was sharing their expertise. They attended events at which they weren’t competing to save some guppies from the sharks. With immense Gracious Professionalism, these sea Horses rode to the rescue.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This high scoring team has been anything but blue on this championship weekend. Consistently rising to the highest levels in short order has become one of its trademarks. These dawgs aren’t chasing any flying squirrels – they’re running with the belt-a-vator.

Every detail from wiring to construction shows this team’s dedication to craftsmanship and performance. This team’s design process blew the judges away with how “black and white” it was. Just don’t ask them or their “power – doinker” what time it is.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team’s control system swims untouched in the water. Their custom swerve library grips the carpet and pirouettes effortlessly around the reef. This bot’s performance on the field simply can’t be Sabotaged.
This team’s robot trains night and day. It uses its autonomous nervous system to navigate like a shark. It swims side to side to keep its eyes on the prize.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team isn’t fishing for compliments, but the judges noticed them anyway. With a themed pit area and robot, they wowed the judges. In yellow and blue, this team might be Beta, but their image is Alpha!

El equipo brinda asistencia financiera a una amplia cantidad de equipos, han impartido conferencias y workshops a diferentes grupos, tienen proyectos consolidados y sostenibles que han perdurado a través del tiempo. El equipo tiene la creencia que el STEM es para todos por lo que su recorrido durante los últimos tres años ha sido de crecimiento, resiliencia y un compromiso inquebrantable para hacer que la ciencia y la tecnología sean accesibles para todos.
