This team has outreach programs at their local elementary and middle schools. They have nearly doubled in size since last season while driving inclusion for all. With a focus in fundraising, they’re going to fly like a bird into funding next season’s build.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team salvages, reuses, and recycles to help build their pit and shop. In addition, their community and outreach efforts create a plan for new recruits on their team. Their sustainability efforts and team structure now provide a place they can call home.
Imagine a team that embrace all students whether incoming freshmen or exiting seniors. They even collaborate with the performing arts clubs in their school. This team’s energy and excitement… ROCKS!

This team took an old school approach to a coral conundrum. What goes up must also rotate forward. Their ingenious lifter linkage system is powered by just one motor and lifts more than just expectations!

The judges are always trying to keep an eye out for those teams that are quietly bringing others up. They may not have been flying over the reef as they anticipated but they have been cruising through the pits lending aid despite their own struggles. While they are not shorebirds, these Falcons should fly with their heads high leaving today.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This small team was able to impress the judges with a unique design feature. It always tries to keep its eyes fixed on the reef. Rub-a-dub-dub - This team’s components are in a welded tub.
This wrench wrecking, motor modding, belt boosted team sets a new standard for robustness. TRIPLE NICKELS is cashing in the coral. Watch out for this team’s flying squirrel!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: The judges are always impressed by teams' abilities to come up with innovative solutions to challenges. Mariners depend on lights to navigate crowded seas to stay on course. This team's lights never lie but their pants are on fire.

This team circles the reef twice with their alliance family. They consistently reach high and prove they’re FIRST when it comes to their autonomous. Whether on red or blue, they move so fast they turn PURPLE.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team had a great seascape. They worked as hard as a rock… lobster. Come into this team’s shanty and see if you can find their… One fish, two fish, red fish, blue fish… BETA FISH.

The structure implemented by this team ensures that all of its members are meaningfully engaged. From maintaining and expanding a pipeline through outreach, to local and international community service, this team looks to share its resources wisely. The judges found it fitting that this event started on March 14, or as this team might prefer to call it: Pi-day.

Sharing their expertise with the young and old alike, this team is no adversary to putting in the work. A host of good ideas with excellent follow through. Definitely engineered to inspire, they're not your rival they're your friendly NEMESIS.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This Team of warriors planned a strong offense, able to score almost anywhere with only one tool. A gorgeous robot from top to bottom, the judges were most impressed that, like a shield and spear phalanx, their dual-purpose coral/algae mechanism could handle any situation.

When faced with an open fracture, time is off the essence. This team grabs what's class at hand to Macgyver a solution. Sometime sawdust, glue, and gauze is all it takes. The judge's award for Robot FIRST-Aid goes to team 8714.
Bear in mind, starting a new team is hard. But like grizzled veterans, this team is already working on BUILDING a better future.
Inspired by Neptune's trident, this team floats to the top. COVID crashed upon them and washed out their foundation But with positive cheer they announce their full return .

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Speaking of hooks, sustainability is the name of the game. Keeping supply costs down, makes the budget go further. That's why the judges are ABUZZ about this SWARM'S creative recycling and upcycling.

If you are looking for motivation look to the SEA and the STARS With their GIRL SCOUT outreach and energy in the stands, their enthusiasm is contagious. Like an OCTOPUS they embraced the spirit of FIRST
This team funneled their strengths through precision and teamwork, Adept on land and now on the sea, They saddled their horses and climbed to new heights.

Another team's swerve wasn't swerving and they BARKED for help. This Team JUMPED to help by providing a complete software upgrade. Their CHARACTER of gracious professionalism enabled their competitor to get back in the game.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.teamName: Titans of Tech - Thrive Charter School
records.script: This team CHARTER-ed their way to newer heights. They truly FLIPPED the lid on scoring through multiple methods. These TITANS will soon reach their Olympus.

The stress of competition can put a robot through the ringer. Rogue game pieces, bent parts, and clicking gears come with the terratory. This team bends but does not break under the heat of competition.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team recognized that they would need to race around quickly but aim precisely. Like Valkyries, they brought the speed and precision strikes. Their S L O W M O - M O D E let this team score with the accuracy of Odin's lighting.
Lighting up the fields with slick LEDS This team glides EFFORTLESSLY between waypoints Like clockwork, this team strikes at MIDNIGHT

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Sharp lines and bold colors keep this team connected. By ensuring consistency between their robot, pit, and shirts, this team STICKS together, When you look at them, they are clearly GEARED for success.

Whether it's mentoring FLL teams or hosting library events, this team has dedicated their time to spreading the message of STEM to students of all ages. Teaching the values of FIRST, these scholars make a great alliance partner, both on and off the field. Their community outreach spans across the globe, even going as far as the stars. These cool cats are keeping healthy minds on more than just the game.

This “small but mighty” family’s inspiration - far exceeds its size. By training the next generation of leaders and supporting FLL teams, they truly embody the mission of FIRST. Their outreach extends all the way to scouting, where they offer both support and an innovative app, keeping the gears of progress turning.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team’s robot demonstrated a robust, functional and elegant design. They effectively scrubbed the reef of algae to grow coral. When Captain Jack Sparrow needs a dependable robot for his forays, this is the team he turns to.

The Judges were impressed with this team's resiliency, perseverance and ingenuity leading up to and during this competition. We were intrigued by the various design elements of this team's robot and its ability to clearly explain the details behind it's choices None more than it's quickly manufacturing a set of custom replacement gears in-house with no time to obtain them commercially. The judges award for MANUFACTURING ON THE FLY, Team number 1626 Falcon Robotics

This newbie team spread their wings and learned to fly. They crafted a basketball shooter during the preseason, putting their building skills to the test. This red rookie team is ready to leave the nest!
Like building blocks for their team, they united as a family. As the walls came down, this team soared to new "heights." They took a serious "byte" out of the competition.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team does not just recycle their components; they also recycle their knowledge. Through working with full and part time students, they incorporate all the "tools of the trade". Turning up the heat, this "devilish team" forged their future.

This orange team left a lasting impression on the judges. Through their dedication to enhancing team involvement and fostering inclusivity, they've sparked team spirit both in the pits and in the stands. This is THE Tiger team.

This robot has the competition asking, "Whose robot is that?" Through their transverse approach they elevated their performance. Using a left-handed sonic screwdriver, they made more room on the inside than the outside.

All weekend this team has been praised by their peers for helping throughout the competition. This team will "fight" through the crowd to get what you need. They are the true warriors of gracious professionalism.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: While many teams specialize in a single focus, this team embraced flexibility, seamlessly switching between defense and algae processing. Their versatile components let them adapt on the fly, making them a formidable force. Like the striking orange and black stripes of a tiger, they can showcase two distinct configurations during a match.

The Judges appreciated the exceptional integration of systems and packaging within this team's robot Multiple prototypes in various materials guided them to a design that excels in meeting Reefscape's many challenges. From the Barge to the Reef and back this team is scoring from the opening bell until the final buzzer.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Innovative control systems blend inputs from humans and machines to guide performance. This robot’s flashy sensors and navigation work together to guide their drive team to score. With their LED turn signals you can be sure this team is staying on point.

This team can see across the seven seas. Through implementation of vision and sensors, their self-trained AI can pick up elements on the field. Racing around with their scarlet banner, these robot raiders sure is smart.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team hand crafted their identity. From the ocean to the stars, their creativity knows no bounds. These astronauts are the pirates of space.

This team looked for a way to be sustainable and to give back to their community. They turned summer camps into FLL grants for Title 1 districts and share their success with underserved communities around the globe following a hierarchy of needs. They created a manual on how to address basic needs as a the first step in a pathway to building STEM initiatives to ASCEND to our top award.

With a special emphasis on women in STEAM, this team is building a pipeline of future engineers brick by brick. Other teams are green with envy about this team's recycling program. This RED team is one to watch.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team has an instinct for success. They have a nose for tracking, fetching, and retrieving algae. This team's focus is like a dog chasing after a squirrel.

These stranded sailors showed dedication and resolve. From bleaching the coral to scavenging the beach for driftwood, they are inspiring for their resourcefulness. The judges wood love to recognize this team for the robot that could.
This school club is setting sail. They swerved their robot into the currents of this competition. We are on the lookout for this legion as they embark on this great adventure.
This team is always looking closely for new ways to improve. A strong business plan is going to take this team around the world. The judges spied something good rising in this team.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team participated in local festivals and interacted with kids to start their pipeline early. They created more leadership positions to develop their skills on and off the field. This team is a force to be reckoned with.
For this team the fun of the competition is everything. Their philosophy creates a robust broth that keeps their team afloat. Our judges are nourished by the chowder of their spirit.

This team separated and reformed like a starfish to tackle each component. Their constant alignment kept the school swimming in the same direction. This team showed who's in charge of the design process.

This team impressed the judges with the creative use of their resources. They went above and beyond to help the teams in their area in the pre-season. Their mascot may be good at hiding, but to the judges they really stand out.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team really leaned into this year's game extending out of the water and a little to the side. Black and white like an orca, but red all over. Team 1807 RedBird Robotics
With such a complex game, this team prioritized doing one thing well. Their robot dove into the coral with a robust effector. They dug their talons in and produced a quality machine.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: With a focus on the relationship between robot speed, turning radius and traction limits. This team destroyed the field by reducing skid. [SING] "Listen all y'all, it's a Sab-BOT-age."
Backwards and Forward, this team followed the April tags. A talon-t for flawless execution always flies them to the top. They put another feather in their cap with reliable coral placement.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team really drew the judges' eyes. They made their pit fun and functional. They had the judges hopping for joy.

This team teaches us how to continually evolve through their strong community engagement and unwavering commitment to sustainability. From linguistic translations to hosting robotics event, this team’s members actively learn about compassion, empathy, and care for others in need. Their RoboCon spirit inspires and shines through their flagship red.

This team has gone above and beyond spreading FIRST values and STEM work not only in their school but also beyond. This team is not only an inspiration for the FIRST community but has reached across the globe with their outreach. They might have completed a full circle with their organizational skills but they still consider themselves a piece of the pie.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team ramped up on design features for their robot. Their multi-functional LED array let them when know it was time to play. The GODS would be happy with their Spartan design.

The judges recognized that collaboration between teams is enough as core value within the FIRST universe. This team takes that concept to extremes by sharing knowledge and resources with multiple area programs daily in an effort to raise the floor within its Robotics family. These big cats lead by example helping their pride to succeed in this ‘water game’.

Through huge challenges this rookie team is starting to see the whole picture. They have shown excellent resilience in keeping their robot going through the competition. Stop by the robot and get a big high five.
This team faced great adversity. Although established, they started from scratch. This team charged back to the top.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team takes the FIRST-class approach to train and build a strong team. They impressed the judges by making the impact in their school and community. This tea-green team cleans up where ever they go.

This team brought enthusiasm and optimism to the competition. This small team’s positive attitude caused a near-doubling in their team size this past year. They may not have many members but this team is as loyal to each other as a pack of dogs and their growth is an unstoppable as a charging bull. Congratulation the Bulldogs.
This team’s dead band is very much alive. They fly around the pits like a swarm of yellow jackets. They do their best to minimize any sabotage to other teams.

This team’s outgoing and friendly behavior colorfully pops out of the crowd. They showed support to alliance members through wins and losses and respect to opponents and volunteers. You may even see their drive team playing mini games across the field before the match.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: The judges have been impressed with this team’s design process and ingenuity as they rise to meet the Reefscape challenges. In a field of teams with enough animal nicknames to fill a zoo this team does not struggle to find an optimized path. These Dawgs succeeded chasing Flying Squirrels.

When it comes to machine quality, this team passes all “tests”. It’s no “puzzle” that they exemplify craftmanship. No need for them to go back to the “lab” because they are ready to go head to head with the best.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: The judges were impressed by this team’s ability to automate everything they do. Aligning and pathing this robot completes every task they want to undertake. These birds really ‘soared’ past our expectations with their well-designed app.

This team excels in the rapidly advancing autonomous field hitting highs scores through out the games. Their engineering expertise is complemented by their bright reef theme that adorns their robot, pit, and apparel. These Sisters make FIRST reign supreme.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team screams Art! Art! Art! Every student gets to express their stripes. Their multiple button designs and bright patterns make these cats stand out from the rest of the pack.
Changing the way things are done in Taiwan, building a new system of outreach and making the future happen now - their name may include "zero" but their impact is from "little hands" to "Big AI".

Some teams build robots, but this team builds a legacy. With a mission to inspire and lead, they have transformed STEM Education into a movement that reaches beyond the competition field. Their impact isn’t just measured in matches won but in the students they’ve empowered and the futures they’ve shaped. Driven teams have the potential to leave a lasting impression on their communities, and this team exemplifies that spirit.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This award goes to a team whose robot showcases an outstanding integrated design with mostly custom-made parts that work seamlessly together. The result is a machine that balances functionality and elegance - much like how a spider weaves its web.

This team has consistently gone above and beyond, creating opportunities for students from all walks of life, empowering the next generation of engineers, and leading by example in promoting the values of FIRST. Their passion extends far beyond their own achievements; it ignites the future. “Passionate individuals can drive progress to the world” and this teams proves it.
They have strong partnerships and inspire students through all of FIRST. They designed all the players into a set of baseball cards to clench victory.
When you hear a bear roaring, run..... Because you know they are coming back very strong!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has laid a solid foundation for long-term success by fostering strong leadership and cultivating lasting partnerships. By continuously evolving and sharing resources with others, they ensure their own longevity while also contributing to the growth and vitality of the FIRST community as a whole. This team’s efforts exemplify sustainability in every sense and will continue to inspire for years to come.

This team demonstrates a strong spirit of collaboration and unity. Each member contributes their expertise to support the team's growth. Their cooperative efforts make a lasting impact on the broader robotics community.

When challenges rose like crashing waves, this team plunged in without hesitation. Armed with sharp minds and rock-solid logic, they turned problems into possibilities and concepts into reality with bold ideas, smart designs, and flawless execution. They are the captains of creativity, steering straight toward excellence.
This team actively shares their knowledge and experience through workshops and online. Their rural school outreach plays a key role in establishing new teams everywhere.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team has impressed the judges with their creative and effective designs as an integrated scoring machine. With their corner mount position sensors, side mount grabbing climber, and one-inch water jet chassis, it all makes for good and stable performance.

Their robot operates very flexibly and stably, consistently achieving competition points. The overall motion control demonstrates a high level of quality. The team has advanced design for quick replacement. And like a deer, they move quietly.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: The winning team wrapped its wing-gilded, dual-metered Beta Bot in the world's longest belt to elevate their success.
This team has excellent algorithms to support it. We found them to be very fast and accurate. Well played.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.teamName: Our Lady of Providence Dream League
records.script: This team emblem combines every key component and integrates the robot. Their symbol demonstrates the rise from the dilemma, and this team has amazed us with their performance in engineering.

This veterans team addresses all aspects of the FIRST mission with passion, determination and perseverance while preserving their culture and inspiring youth locally and abroad. Through tireless intercontinental connections, there was an historic moment: a successful team was born! In addition to this incredible accomplishment, they also reached over 5,000 students locally; maybe you saw this team reading their book to another 42 kids yesterday!

Facing the challenges of this season could make a team go red in the face, but this team chose to go above and beyond by creating a quality robot and inspiring the next generation to pursue STEM. When you see what this team is about, you'll know it's hip to be SQUARE. The winner of the Engineering Inspiration Award is team 2429, The Blockheads.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Whether they are taking down the bad guys or flying off to space, it's important to pair up with a friend like this. This team has earned their technical prowess through blood, sweat, and tears. Be sure to hit the road running to see this robot's namesake in the latest Marvel movie this summer! The Industrial Design Award goes to Team 7426, Pair of Dice.

This team slithered through the dust and the competition. They rattled their robot and the other teams through their high trajectory shots. For their tenacity, the judges award goes to team 10368, the Robo Rattlers.

This rookie team looks like, sounds like, and acts like a team that's been a-roaring for ages. They have learned the ropes and fidgeted with their toys, I mean tools. Let's hope they ARC strong and re-mane excited about their FRC Future.

For a team whose aspirations are on the rise, these all-stars have readily met the challenges of global competition. They brought energy, enthusiasm, and a level of zen that transcends geographical boundaries. This Rising All Star Award goes to Team 9498 Zenshin Robotics.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: The winner of the Team Sustainability Award really sinks their teeth into energy-saving projects and community education to benefit the environment. This team's activities keep their community in the pink. The winner of the Team Sustainability Award is Team 597 - Wolverines.

This team travelled far and wide to celebrate FIRST. They do not fake their enthusiasm or spirit in Vegas. Their presence is shown throughout social media. The team forges their own path with their ferocious spirit. If you haven't gotten a map cookie, stop by the booth for 4421, FORGE Robotics.

This team has tackled valleys and mountains, throughout the season. Who knew coral could bite! This team iterated and designed custom parts using both simple engineering solutions and next generation innovation with dual arm use and ground pick up capabilities. They might not be from Florida, but these Gators have excelled in the swamp of this competition.

records.teamName: Kingman FIRST Robotics Team 60 (The Bionic Bulldogs)
records.script: We heard it through the volunteers that this team recognized their contribution with cards and gifts. A true example of coopertition, this team spread their light throughout the event. Bringing the friendly warmth of Kingman, Arizona to this regional competition, we recognize the Bionic Bulldogs as the Gracious Professionalism award winner.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: It’s annoying when that algae gets in the way of coral reef building. Rather than grab handfuls of that gooey stuff as a separate action, this team clears the reef WHILE placing coral pieces. They kick the algae to the curb, with shoe parts, without using any additional motors. The Creativity Award goes to 1388 Eagle Robotics.

We would like to celebrate this powerful and rigorous machine. This robot is a model of meticulous craftsmanship and character which persevered through the challenging elements of the playing field. Hailing from the northern land of bi-lingual power, Tech For Kids showed us the definition of quality and workmanship throughout the competition.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: The design of this team's control system really holds water. Their robot's ability to differentiate between coral and algae using sensors puts their robot at the highest levels. The winner of the Innovation in Control Award goes to team 4414 High Tide.

This team's autonomous mode consistently crested the high levels of the reef. Due to their expertly crafted programming, they did not have to gamble when rolling over the competition. The winner of the autonomous award is Team 987, the High Rollers.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: The team's theme scaled new heights while also embracing FIRST Core Values. They definitely took the "high" road while epitomizing a "mellow" mentality. The imagery award goes to Team 3009, the High Scalers.

This is the true meaning of a team with members who have varied interests coming together to aim high toward a common goal. Over the past 3 years, this team has created a revival of the FIRST mission in their community, roaring with determination and strength. They embody the FIRST core values through their unified efforts, leading with the power and unity of a lion’s pride. Give a loud roar for the RoboLions of team 564!

These wild mustangs raced to other but did not fall. By hosting, mentoring and assisting they Fastracked STEM for all They had days of discovery and Robotics that RISE And even taught Girls Scouts to keep their eye on the prize. Congratulations to team 6806 the Wild Reds from Mineola

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Our winner for this award generated an elegant robot that performs. Attacking multiple gameplay elements with a clean design, their machine has chops on the field and looks the part. Even through their industrial design, this team exhibits respect, integrity, compassion, and equity. Congratulations to team 870, Team R.I.C.E.!

This young team changes STEM to STEAM. Their legacy of volunteerism thru education grows FIRST and STEAM throughout their sphere. This super team authored their way to this JUDGES award. Congratulations, Team 9016, Syosset Supersonics!

This nine-person rookie team overcame numerous challenges to establish their school’s first FRC team. Their unwavering “can do” attitude drove them to do everything in their power to earn a spot at this championship. Along the way, they formed a bond so tight, they became a second family overnight.

This team swims through the water to find new members Cleaning beaches and flipping pancakes to rise as one Their nets mau have lost 20 seniors, But working with a neighboring school SPEARED new members!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Using various methods, this team successfully reduced its carbon footprint. Their work with the Atlantic Marine Conservancy Society cleared 750 pounds of trash from local beaches. The training of their members, SWAT, data analytics and AI data is used to improve this team. The data is stored to sustain the team into the future. The winner of the Team Sustainability Award, in the sophisticated black blazers, is the POBOTS.
This team is loud and proud. From the stands, the judges could hear them as they cheered for the team and alliances as their matches progressed. Watch them soar, here come the Soaring Colts.

Their overly expensive late night pizza parties fueled their passion for engineering their robot. Inspired from 3-D printing, they designed a flawless slide mechanism. Design process was so well thought and engineered. Patrick will be so proud! Congratulations to Team Spongebot Square Drive! You absolutely exceled in engineering.

The winning team didn’t just focus on their own robot — they went above and beyond. They shared equipment with other teams, giving new meaning to ‘teamwork makes the dream work.’ When another team needed help, they were right there lending a hand in building their robot. They also host a round table, bringing people together to share ideas and collaborate. And let’s not forget about the annual Rampage. For all their contributions, collaboration, and spirit, this year’s award goes to 2869, The Regal Eagles!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team had no issue picking up coral in a rough surf Even though they may use one, their robot is by no means ratchet. They had a creative approach reinventing the gear

The dedication to excellence and meticulous craftsmanship truly shines through in your robot, The quality of your build is evident in its consistent and reliable performance throughout the competition. This is not just a robot; it is a showcase of thoughtful engineering and superior construction. The evolution of your design transformed the robot from a mere “magicarp” into a true Gyarados. Coupled with the evident strength and reliability of your creation, it tickled the judges magenta and green with envy. Congratulations to team 287 on winning the quality award.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team showed a “breadth” of controls knowledge, and impressed with its “Autoscore” mode. We didn’t need a “Cyberscout” to select this team for the Innovation in Control award. Congratulations to Team 2872, Cybercats.

This robot combines the simple with the complex. The user interface is rough-hewn but it controls very sophisticated code. The result is a high-scoring, consistent performance, for a low rider. Although Colin Firth is not a team mentor, The Kingsmen of Team 5736 are world class!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team is very bright—and their pit and robot are, too! Their color isn’t shy. It represents strength, commitment, and bravery. From their banners to their shirts to their flyers—everything’s coming up ORANGE! The Imagery Award goes to Team 6024—FACTOR, from Pan, India.

This team turns obstacles into opportunities and is roaring forward with a message: STEM is for everyone With a 2:1 female-to-male ratio and a mission to #makeSTEMviral, they’ve distributed 275 STEM kits across Mexico, Ecuador, and Canada to spread STEM globally with measurable impact and the creation of new FIRST teams. They also have ongoing advocacy with 10 state senators for increased STEM funding and supported 101 teams through their RTESS initiative an efforts have been recognized through heartfelt letters from fellow FRC teams, libraries, their school and local organizations grateful for their mentorship and STEM initiatives. For transforming access into action and leading a movement that proves STEM is for everyone — the FIRST Impact Award goes to Team 1796, the RoboTigers from Queens, New York!

This team inspires the judges with their commitment to volunteering and mentoring. Acting like a big family, they reach a large breadth of underserved communities. In addition to building robots and making waves, they are getting middle schoolers involved in STEM by making wheels to race

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: The industrial design award sponsored by General Motors celebrates the team that demonstrates industrial design principles striking a balance between form function and aesthetics. This multifaceted robot sparked our judges interest as they juggled both algae and coral with ease. With custom wheels to coast across the field and interactive lights to guide the way, this team’s bot set them up for a weekend of truly electric game play.
COVID hit this team hard, and they took that personally They picked the coral and themselves up off the floor They’ve come back strong, congratulations team 334!

This team impressed the judges with the tenacity with which they formed their team. Undaunted by lack of initial support, they found sponsors and continued on, attracting many students from the their school to form their team. We have no doubt they will quickly rise out of the basement.

This very young team spends a lot of time doing amazing outreach in their own community. Despite numerous challenges, such as getting sponsors, getting space to practice and getting initial support, they held their own at this competition. Outreach aside, this alliance captain also did an amazing job reassembling their robot from their suitcases and rising to the top of the competition.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Sustainability Award TEAM 3204 – Steampunk Penguins This team transforms every year, mentoring each other to cultivate an excellent team of women. They fund their team by turning trash into treasure they can sell to their classmates. In addition, they also use their inventions to improve their community and environment. Clear some space on your “windowsill of failure” for this award shows you can learn equally from your mistakes and achievements. Congratulations, Team Number 3204

This team spirit is flying high, displaying strong enthusiasm and cohesiveness within their team. Meanwhile, they haven’t forgotten to have fun. They don’t want to be a chicken and they don’t want to be a duck.

This team demonstrated strong engineering practices by creating their own testing framework which included unit, system and simulation tests which ensured reliability. They documented all aspects of their work product allowing them to share with other teams to help them improve their engineering practices as well. Their quick iteration time makes it seem like they have EIGHT ARMS.

TEAM 806 – BROOKLYN BLACKSMITH They’re got FIRST down to core sportsmanship Helping others make it in the door with off-season contributions galore. Assigning tasks and doing much more with B.L.E.S.S – the Blacksmith Emergency Support Squad. GRACIOUS PROFESSIONALISM

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team has a creative method they use to figure out how to line up and deposit coral. Who knew using a simple piece of plexiglass could be so effective? With an 80% success rate for depositing coral, the creativity award goes to team 6873, The Generals.

This team impressed the judges with their meticulous documentation, every design iteration and decision was thoughtfully recorded in their engineering notebook. Their robot featured a consistent, well-thought-out aesthetic everywhere, from the robot all the way to their cookies! They designed a strong, stable robot with the ability to do all levels of coral & shoot algae, showing a deep understanding of both form and function.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team has created and makes use of innovative software to record it’s progress during match play. It is able to then review the actual game play and compare intent to reality. Hopefully they continue to replay their success for years to come.

This team’s intelligent design defines their approach to autonomous control, as well as everything else they do. Their robust systems carry the same rhythmic pulse from auto to tele-op You can’t miss this fiery team in red, congratulations to StuyPulse team 694.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: From dusk to dawn – starting anew with impactful imagination Look beyond the horizon their machine can be seen Leading the way with fun & creativity

records.teamName: The Giant Diencephalic BrainSTEM Robotics Team
records.script: Some teams make local impacts; some teams reach globally. Some teams support FLL or FTC growth, while others focus on community involvement. These are all admirable and applauded endeavors. This incredible team hosts FLL competitions, brings joy to hospitals with STEAM kits, and embraces a border-free approach to education. Students teaching students fosters a culture of mentorship and growth, supporting seamless transitioning from FLL to FTC to FRC. A team that achieves this and more must have a huge team! However, the judges were blown away by this 3rd-year team of just 18 members. It is clear that their brainstem of operations is strong and well-connected! Please join me in congratulating Team 8393, The Giant Diencephalic BrainSTEM Robotics Team, the winners of the FIRST Impact Award!

After a long day of attending classes or working on the robot, these students will feed you. This team has touched all aspects of first including creating courses in their school and online. You can spot this team walking around the competition with their matching letterman jackets.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: If performance is an indication of fit, form and function, then this team exemplifies industrial design. From autonomous efficiency to multiple design groups bringing subsystems together beautifully and hidden wiring in powder coated structures, a terrific robot surfaced. This GRRReat team emerged as an industrial design leader.

The Cindy Lou Hoo Award: This teams unique outreach helped spread Christmas cheer by making their towns displays just that much more animated. Their excitement for their community made everyones hearts grow 3 sizes. Dr Seuss would be proud
They may be new but by connecting with the FIRST community they grew. They continue to use their expertise to rise and become a jewel.
This multi-national team persevered through murky waters with team members in distant locations. They learned to float and swim to become the rising all stars Just keep swimming!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Sustaining the theme with effective training and complete online docs is just what they do. Helping all teams recycle supports environmental sustainability too. They roar into the future. They are team 2228, Cougar Tech

This team can be heard cheering from the mountains and the valleys. They are a tight knit group whose enthusiasm can be felt with a rumble. If you try to split this yoke, you just might get the horns.
Platform design enables flexibility and other features. Early competition in an arena drives excellence. When resources are scarce, developing with fellow Gladiators is a strategy for success.

Respect for others is a hallmark of this team, with an impact across their state. They welcome and promote those in underserved communities and work to make STEM accessible to everyone. This team takes off from the mountains and shoots for MARS!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Sometimes the simplest ideas are elegant, inexpensive and solve hard problems. Wonderful things manage wires in multiple machines, but only one can also walk down stairs. Can you hear the slinky over the Thunder?
To avoid toppling over, physics is key. Well designed geometry results in a clean and elegant arm and keeps their circuitry flying through the water.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: When it comes to this team, repulsive vectors turn math into attractive forces to pull coral to the reef. Using simulation to test & refine their motion planning process, they optimized the path from acquisition of coral to the reef branch. This team from the beach was in control. Congratulation Team 695 Bison Robotics.
Their autonomous lit up the field. It was easy as 1,2,3. Their vision kept them in Range!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This year's game and their theme are both underwater. But their messages and kindness made them rise above. They cast a spell that locked us in. They are team 1507, the Warlocks.

Drawing on a wealth of talent from many schools, this team comes together to attack with one mission. Focusing on strong advocacy and community engagement, they make an impact throughout the land. Libraries are their stronghold as part of the battle to inspire future STEM leaders. From robots to rockets, their summer bootcamp is taking off with great momentum.

Soaring to new heights, this team fosters and inspires future generations of FIRST participants, ensuring that STEM opportunities take flight. Whether in their local community or reaching across borders, they lead initiatives that help grow and transform STEM education for all. Spreading their wings, they swoop into action with impactful missions, uplifting underrepresented teams and advocating for a future where robotics has no limits.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team transformed complex game piece handling capability into an elegant and efficient solution. They designed a V claw mechanism that grips like a hawk. This team’s coral scoring was a slam dunk, helping them sail through matches.

This team excels in select major initiatives with nearly countless examples of outreach and progress. They make technology accessible to all ages, as well as tackling hunger in their community and helping the environment. This team is so, so, talented, they definitely earned their letter jackets.

This rookie team loves mentoring in their community and at school. They introduce engineering through effective outreach and inspiring students to “play” soccer. This team keeps their eye on the horizon as they inspire future FIRST friends.
If we look into a crystal ball we see only great things. This team is setting themselves up for success on and off the field. Watch out future, this team is on a roll.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team identified needs both internally and in their community at large. They achieved legendary recruitment metrics, appealing to inclusivity with non-technical roles. They also established multifaceted sustainability practices from across the pond.

This young team is busy empowering kids in Westchester. Setting an example worth following, FIRST is ready to bottle the enthusiasm and buzz about the exceptional camaraderie of this bionic team. In the name of spirit and with recognition of this exceptional team, it’s time to light up the stage and welcome these electric bees:

Hailing from islands, this team’s knowledge of prototyping and design showed superb skill. Navigating turbulent waters, they charted simulations to anchor robust defensive strategies for their robot. This community of students inspires new trends in practical and functional design.

This team made STEM viral in three countries and 5 boroughs. Making STEM accessible, 2000 bags, and counting was the name of the game. Rocking a two to one ratio for female leadership, every member of this Queens-bound team engenders the BOAR spirit. Sparking hope and equity, these humble cubs have now earned the respect of our FIRST Kingdom; behold the gracious professionalism of our fearsome tigers!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Coming from the Big Apple, and aptly dressed in red, you can’t miss this team or their unique robot. This robot scores in each sector, in any direction, and is a unique all-round competitor. They have creativity pulse-ing in their veins.
FRC was truly a blast, showcasing bots built to last. To ensure this team wasn’t reckless, they followed their checklists. System status checks were their secret weapon.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: O buoy! This team knows how to navigate the waves of competition with ease. Their innovative button box control made waves, delivering coral with precision and clearing algae from the waters. When navigating the high seas of competition, this maroon-clad crew pressed all the right buttons.

This team didn’t leave its robot adrift as it autonomously cut through the competition. Their tracking capabilities ensure their robot is never marooned on the field They sat back like Kings as their robot racked up the score.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Wherever you looked, you saw this team’s bright electric colors. Their quirky mascot was everywhere – from their pit to their shirts to the sides of their bot – and of course in the stands cheering them on! This animated team was charged up!

This team explores the depths of the ocean, growing new STEM ecosystems around the world. Like building a man made reef, they established engineering and science curricula, stimulating the growth of STEM and FIRST. From the waters of New York, this team dove into the reefs of South America and India, launching summer camps, providing STEM education programs, and founding FLL teams.

With a focus on simplicity and education, this team shares STEM and FIRST with others, storing those memories for the future. This team excelled in outreach to their community, elementary schools, other states, and internationally. Let's all celebrate the titanic achievements of this unsinkable team's world-wise inspiration.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team's bold red logo symbolizes their fierce drive and determination. Their cutting edge proto-bot designs and their teamwork enable their excellence in industrial design. A bright spot in the Flower City, they're "all good."

Like a tidal wave crashing down, this team's impact can be felt far and wide. The limitless scope of their programs set their students up for success in their local and global FIRST communities. Discovering and sharing the treasures of STEM, they are charging ahead with mechanical prowess.
These rookies know how to cache coral. This team exemplifies how to positively reinforce their robotics learning. They mesmerized us in their first competition to become this year's Rookie All-Star.

With grit, innovation, and unstoppable spirit, this team stormed onto the scene as a true Rising All-Star. They engineered a reef-rocking scouting app to revolutionize their alliance strategy with data-driven decisions. Despite a sudden sea change, this team designed a coral- and algae-swirling robot in just two weeks.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team established a sustainable organization by building robots and deep connections with schools and the community. They developed a strong, continuous funding source while helping students with tech problems, recruiting, and training new members. Let's all step up to the tech window and recognize them for their more-than-tangential cohesive spirit.

This crew exemplifies spirit as a unified team in appearance, partnerships, and commitment to community. Their excitement radiates as they make stem kits for others, share their practice field, and support FLL teams. Their Sparketing Spirit keeps the pirate ship steering through canal days and ice cream socials.
This team uses a professional design to align with the reef. Get the robot close enough and the scanner slides to the right spot. They ARRGH our neighbors to the north.

This team makes a continuous and deep impact by sharing their resources. They exemplify the definition of Gracious Professionalism by supporting FIRST throughout the Capital Region. Their local partners are grateful to the hosts of Robot Rumble.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team tightened the belt to securely grab game pieces. They truly split themselves apart from the competition. Their dual function gripper was SO unique.
Their top-performing robot is an engineering marvel. They expertly crafted a robot that seemed to function without wires. The tiger is victorious when it comes to quality.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This energetic team from the north of the border must be fans of "Drive to Survive". Their custom software and display set up in the pits would fit right in on race day. Through their custom scouting application, python-based vision system, and C++ mastery, this team displayed a robust and dynamic control system.
This team's robot restores our underwater habitat without a dive team. Not only did they seed coral, they also harvested algae onto the barge. This team is a titan from up north.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: While everyone else is feeling blue, this team is hard to miss on the field and in the stands. Their blazing sign and bright color clearly mark their spaces. They avoid French police Detective Inspector Clouseau and are pretty in pink.

This team is a leader in national and regional advocacy and has had international impact on the FIRST community. The judges were impressed by their sustained impact on the FIRST pipeline, FIRST global, working with young people with cognitive disabilities, local poverty relief, STEM literacy and their continued effort with rookie teams. Their NEIGHBORHOOD outreach really ROCKED the SOCKS off the judges. It may be raining outside, but the THUNDER is really ROLLING in here!

Distance is not a limitation for this team reaching others. Travelling great distances in pursuit of community outreach, this team set up computer labs and STEM curriculum to underdeveloped villages as well as supporting FLL and FTC teams. Their mall recruiting, national TV spots, and active engagement with government officials is not a MIRAGE. They are that exceptional!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Some robots follow the rules and then there’s this one, writing its own code of excellence. With a form that’s fierce, a function that’s flawless, and an aesthetic that’s just plain RANGEROUS, this team proved that beauty & brains can come in the same aluminum-clad package. So, for coding excellence, precision design, and style that screams, “Don’t RANGER on our parade”

Everything this team does has a POINT. Their involvement within their community is MYTHICAL as the FIGHT for equal access to STEM in their school, sports arenas, and even across the world. Their robot doesn't just swim under the sea, it also BOOGIES on the dance floor.

While this team is SHORT on mentors, they stand tall as a model rookie team. This dedicated group of underclassmen CHARMED the judges with their enthusiasm for collaboration and their excitement at technical successes. The future is bright as this team chases their very own FIRST Robotics Competition Pot of Gold.

It's no SHOCK that this team stood out for calling out their fellow teams' accomplishments. Their enthusiasm is so apparent, you can see it from space! They are MAGNIFICENTLY building the team's future through mentorship and summer camps.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: The judges found that this team’s approach to sustainability was “CLAW-some”! Not only do they recycle team knowledge and experience for future members using industry standard software tools, they hae also discovered a way to raise funds by recycling bottles for a profit on Super Bowl Sunday! The judges POUNCED on the opportunity to recognize this sustainable and PURR-fessional team!

This year's winner brought an energy so contagious, you could feel it radiating across the venue. Their cheers echoed with pride, and their smiles powered every pit stop like STEAM ENGINES of support. This team's spirit can be summed up in one phrase, <Kay-Low-Kay>.

This team’s engineering process started at kickoff beginning with a matrix of perceived values and difficulties. They chose to be specialized and compact so they wouldn’t be STUNG. Stress-tests and simulations in Fusion360 enabled their final product to, “keep all 4 wheels always on the ground.”

The judges were impressed with the gracious professionalism of several teams, but this one team stood out above the rest. With 78 outreach activities, support for 9 FLL teams, and translating engineering resources into 17 languages, the winner of this award shows a true commitment to gracious professionalism on a global scale! Their welcoming spirit and positive attitude LUBRICATE the gears of this team to keep them RUNNING SMOOTHLY.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team found new ways to stand tall in the crowd. Balancing impressive ROTATION with an expansive reach, each team member explored new depths in their skillset. A SHARP attention to detail kept their wires from getting TIED in a BOW.

This team’s work in and out of the ring culminated in GREAT SUCCESS. Their design was FIRE and their performance HOT, as they HEATED UP the competition this year, placing in the top ten in the qualifying matches. Truly, their DOCUMENTATION and DURABLE DESIGN set the judges’ hearts ABLAZE.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team made a vision control system to prevent motion blur. The developed their own April tag detection system on the FLY. Their impressive object recognition helped them SOAR above the competition.

This team relies on a TABLET to select their autonomous strategy. They use INFINITE OPTIONS for consistent and reliable performance. When the clock starts and the drivers stand still, they are leading the way with their TRIDENT held high!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This year’s winner didn’t just stand out – they LINGERED in the minds of everyone they passed, thanks to a theme that was anything but ordinary. From their sleek pit design to their perfectly coordinated team gear, their aesthetic was bold, unified, and refreshingly unexpected. The judges were floored by their attention to detail, full commitment to theme, and their ability to make black, white, and hot pink a signature statement. So hold your noses – but only to brace for the excitement!

THREE team members got to the POINT and made ONE great presentation FOR this year’s FIRST Impact Award Submission. Facing the destruction of their FIRST ecosystem, they gathered the outside resources and support from the FIRST community to reestablish and sustain their FIRST environment. Their program was so well-ROUNDED that it made the judge’s decision easy as PIE.

This trailblazing team has been forging new paths, spreading the spirit of FIRST through extensive community STEAM events and compassionate outreach. They have helped many reach new frontiers by forming a second team and supporting FLL and FTC teams. Over the past two years, they have played an instrumental role in helping to provide 25,000 meals to surrounding neighborhoods. Truly, this pioneering team is an inspiration to its members and community.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Like many teams, they incorporated strategic and functional goals into their design. This team took it a step further by documenting and categorizing each assembly and part. Even if you’d never seen their robot, you’d be able to build it with their step-by-step instructions that would make LEGO proud.

From the GREEN hills down south, a certain team stands out for their teamwork and compassion When disaster struck, this team took care of their community in a way that greatly impressed the judges. The team serves as an inspiration to us all as they volunteered their time after Hurricane Helene to provide significant support to their entire community.

This team successfully navigated a tough LABRYNTH of losing their lead mentor and over 90% of their members. Their LEGENDARY documentation, recycling plan, and re-use of old parts sets them apart as a role model for others. Their BULL-HEADED, intentional team structure and business plan ensures EXPONENTIAL IMPACT for years to come.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team exemplifies long-term sustainability for their team and the earth. They BANDED together with their environmental club, getting the GREEN LIGHT for a 3D part recycler. To minimize MAYHEM, they pair rookie members with veteran MUPPETS to TAKE CHARGE in the years to come.

The cheers of this team rose above the rest. They bring the heat as they embrace their teammates and others in their community. With flames of red and blue they soared higher than every, igniting the spirit of everyone.
This team FLIES above the competition. They SOAR with elegant engineering processes. The team LAUNCHES rigorous design actions, creating a winning modular PEARL of a robot.

Instead of kicking the CAN down the road, this team helped others fix it! The collaborate during on and off season with other regional teams and invite them to practice at their space. Their impact runs deeper than the game. With their WAVES OF KINDNESS, they help spread Gracious Professionalism through a MESSAGE IN A BOTTLE.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Racing ahead with creative thinking, this team galloped past the competition with a design as clever as it is effective. Their robot’s unique lift system allows it to climb with the precision and control of an elevator. Charging to victory with Elevator Ed, this team has truly risen to the surface.

This energetic team impressed the judges with their meticulous pit checklist and functional checks done with a mock coral reef ahead of each game. Their robust construction and wire routing within the elevator arm ensured error-free operation on the field. This team has an outstanding pit crew that RESTORES the robot after each game.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team helped the Judges understand their vision, which used one camera at a high frame rate. They used a single motor to collect both coral and algae with ease. This mechanism definitively proved their WORTH.

The winner is a “grr”-eat team from the East. They autonomously add three corals to the reef—using advanced vision systems and IR coral sensing. While upholding WILDLIFE CONSERVATION and AVOIDING THE BEACH, they set a high bar for autonomous operation.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s image will outlast most known lifeforms. Their branding CRAWLS through all aspects of their drive station, robot, and team. Their impact is resilient and GLOWING, and they definitely didn't BUG the judges one bit.

This team doesn't tilt at windmills when it comes to their efforts in the community. Even though they can't fly, they RUN across the state while taking teams under their wing, ensuring they do all they can so FIRST rocks year after year.

This team of dedicated professionals ACCELERATES above and beyond the competition to celebrate FIRST core values through their remarkable passion for engineering, at home and abroad. This team engages not only to recruit, but enhance their community through the spirit of engineering to all ages and demographics. The judges are OVER THE MOON about this team that's OUT OF THIS WORLD! 3...2...1...BLAST OFF!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: The judges were impressed with the frequency of this team's cycles. They designed a four-killowatt elevator and a lightning fast climber with spares they never need. This team is more well known for their AMPLITUDE.

In a world where the boundaries between programming, engineering and design blur, fruit and robots coexist in the most extraordinary ways. Present and qualified in many areas with their efforts being casually heroic, this robot and team shone through like a yellow toupee in the darkness. This team is definitely not monkeying around!
They are starting their journey, but are not completely as a fish out of water. These rookies are taking FIRST to ALL the stars!
It ain't about how hard you get hit, it's about how hard you get hit and keep moving forward afterward. Risin' up, back in the arena, they always keep going the distance!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has impacted over 20,000 individuals through their sustainable practices. Known for their green color and motto, this team is also 100% self-funded. Their innovative efforts are driving long-term change for future success.
This team is smooth, and it always shines through. Their eagerness is almost impossible to contain. Their sharpest attribute is their entire team's spirit!
This team met every challenge with future-focused innovation. They turned obstacles in to opportunities, refining every detail. Their professional approach to their design is a glimpse into tomorrow.

When other teams ran into CATastrophic problems, they covertly assisted them by sharing knowledge, tools and parts. They stalked the pits with cat-like strength, courage and a positive attitude to ensure they were able to help everywhere help was needed.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: When this team lost their scoring ability, they had to get creative. This team redesigned and refocused their robot in an effort to stay competitive. This team's magnetism helped them climb to titanic levels.
This team is always ready for the green flag. Their ability to race for answers allowed them to build a consistently functional and robust robot. They finish in first place when it comes to quality.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: While navigating turbulent reefs, this team managed to always stay in control. With their innovative haptic feedback system, they always knew where they were, despite not being in Tiger Country.
When not flying high in a "V", but under the sea, this team's robot can SWIM to any location with autonomous choreography, and the sweet tunes of Taylor Swift to power these mechanical mallards home.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Part of this team is fuzzy, where other parts are clear and bright. Their ordinarily cute imagery is the absolute fiercest!

They are bright, purple, and support FIRST across state lines. This team has started and sustained dozens of teams in recent years, reaching thousands of students annually, through hands-on events and workshops. Their outreach has played a CRITICAL ROLE in spreading the impact of FIRST, FORGING AHEAD of the competition. Congrats team #5454, Obsidian!

The judges heard about this team's support for others in the event coming from far and wide! They started over a dozen teams this year, promoting engineering through large community events, and have sponsored countless FIRST events this season, from FLL to FRC. There's no slowing this team down, they're always on the run! Congrats Team # 8711, Midnight Ostrich Runners!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Their design process, unlike their name, can be seen in all aspects of their robot. While creeping through a jungle of ideas, their cat-like focus and modularity exemplifies a great design. Hear their growl as they overtake the competition. Congratulations team 6424, Stealth Panther Robotics!

Though this herd is small, their efforts and their robot left a mighty impression across the field. They used their team’s innovation to create new ways to CORRAL falling algae. They HERDED up points by adjusting their design to increase the scope of their robot, and took their areas of opportunity BY THE HORNS using Microsoft Power BI. Used their knowledge of pneumatics to roll up algae like tumbleweeds. Stampeding through the competition, congratulations to team 2165, The BisonBots!

Rising from the world of LEGO, this team’s future burns brightly. As they dream, these Rookies soar like Veterans. Out of the BLUE, they are no longer in the ashes. Congratulations to team Blue Phoenix!

This rising all-star team stood out by going the literal distance for FIRST. Their actions at home and during the competition could not be sunk by any obstacles they faced, and have proven to be a strong, resilient team with the FORESIGHT to exemplify FIRST principles in their community. Congratulations to our friends from Turkey: Team 8760, the Foresighters!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: SOFA STEM on Wheels This team of professionals is the embodiment of sustainability not just within their team, but throughout the globe. With their ten year plan for creating STEM opportunities, their focus on careers, coaching, and community engagement, has had a generational impact through promoting the spirit of FIRST. There's no grinding gears here! Congrats team #2341, Sprockets!

This team is high energy, leaving behind a spectacular trail of positivity and enthusiasm for FIRST. Cheering and dancing in the stand and in the pits, their Southern Charm has captivated us all. Marching in like a Mardi Gras band, this team throws out Team Spirit everywhere they go. Congratulations to team 2080, Torbotics!

This team performs with ICE-COLD precision, crafting CAD created parts that are as solid as a glacier. Every component is engineered for superior performance ensuring they skate past the competition, leaving them shivering. When the game heats up, their robot stays cool under pressure. Chilling in the name, thrilling the in the game… Congratulations team 5690, SubZero Robotics!

This team beams with sportsmanship and collaboration. Demonstrating professionalism in the pits and off the field, they combine unity and respect into a well-balanced force. Congratulations to team 3660, The Lightsabers!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Their team name was originally created to impose fear on the competition, and they designed a unique fine threaded solution to a challenge they faced with alignment in the field. The Festival of Lights in Chickasha is a great place to spot the WHOOP WHOOP of these fearsome yard birds. Congratulations to the Cockadoodle Dominators!

This team has a robot EQUIPped well for all challenges it ENGAGEs in on the field. This EMPOWERed robot consistently rises above, EXPANDs the team's ability to lead, and EXCITEs their alliance toward victory. While easy-going and CASUALLY HEROIC, this team and their high-quality robot are sure to BREAKAWAY for the win! Congratulations TEAM 3937, Breakaway!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Cutting like a sword through ice cream, their controls allowed them to rule supreme. Their ALL SEEING control system gave their robot its position in real time. These sneaky engineers have a sense for the importance of every second. Congratulations team 2383, the Ninjineers!

By always knowing which direction was south, they flock to the center of the Reef and knew where to anchor their collected coral. Without running A-FOWL, they scored during autonomous, time and again, which fits the bill! Congratulations team 1561, the Roboducks!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team sets the imagery bar high for all of the teams in the pits with their consistent and hard-to-miss visual display. From matching pants and shirts, to being calm above and paddling like crazy below, this squeaky-clean team is scrubbing the pits clean with their image. So, glub, glub, cluck, cluck, this team is leaving no rings around their tub! Congratulations to team 10219, the Bathtub Chickens!

How does this team spell success? S-T-E-M This team demonstrated remarkable commitment to FIRST teams across FLL, FRC and FTC. Their ability to overcome obstacles and their impressive outreach in both official languages has enabled them to reach hundreds of thousands of Canadians. A strong community focus ensures that even in the face of adversity, they manage risk and execute their 5-year sustainability plan for long term success. These high school students have really FLOCKED together and SPELLED out what it means to have a lasting impact in their community.

This team doesn’t just CRUSH it on the field, they are a GLOWING example of FIRST values. With a solid sustainability plan, a robust strategy for sponsorship and a well-diversified STEM advocacy effort, this team empowers a BROAD SPECTRUM of humanity. They took support that came from increasing visibility and used to shine a light on others in need. Like an arc across the sky, their reach extends into global communities, ILLUMINATING paths for STEM through advocacy, accessibility, and innovation. They have SHIFTED perceptions with their unwavering commitment and RADIANT impact on FIRST.

This team embraces their diverse passions to design impactful community outreach programs that truly make a difference. They EDIT… their community by mixing a mobile, hands-on learning adventure with virtual training to inspire countless schools across a sprawling region They always use their compass to ensure their DARTS… reach the bullseyes.

records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: This team of FLL veterans forged strong bonds and overcame numerous challenges throughout their rookie year. By reflecting on their journey, this team effectively showcased their fundraising structure, established a solid succession plan, and secured their future by returning to their roots and continuing the mentorship of 4 FLL teams. In fueling dreams and shaping futures, this team really BUBBLED… up to the top.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team views the field from a different angle. Their lightweight, compact, coral delivery system ensures they don’t go past their designed limits. A robust, high performing robot proves the THEORY… behind their design.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.script: This small but mighty team fully embraced the spirits of FIRST by innovating fearlessly. These champions for environmental causes make an impact far beyond the robot. As stigma fighters, they know no limits and rocked the Judges with their passions and perseverance.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.script: When overcoming one obstacle made two more appear, this team wouldn’t stop. Cold calling sponsors, leveraging resources and recognizing their limitations allowed them to SCALE up their success. Watch for them to RISE UP and STRIKE at future challenges.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: ROOTED in strong values and BRANCHING into the future, this team has built a legacy of sustainable practices. You WOODEN believe the training program they used to pass knowledge to younger members resulting in sustained excellence. Their commitment to long-term impact is as solid as OAK!

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.script: From a place of water and snow, this team makes every member feel welcomed. This team stood out for its creativity and originality. The Judges’ tip our HATS to this team don’t just show their spirit, they KNIT it.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.script: This team RISES to the occasion with precision and a SPRINKLE of innovation - like the perfect recipe for engineering excellence. Their designs are CRISP, their problem-solving is GOLDEN, and their impact STICKS with you like SYRUP on a Sunday morning. This year’s Excellence in Engineering award goes to a team that is truly STACKED with talent.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.script: When other teams are in distress, this team is ready to ATTEND with open arms and good sportsmanship. They don’t hesitate to provide LIFE SUPPORT. With this team, the gracious professionalism CLINIC is in good hands.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s robot is making waves. With an original algae mechanism and an embedded multi-function climber system, this team’s creativity and performance are forever stamped in our memories. From vacuums to smiling buckets, we’re all on the same wavelength…

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.script: This team turned the idea that ‘less is more’ into a winning strategy. With each iteration they learned to turn their ‘weakness into strength’. In the end, they ‘discovered the paradox’ that what begins as a challenge can become a triumph.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: These regal hunters prey on ground corals and algae with precision and efficiency. Using a harmonious integration of software and hardware, they can seamlessly interact with the environment. It’s no wonder that this wise and watchful team took control of the competition.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.script: This robot navigates the REEFSCAPE with 20 millisecond ELECTRORECEPTION precision. It DRIFTS through the TIPPING POINT and consistently scores 4 coral autos before flawlessly switching to algae. This self-propelled SHARK leaves the competition in their wake.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Science Division
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: You won't find a PATINA on this team's look, which is integrated in their robot, pit, and team uniforms. Their logo melds their mascot, technology, and faith with bold color choices that really stand out. You don't need HAWK EYES to see how their visuals really SOAR.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team's iterative approach to build and design delivered a sleek, dark robot of amazing efficiency. The robot's movements strike with lightning-like speed and unerring precision. Their beautiful design will bring the lights down on the competition field.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.script: This team has a gracious grip on entrepreneurship and professionalism. They donate custom-made parts to the teams that need them and sell them to teams that can afford them, spreading technology to their community and across the world. This is bound to rub off on any team that might be spinning their wheels. The Gracious Entrepreneurship award goes to

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.script: The renewed energy this team puts into FLL mentorship and summer camps, serves as a role model for future generations of FRC participants. They have put in motion a recruitment strategy that has transformed the team from an 8 to 29 member team in 3 years. They Valiantly champion the advancement of STEM in their community by awarding their own educational bursary!

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has definitely done their part to clean up the world around them. Not only do they work hard to get team members onboard in their understanding of climate change, they also published books about climate for the next generation. They RISE above the crowd with STEM funding for their communities while calculating their carbon footprint to help maintain their carbon neutrality.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.script: This team’s enthusiasm will have you howling at the moon. They truly come out of their shell for you. This ship sails true with their CAPTAIN ON DECK!

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.script: These students have a design process that any professional engineer would be proud to follow. Their clear and detailed documentation shows the progressive phases of their robot design leading to recognized results on the field. This team really loves their zero, alpha, and beta bots

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.script: The weather this past Wednesday seemed ‘tailor-made’ for this team’s arrival. They worked tirelessly to build a welcoming community within their own school, in the pits, and with their collaborators online. When on-field mishaps almost caused their success to drift away, they were exemplary champions of FIRST ideals.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
