records.script: The inventiveness shown in the design and build of the “rotating end effector” is outstanding. The robot’s ability to manipulate both algae and coral speak to a clear, concise strategy and planning. The engineering and control of the robot leaves the pack in a spin!

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.script: This team demonstrates a focus on quality throughout their design and build process. They have built a distinctively robust machine with sleek laser cutouts to manage their weight in an elegant black layout. Their welded bottom frame is stronger than a charging bull.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: The robot’s aggregated sensors provided an effective control for both autonomous mode and tele-operated mode. By integrating sensors throughout their iterative design process, the team found a solution through their own circuit board design. Their control strategy made for a dominant lean GREEN machine!

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.script: Coming from a land of apple trees, they are used to picking things off the ground; they taught their robot well. At the beginning they play “Reach for the Top” and get it right 5 times in a row. And then with lightning reflexes the robot lights up the arena when it is time for its human to shoot.

records.eventName: FIRST Ontario Provincial Championship - Technology Division
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team was an animal out on the field, true to its roots. Connecting the flow of nature and technology in a sustainable manner. This sacred imagery award comes to life with the IRON DOG.

This team did an outstanding job on showing who they are and what they achieved for the community. They truly implemented FIRST core values and had a strong environmental impact. They touched rural communities locally and internationally. Everything they do is just BEEEE -autiful!!!

This team is a true blueprint for engineering and a role model for many. From mentoring young innovators to sharing their practice field with over 35 teams, they inspire at every level. Flipping the script on engineering outreach, this team turns paradox into reality.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: When looking for industrial design, this team got the judges buzzing. Their commitment to create a robot with a state of the art arm that can reach different depth levels is evident, and combines well with the overall aesthetic of their robot. Their workmanship has electrified the judges and has taken them to the next level.

This team flies high in autonomous mode. Focusing on the mission of FIRST, this young team caught the judge’s attention with their unique design. They migrated to share their knowledge with others and they left the judges feeling inspired.

This new team has a true grassroots start. Not only did they build a robot, they embody the spirit of FIRST and are actively contributing to its mission. This team is sure to not lose the signal of FIRST.

When this team was swatted at with challenges, they didn't sting in self-defense but flew like a rising star. The chosen team worked together to build and maintain their colony. They approached the competition with persistence and launched their robo-NEST to new heights.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Discussions can get very hot when trying to improve from one year to the next. This team can make your eyes turn green with envy with all their efforts to increase their cohesion while reducing their environmental impact. This team is always improving their processes, training, and sustainability with their Robo-Links and Mini-Bots.

The judges were amazed at this team’s infectious enthusiasm and how they interacted with each other. The team's spirit was ever obvious in the way they presented themselves. It was “ALL HANDS ON DECK” To the winning team, the judges can only say “AYE AYE CAPTAIN!”

The judges have been watching for teams demonstrating a professional approach to the design process. This team documented, communicated, and executed their time analysis and archetypes to squeeze every point from a match. They say Lamelo can’t BALL, but this team thought of it ALL!

This team’s gracious nature set them apart from the rest. Their structured approach is evident and you can be sure they are always ready to lend a hand. What makes this team ideal for the Gracious Professionalism award is their Simbiotic relationships.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team blew into the competition with an ice cold approach to the game dynamic. Designing their single intake to handle both coral and algae at the same time made their robot a tempest on the field of play. Riding their super cycle to rise against the harsh winds of competition…

This team focused on a simple and compact design. Their attention to details, including a low profile, enclosed wiring, and strategic use of 3D -printed parts for robustness, was key to their success. Their divine vision from the legendary age has led to top quality.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Their speed on the field is achieved with a push of a button. They have a vision system allowing them to track and ingest algae and coral from the ground. They’re at the top of the food chain in both the ranks and in controls.

Deep in the sea is a green machine lurking for coral and algae. Self navigating the field and scoring at will, their driver assist is a slam dunk. This team is full steam ahead and has chartered a course to the emerald isle.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team embraced the Reefscape season with their water based theme. They used powerful imagery that starts at the pit, and continues through their team gear and robot. This team inspires the entire FIRST community with their commitment to imagery.

This team is recognized for combining this year's game, Reefscape, with spreading the mission of FIRST throughout their community and outreach events. This team has long standing connections with their industry sponsors, and continuously reaches out to grow their network. They are generous with their success by sponsoring and mentoring multiple teams in the FIRST community. With more outreach days than group members, this team prioritizes full integration of even the youngest team members into all aspects of the program. Their robot is just the tip of the iceberg. Despite a tragic setback, this team reinvented itself. Ne jamais lacher. Nunquam cede. Gaan wiikka boontaaken. NEVER EVER QUIT.

This team’s efforts to recruit students and BRANCH out their SPRAWLING network amazed the judges. The judges were beyond impressed with this team’s succession planning and training programs. They are PLANTing the SEEDS for the FIRST community. Their deep ROOTED commitment to STEM education is strong as an OAK.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: With a coiled focus this robot strikes with precision when it matters most. This team iterated & improved many key features, leading to a clean robot design worthy of recognition and one built to withstand the demands of competition. Their robot can be ssseen ssslithering around the field

A picture can paint a thousand words. This Judge’s award celebrates a team that is developing tools which empower children & adults impaired by head injuries to contribute their ideas. Their work has helped break barriers for people with Aphasia. This team proves they’re built for teamwork and wired for greatness, showing that together, anything is possible.

Riding the tide to success this rookie team seems to have the wind in their sails From a thriving FLL to this year’s FRC debut, this team has made a big splash! Growing under pressure of competition, no challenge will “burst their bubble”
They took on the challenge with a passionate crew Forging ahead with armour anew Second year team with strength in their metal, pushing on through.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team definitely shows the ropes to the younger generation. The judges were impressed by their deep dive into both team sustainability AND environmental sustainability, shown in their detailed succession plan and recycling program. Together they make sure to keep their northern hometown beaches sparkling clean.

This team shares the spirit of FIRST with their community through their “playroom experiment” and STEAM. Their team cheer makes it clear: not only do they build robots, but robots also build them! When other teams need a hand, this team’s mascot “gives a dam”, and if you’ve “lost your socket,” they can definitely help!

Before this ship could sail, there was a lot of time “whale” spent in the engineering and design process. The judges were “ferry” impressed with this team’s well-articulated and thorough design cycle, telling us their needs, wants, and wishes to their wills, mays, and won’ts. The result might be the inverse of what this team wanted, but it’s about the “sea-nic” journey not the destination that matters.

Like coral strengthening the reef, this team uplifts others on and off the playing field through their generosity and leadership. With their ongoing tide of commitment, they continue to chart a course of gracious professionalism year over year. This team empowers and financially supports indigenous youth in technology, propelling them towards success.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Making waves with their multi-purpose intake design, equipped with a high-speed, swiveling shooter, this agile machine showcased exceptional maneuverability through the competition. This team turned a THEORY into reality…

This team's rugged machine cruised to the front of the PACK. They unleashed excellence in their robot’s design and craftsmanship. From its reliable mission mechanisms to its clean wiring, this team asserted their ALPHA position in this competition.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Getting out of control is very easy for robots on the reefs. The judges were impressed by this team’s meticulous P.I.D control fine-tuning process that used linear equations, letting them soar above water. This fire(hawk) is a shining light of innovation excellence.

This robot had no captain to guide them in the sunken realm beneath the waves. Their vision sensors, combined with smart filtering like Kalman filter, ensured their precise motion and buttery-smooth scoring. They never “WAFFLED” on accuracy.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s pit, clothing, and robot had a beautifully coordinated aquatic theme. The judges loved that the robot also served as the team’s mascot. The winning team’s imagery really made WAVES.

With a mission to make STEM, agriculture, and accessibility better for everyone, this team mentored future innovators, hosted workshops across the globe, and even adopted a park because they know changing the world doesn't stop at robotics. This group is more than just a team; they’ve been coding their way through Lunar Hacks, running with the best at the Army Run, and proving that purple isn’t just a colour; it’s a way of life! They’re a flock of inspirators, committed to spreading the FIRST mission through their innovation, dedication and a whole lot of baaaaaaaaaaaaaaad puns. And when it comes to safety, they don’t just follow the rules – they lead the charge….‘Safety first, or you’ll be in deep sheep!’

Living near the water and making waves, this team has breached the reef without leaving a trace. By promoting FIRST values they are inspiring other FRC teams to BEE net-zero. Their summer camps are buzzing with FLL teams, their project RISE and books for kids are helping FIRST dreams.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team, with a sharp predatory mindset has designed a robot that blends precision and efficiency. This bot combines a tensioner pulley, custom absolute encoder and a proximity sensor which allows them to catch coral, algae and cages. Their iterative improvements make BRUCE an industrial force.
This team advocates for sharing FIRST across the globe. Even a dry rinse cycle couldn’t hold them back. This team had to overcome “a little shop of horrors” by going with the flow.
No one is ever alone in FIRST Robotics. Each team stands on the shoulders of giants. With great partnerships even the smallest team can have a big impact.

When it looked like "game over" this team stepped up. Significant setbacks early in the year were no obstacle for these enthusiastic students to overcome. In their quest for a "high score" they are ready to press "play".

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team focuses on leadership and longevity with exact precision. They target all aspects of FIRST. With a research based approach, they have hit the bullseye on inclusive, robust STEM outreach programs that promote long term continuity. Their Teach the teacher program and no burnout system, is sure to keep this team sustained.
This team is a unified force, dedicated to coopertition. They are fiery advocates in all details. Their enthusiasm on and off the field is red hot!

The team took a BOTTOM UP approach in the engineering design of their robot. With snake-like precision and unwavering focus, their systematic engineering design approach delivered complete and signed documentation. The team's sleek black robot has CHARGED forward in this competition.

Like a river connecting communities, this team has extended support to many teams, enabling them to experience First Robotics to the fullest. Their many acts of kindness combined with coopertition form a torrent of gracious professionalism.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Rounding out any fleet, this team’s focus is on a clean reef and a full barge. To avoid getting “trapped” in the weeds, they “spring” into action With this creative approach, Earl’s not mousing around.
When it comes to shooting for the moon this team is all business. This machine is the leader of the pack for survivability. Can we get a Yip Yip for the winners of the Quality Award.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: With the push of a button, this team can navigate rough seas with ease. This innovative control floats to the top and brings their identity to life. Congratulations on developing THE ice cube.
This team trained with high visual acuity from the 905. They slip across the field with a single command like a walk in the park. You'll find no ticks on these Huskies.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team's aesthetic is interwoven into the fibre of everything they do. There is a common thread of brilliance that's integrated even into their robot. We are all in awe of their purple pageantry.

This is large team of highly motivated students: tomorrow’s engineers, mathematicians and Master’s of the Universe. They have spread their message, transforming the culture, throughout the GTA and across the seas like leaves in the wind. They reach out to the elderly, the differently abled, and the neurologically challenged. They are a team firmly rooted in the core principles of gracious professionalism. We believe they are a team grounded in excellence and a shining example of what FIRST can accomplish.

The judges were amazed at this team's commitment to spreading STEM education within their school and the greater community. Utilizing their own workshop and resources they uplift other young innovators, especially in the areas of manufacturing. Their open documentation showcases a degree of excellence that is on par with a particular NBA team from Boston.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team excels at taking shots at the net. Their robot’s aesthetic design and innovative re-use of materials was hard to miss. If GOALIA were watching, she’d be proud

With their strong foundation, these guppies have a bright future. By building symbiotic relationships with community and industry sponsors, these students have now become the teachers. Rising out from 10,000 leagues of pressure, this former FLL team floated to the top.

Embracing knowledge, creativity, and strategy, this team gave it all. With their name on the line, they have introduced FIRST to their town. Without a school location, they learned from mentors and other teams in the comfort of their basements.

Like a Rising Star in the night sky, this team faced the challenges of team turnover, training, and partnerships on the field of play. Before the season, they suited up to conquer recruitment and get themselves ready to reemerge as gallantly as possible. Like Knights in battle, they fought through to rebuild their team.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This green team is making waves with consistent recruiting and community engagement. Turning old into new and junky into functional, this team is the master of repurposing. With the help of their electrifying sponsors, the team is King of Sustainability.

This team has a spirited collaboration that allows them to gallop over diversity They exude enthusiasm as they travel across their community to suture the Bleed Everyone, steel yourselves for these stallions

This team RED all the manuals and took a slow methodical approach to their design. Translating good engineering practice into a dominant force on the field. They overcame many obstacles and did not turtle under pressure.

This team makes a splash causing ripples across their community. Their vast network invites students from Primary through high schools and the community at large to continue their FIRST mission. From their humble beginnings to the world stage reaching thousands, this team truly sparkles

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s creative approach to the robot game shows they are playing with the pros. Their elevated approach to coral let the pendulum swing in the right direction. In a league of their own, this team was a logical choice for this award.

When other teams appeared unsteady, this team stood tall with strength and pride. Guiding with stability, they went to great lengths to ensure the team remained unfrayed. This team thunders to new heights of quality.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team doesn’t have any sticky buttons. Their controls integrate multiple sensors to always know where it is. They ironed out all the kinks on their robot.

This team’s robot is the deadliest predator with extreme consistency. Wherever they might be on the field, they swoop down to grab prey and bring it to the top through robust autonomous functions. This team may seem a little flighty, but don’t be mistaken by their costumes, they really are owls at heart.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: The judges were impressed by the way this team's imagery was deeply ingrained within their tradition. Beauty brought their pit to life, and was integral to their inclusion of new team members Hat’s on!

This team manages to leave an IMPACT on every community they meet local and worldwide. The stories of their team’s efforts, and how they inspire girls to pursue STEM, reach people in multiple languages. These GIRLS WITH A WRENCH have created a legacy in their team and community.

This teams hits the BULLSEYE when inspiring the next generation of engineers. With a decade of dedication, they stay on POINT to deliver a thriving education pipeline, empowering students. Their DARTS program and commitment to learning have inspired 1,000 students in Sudbury and beyond.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: With a key combination of skills, engineering, and innovation, this team’s robot executed flawlessly. No SHORTCUTS were taken in their design decisions, fine-tuned for efficiency and performance precision. They SHUT DOWN their competition with their ring gear rotation mechanism, delivering high performance and unmatched precision.

The Judges were ATTRACTED to the unique ELEMENTS of this team’s robot. Their exceptional team cohesion SHOULDERS the weight of competition on and off the field. They CLAWED their way back up after a long HIBERNATION.

This rookie team’s SPARKS were first IGNITED at FTC. They were laser focused on their defensive strategy to launch themselves to new heights. This team gave an ELECTRIFYING performance in their very first year of FRC.
On the verge of extinction, this team has POUNCED back. They SHARPENED their technical skills with help from other teams. With hard work and bake sales, this CAT is back in the hunt.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: In terms of team sustainability, their consistent recruitment and training of new members makes waves. Their team is a centerpiece of their school, collaborating with other student clubs to run recycling drives. Their members are DROPS OF WATER, but together, they have a huge RIPPLE EFFECT.

Always exploring new ideas, venturing into the unknown, and conquering the challenges they face, this team showed a big presence in the stands and could not be ignored on the field, in the stands, and in the meadows. Their namesake disappeared from Newfoundland 1000 years ago, but this team demonstrates a spirit that draws inspiration from Valhalla.

This team showed great effort in their design and build process. Narrowing down from an everything bot to a specialized bot, this team manages to stay on top. They combined science, sports, (...PAUSE...) and socials, to create a well-engineered robot.

Like a breath of fresh air, this team LIFTED UP everyone around them. They provided a WHIRLWIND of support and positivity through every booth. The Judges were BLOWN AWAY by their pneumatic system and unmatched teamwork.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team is agile and has a clear VISION for their goals. They were able to finish the game creatively with their unique hang feature. Using signals to alert their drivers, this team is a HOOT in the night.

The Judges were HOOKED by this robust build. While harvesting aquatic life with their multipurpose manipulators, this team sustained impacts without capsizing. They proved that electricity and water DO mix.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team is above the PACK. Their precise, reliable, and controlled aiming algorithms combined with intuitive design to redefine efficiency and adaptability in robot targeting. This predator’s sensing and HOWLING effort was as clear as the moon in the night sky.

This team rose COURAGEOUSLY to venture in the deep. They were quick to place corals and load them onto the net, optics and proximity sensors. SNOWED IN but never slowed down, their KINETIC and CHIVALROUS energy runs deep.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This FASHIONABLE team makes a LOVELY statement. As a team, they embraced a vibrant theme with HEARTFELT COORDINATION. They “HEART” robotics.

Impacting their community and beyond, overcoming barriers, bringing change by influencing their schools’ superintendent and getting their school rebranded as a focal point for STEM learning, this team brings hope, optimism, and playfulness to their world. This team of 45 strong-willed individuals has impacted more than 4400 growing minds and teachers over the past 3 years in FIRST programs. With an almost 100 to 1 ratio of FIRST effort made to results proven, this investment of their time and efforts is a truly great achievement worthy of their name. The depth and breadth of their outreach have touched many students and new immigrant youth who thought achieving success in STEM projects was out of their reach. Their shared vision brings it all together. If you wonder what they will achieve in the years to come and how they will continue to expand the principles of FIRST just “PINK of the POSSIBILITIES”.

A true community team spreading their wings far and wide engaging with many schools. They are focused on ‘growing’ FIRST and STEM through extensive summer camps, school robotic events , fun fairs including the CNE. This team is “growing” a forest of inspired young minds.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team’s robot is the Crown Jewel of Aesthetics and functionality. They are The King of CAD and precision engineering with a majestic design that reigns above all others. The monarchs of machinery, who set the royal standards of superior design.

This team sheds light on the good, as they are in sight when showcasing their strengths and skills. They are building online support for other FIRST teams, supporting both local and international communities and charities, while ensuring to seek new opportunities. This team wears multiple hats and is seen as ‘A Ray of Sunshine’

This community team is fresh off the game board. They fearlessly take risks, are resourceful, and have built a dynamic team from multiple schools. You can count on these Rookies to leave a lasting mark at future events.

This team showed they have both bark and bite when overcoming challenges. They are leading the pack, have a solid multi-year plan, guiding their fellow young teams as stellar role models. These all-stars are oooon (on) the chase!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Iron-clad on preserving the environment and their team. They practice the 3Rs (Reduce, Re-use, Recycle) and build for the future. This team is the epitome of positive and sustainable impact.

When they heard a howl from the pack they joined in along with their alumni , mentors , parents, and sponsors. The pack expanded and rebranded, gathering local support from suppliers and the community exemplifying team spirit!
This team in black, presents such an elegant fine finished robot. Each of their alliance partners enjoys how this robot makes the game look so easy. There is No ALT - F4 in this team’s gameplay.

Keeping everyone safe was a priority for this team. They were proactive in supporting teams and volunteers, to ‘Safely See’ in the pits and field. This team joined the brotherhood of Gracious Professionalism.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: When presented with a design challenge this team sailed against the tide. They stayed low and fast but pivoted to new heights. They plundered the riches of their creativity.
This team’s design was lean, powerful, and built to endure. They ‘Prowled’ for a robust, agile design to quickly replace components as the ‘Jungle’ demands. They Pounced to claw the quality award.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Sightings of this team were reported searching for coral. Their innovative use of cameras let their drivers see the field and bolt ahead of the competition. With a truly monster performance, they made others green with envy.

This team came to each match cheering loudly and ready to play ball. Their effective use of cameras and other sensors led to revolutionary advances in their robot’s capabilities. Their consistent performance in autonomous operations was a ‘Real Coup’.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team is right at home in the ocean waters. They beautified the reefs with the support of a ‘gold-caped goddess’. They knew how to add eye-catching imagery to the reefscape.

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.script: In the rough seas around the reef, the judges were left with a HARRRRD decision about the savviest ship. This team nurtured their reef through an outstanding outreach effort, global mentorship, innovative authorship, impeccable inclusion of all ages and genders, providing lifeboats, starting planks and ABC’s for other teams. They left no question about “WHO” ARRR the most impactful.

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.script: This team has a wide and diverse impact on FIRST and their entire community, starting teams where there were none, mentoring teams through black and white patches, and assisting teams, even at events. Many teams find they need a part replaced or some help fixing a problem. “Who ya gonna call?” For this event’s Engineering Inspiration, you’re gonna call this team.

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Forged from metal showcasing their innovative design. With circuits etched in wings, it is a precision crafted robot that soars above the rest, This steampunk bird of prey swooped down on the competition.

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.script: This team starts with strategy, hopping between their strengths and weaknesses. Their involvement within their school and their weekly support of each other caught the judges’ eye– like a frog catching flies. For recognizing their greatness

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.script: This rookie team attributes their accomplishments to detailed planning and focus. Even though they are a rookie team, they have a safety program that could rival industry leaders. With COVID decimating most teams in their region, this team built itself up from the rubble, emerging strong and resilient!

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.script: The recipients of this award arrived with an elegant and innovative robot. They soared to new heights and swerved around their competition. They lit a fire for girls in STEM.

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team impressed the judges with their extraordinary outreach, recycling, and team approach to cold calls. Sustainability is exemplified in the sheer number of camps they host and their sunny continuity plan. When they do stuff they do it well, and they teach the next generation to do it even better.

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.script: Despite delays, short build time and other challenges, this team exuded enthusiasm in all their interactions. This all-girls team showed their Amazon spirit. Congratulations to the Goddesses of the Sea.

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.script: This team’s clean, sleek machine moves fast and does so with style. Building countless prototypes, their final 4-tier elevator design rose to the challenge. Their high flying machine lights up the competition and fully stands above the rest.

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.script: This team welcomes girls of all schedules and schools, valuing every contribution they can make. They lend parts to other teams and have recently partnered with a local library to start an FLL team. The winning team graciously corrects safety issues in a fun way by having the safety frog point them out.

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team had a creative multi-purpose approach to their gantry system. They have a future in Formula One racing with their professional fast pit stops. This team could expertly juggle algae and coral at the same time– and is known by name.

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.script: This team’s robot is a model of clean design and professional craftsmanship. With organized wiring, modular systems for future upgrades, and an elevator so effective they sold it to other teams, their build is as functional as it is polished. Their use of an absolute coder ensures precise arm positioning every time.

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team circled up their coral with ease– and buttoned up with complete control. They buttered up the field with their hot approach during the competition. As part of the world record-setting performance yesterday– they brought the popcorn to celebrate!

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.script: When the buzzer sounded and the match kicked off, this team’s robot sprang into action with unwavering precision– no driver needed. By engineering a custom circuit board to fuse multiple sensors into one powerful brain, they built an autonomous system that saw the field clearly, reacted instantly, and executed flawlessly. They’ve knighted their code and crowned their sensors

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Casting their nets wide, this team looked to their surroundings to create their image. Integrating imagery with layered meaning into their robot, booth, and appearance. This “horse-fish” robot team masterfully combined culture with technology.

This team has had an strong impact on their community, starting plain and simple, helping a few FLL teams get started. Adding a bit of colour to their community, they spread the FIRST mission while applying great engineering to solve social challenges. This team is winning this award for the set of their rainbow sails… Congratulations to team 4039 Makeshift Robotics

From student-led technical training to weekly FLL outreach, this team creates space where all are welcome, inspiring engineering in their community. They put the “A” in “STEAM”, mounting online virtual STEAM tutorials while earning high-school leadership credits. Staying behind late to clean the stands with their bright yellow presence, this team RAIDED the judges’ hearts. Congratulations to team 5024, Raider Robotics

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team is all about fit, form, and function. From modular design, to each piece fitting together perfectly, this team’s work came together as one seamless unit. They considered every possible failure, from repairs to replacements, ensuring that nothing gets overlooked. Their strategy was “Go straight, pick and BAM!” Congratulations to team 2702, Rebels

This team is recognized for the unique logistics, travel, and staffing hurdles they solved with even more unique solutions. A team so ingrained in their community’s identity that their robot is featured in their museum and annual parade. They swooped in Friday representing the nobility and industry of the mighty beaver with pride. Congratulations to team 6098, blrobot

The FRC learning curve is very steep, especially for teams starting from scratch. This one impressed the Judges with solid design choices that keep their goals in front of them and allow them to strike quickly. From London Ontario,… Congratulations to team 10554, Team Vipers

After the loss of prime members, this team united around community and family to re-invent themselves. Through looking inward and tightening the purse strings, they survived their wilderness to be here today. Their robot does more than just compete, it’s helping transform their team into a true PACK of rising stars. Congratulations to Team 5689, CK Cyber Pack

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team's dedication to environmental sustainability and outreach have impressed the judges. They have effectively utilized donated parts to minimize waste. They managed to sustain their team through sustaining the environment. Their commitment to the cause is obvious through their work style like a colony of beavers. Congratulations to team 2609 BeaverWorX

This team has demonstrated unity, enthusiasm, and deep commitment to each other and their community. Throughout the competition, they have shown unwavering support for one another, constantly uplifting their teammates in the pits. Their contagious energy was felt everywhere, and their attachment to the team’s message and success is ROCK SOLID. Congratulations to team 8089, Rockway Robotics!

This team used a professional design approach featuring CAD and prototyping. They made extensive use of light sensors, simulations, single-button controls, and offset tags. They believe that it’s impossible to jam their robot! Congratulations to team 1114, Simbotics

This team’s level of gracious professionalism impressed the judges. Their effect could be felt locally, domestically, and even across the globe. They spread joy with their unique headwear this weekend; despite their struggles they CLEANED up for this award and are AWASH with positive feelings. Congratulations team 7757 Atomic Dishwashers

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team has been around a while but still focused on keeping it simple. They managed to find creative solutions to what could have led to complex designs. Using tie rods instead of a heavy base made them light and fast. Congratulations to team 3683 Team Dave

This team exuded overall quality in all areas, from design and engineering to actions on the field. Speed and robustness were forefront in the concept and fabrication of their robot. They achieved goals their through evident teamwork and a quality-minded approach. This team’s mantra this season was focused on robust, effective, and fast results. Congratulations to TEAM 2056, OP Robotics

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team’s innovative, hands-on approach to robot development resulted in a unique strategy focusing on filling the barge. This led to excellent shooting that couldn’t be matched on an NBA court. Their Sponge Bot Square Frame was the Michael Jordan of the competition. Congratulations to Team 7476, EOM Lions

This team proudly represented their community by employing robust engineering principles and an ongoing commitment to continuous improvement. The judges were specifically impressed by the elegance of their vision system, which helped the robot moving swiftly, effectively and with style! This ‘bot could see its way even through a blackout! Congratulations to team 2200, Burlington Community Robotics Blackout.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s commitment to their image is reflected in their coordinated attire. Their pit and robot are also spotless and aesthetically pleasing. With their comprehensive brand guide, when it comes to their image, there’s no room for GUESSING. Congratulations to Team 1646, Precision Guessworks

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lake Event
records.script: This next team knows what it’s like to be under the spotlight and face some tough questions. Under pressure, they presented their case and delivered some truly compelling evidence. And despite their vibrant colours, they certainly didn’t go green in the hot seat.

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lake Event
records.script: Tough, competitive, innovative, with a fiery passion. Cleverly using the best concepts from their whole team, this team’s engineering efforts are inspirational and ON FIRE.

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lake Event
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This sophisticated design emulates this deep blue city. With an impressive balance of beautiful finishes and iterative design, their robot exemplifies versatility and unique solutions to difficult challenges.

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lake Event
records.script: The judges were impressed with their unyielding resolve, swerving through the reef and clawing through the competition. This team’s season has been dedicated to the honour of their superhero, living up to their team name.

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lake Event
records.script: Just as a star begins with a spark of energy, pulling together gas and dust, fueled by passion and courage, a new team was formed. Through collaboration, friendship and trust, new stars have been forged with skills, knowledge and experience that will light a path to their future. This team has proven that a newly formed constellation can shine with the brilliance of a thousand suns.

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lake Event
records.script: In the face of adversity, they are fearless and resilient warriors. This team is thriving on only the most basic tools. Rising from the sea,

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lake Event
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: From a small school with big ambition, this team is laying the foundation for future innovators with heart, hustle and a high-voltage vision. Their commitment to mentorship, sustainability and student leadership charged them ahead of the curve. They don’t just plan for the next season - they surge forward with the kind of energy that builds a lasting legacy in FIRST.

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lake Event
records.script: When their school teams folded and the battle seemed lost, they banded together with the spirit of the myth they represent. The community heeded their war cries and helped fund their creative pursuits. Their shared energy is as powerful as the wonder women they are sure to become.

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lake Event
records.script: This team lowers the boom on the competition. With an outstanding dual intake system, their unique telescoping arm and stabilization system allowed them to achieve seemingly impossible feats. Although many may have thought they “sucked”, in fact, they are truly on the same wavelength and an excellent choice for excellence in engineering.

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lake Event
records.script: This award is about more than building robots, it’s about building community. This team embodies the spirit of FIRST by sharing their “pride” at local events and festivals. They are wired to help other youth through their work with children with disabilities, proving that education is for everyone.

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lake Event
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team clears the water of coral in more than one direction, allowing them to avoid the opposing alliance’s defensive robots. They employed innovative approaches and non-traditional materials that draw inspiration from our National Pastime. Their ingenuity and resourcefulness see them through the game challenge, on the strength of a Fin and a Prayer.

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lake Event
records.script: This year, all eyes are on this robot. Surging back from being knocked down, they showed that this robot has grit & durability. Their captain persevered through the tsunami of competition.

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lake Event
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This robot is an absolute monster, in loch step with the competition. All eyes were on this team’s unique control panel resulting in repeatable autonomous performance. It was as easy as 1-2-TREE to select this team for the innovation in control award.

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lake Event
records.script: This team POPPED to the top of this award category by cutting no CORNERS and integrating autonomous technology that they could consistently count on in every match. From their robot’s ability to wrangle coral, Incorporating Lidar into their build, and integrating multiple driver-assist systems, to enable their driver to hold the reins while letting their robot do the trotting and score in multiple ways. This pony had a whole mind of its own,

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lake Event
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Surrounded by water, they have a strategy in place in case things get wet. Coordinating mascot, robot, and human players, with intent and passion, this team’s imagery memorializes their beloved Cooper.

Our Impact Award winner has been bringing the FIRST message to its community for years. From bringing STEM to schools to working with other FRC teams, they do it all. With their ***BRIGHT YELLOW*** uniforms, they are navigating their ship to the future of robotics.

The Engineering Inspiration winner spreads interest in engineering throughout their community. Recruiting young students by showing them what engineering can do. Their onglong efforts to load FLL teams onto their *** BUS *** advances appreciation fo engineering.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team exemplifies rapid prototype and *** ELECTFIFYING *** solutions. They used 3D printing to merge parts and test failure modules. In gameplay, this team's elevator really *** RIPS ***.

This is the *** EYE OF THE STORM *** award. As the *** WATERS *** get choppy, this team keeps their first community *** AFLOAT *** With a *** SCHOOL *** of outreach programs and helping other FRC teams There is nothing phoney about the *** MONSTER*** in this *** LAKE***

The *** STARS *** are in their name! While newbees to FIRST robotics, they never ever gave up getting their robot to work! As their high school name implies, they are *** TRAILBLAZERS *** in their community.
Diving into FRC, 75% of the *** HIKERS *** are new to the team. They rebuilt their team using a pipeline through the FIRST programs. *** RISING *** up to the challenge.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Adopting to the challenge facing their *** COLONY ***, these engineers have built a robot from debris, giving it a second life. Nurturing an ecosystem for long-term success This team certainly is not *** ERATIC ***

Given *** THREE *** changes to be positive, this team takes them *** ALL *** They did not let anything *** BREAK *** their spirit... We could *** SEE, SEE, SEE *** their enthusiasm throughout the competition with team bonding and a growth mindset.

The team did *** MULTIPLE *** prototypes to integrate their builds into the design process. They were able to engineer solutions to problems discovered during play to have a more robust game experience. Though coral intake can lead to unknown problems, this team *** DETERMINED *** to flush it out and come back for more.

There is nothing *** AVERAGE *** about how this team *** DISTRIBUTED *** support in the pits. They *** MULTIPLIED *** their impact to help several teams adrift. In the PITS, they jumped and *** MACHINED PARTS *** for other teams.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Faced with the challenge to catch corals, they turned their gaze *** WITHIN *** --- and innovation began. With roller manipulators, they gripped with confidence and precision, again and again. You can *** SEE ** their creativity shine break with a beautiful display proving their brilliance will win.
When it came to quality, this team was as reliable as the *** TIDE *** With *** REDUNDANT PARTS ***, *** RIVETED *** with care. They *** SPREAD THEIR WINGS *** and cleaned up the competition.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team's reusable *** CODE *** reliably led them to shore. They programmed the robot to function consistently throughout the match. They used the same code and did not *** COPY OR PASTE *** any errors.

records.teamName: SWARM - South and West Albany Robotics Maniacs
records.script: A group of *** JELLIES *** can be called a bloom. They move together as if programmed where to go. But when they attack, we call them a *** SWARM ***.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team *** BLEW *** our expectations out of the water by how iconic they are. They displayed their team spirit and pride boldly with their integrated design and imagery. They have *** SHOT *** our hearts right in the center.

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fair Event
records.script: It's no secret how important FIRST is in this community. This team's advocacy from coast to coast supports the impact felt from K through 12. We'd tip our hats to all the work they do, but Shhhhh! ...... It's confidential.

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fair Event
records.script: They wanted more team members—how about twice as many for this year? Their tin cup was filled with a flood for a STEM Lab. From outreach to community impact, this team is a Monster.

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fair Event
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team demonstrates an elegant use of pretty metal. Their rack and pinion elevator demonstrated a great mix of functionality along with aesthetics for an overall well-polished machine. <SING> We all live in a yellow submarine, a yellow submarine, a yellow submarine.

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fair Event
records.script: This team's community OUTREACH to lead potential teams and team members from a wider audience. In addition, this team was fast and accurate with coral scoring as well as removal of algae for all around success. Most importantly, this team's legislative advocacy that includes robotics as a CET program for state funding. The winner of the ADVOCACY Judge's award....

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fair Event
records.script: This team was passionate with members clamoring to talk the judges. Bouncing back from Covid and relocating they used their spiky determination and worked to train new members. Flying to new heights with the support from their community........

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fair Event
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Through innovation and dedication to sustainability this team is weaving together a greener future. I don't want to DRONE on about them but they recycled parts from other students programs into their designs. With the heart of a lion this young team is making a roaring impact one BYTE at a time.

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fair Event
records.script: This team formed a conspiracy of kindness with their emphasis on mental health. They flocked to each others aid sharing successes and putting fun first. With their newly elected FUN officer, their team members will fly solo nevermore.

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fair Event
records.script: In a competition full of complex robot design, this team showed that competitive robots do not have to be over-engineered. Their sleek design, alongside pages and pages and pages(!!!) of technical documentation spoke to a professional standard of engineering. This team proved that when dealing with a leviathan of a robot, it is imperative to have nerves of steel.

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fair Event
records.script: This team has their finger on the pulse of what Gracious Professionalism looks like on and off the field. Their efforts to lift up members of their community and to cross borders to share their love of FIRST has not gone unnoticed. Just as their namesake melds the organic and technical, this team has melded FIRST Core Values into their personal and technical relationships.

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fair Event
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team's creativity could rival Shakespeare. There's no robot they can't build with just an angle grinder, power drill and some fancy knots. It's sure to say that this team is everyone's favorite.

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fair Event
records.script: This team's clean and accessible design set this group up for fast troubleshooting. Their decision to use separate independent can bus systems provided design robustness. Thorough testing of their bot allowed them to hold up to the rigors of competition with no sweat off their stashes.

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fair Event
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This year’s winner in the gold and green has taken innovation to the next level. They used their own custom controller and a path planning algorithm for success. With their hexagonal controller incorporating a unique 12-button panel allowing for more intuitive and precise control they used a manual over ride to overcome their challenges.

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fair Event
records.script: This team's robot can score multiple game pieces while swerving to different stations. They SPARKLE as they zip around autonomously. They score so quickly SPARKS fly with their robot Guillotine.

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fair Event
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team's theme paved a trail through every part of their designs. They took their time with the details, but were speeding through the competition. Fun fact......when it comes to imagery, this team SNAILED it.

This team has greatly expanded the impact of STEM within their community, using FIRST programs as the catalyst. With a goal of bringing STEM to all their predominantly agricultural community, this team has become the roots of STEM education in their region. This team has partnered with other local organizations to increase their capacity and support for all their initiatives. From founding an impressive 34 new FLL teams in the last 3 years to developing a high-tech mobile STEM classroom, this team focuses on bringing STEM to underrepresented groups through their entire community. These FABulous students will stop at nothing to annex the ultimate STEM celebration wherever they go.
Sailing uncharted seas for two years, this team handled their sails solo. On and off the boat, their inspiration sparked excitement! Despite their size, their Flare is undeniable.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Their design is a perfect blend of form and function and rich in creativity. From a carefully crafted structure to sleek aesthetics, this robot not only performed at the highest level but looks the part as well. Just like an archer carefully aims and releases with precision, this team’s robot is a symbol of accuracy, power, and grace.

Faced with the fear of isolation, this team looked for a unique way to stay afloat. They recognized their lack of resources left them at a disadvantage, but they still showed up with unlimited passion. Digging in the trash for robot parts may not be anyone’s favorite, but this team sure is ours!
This team went from mini to king sized. They used the stars to navigate through turbulent waters. Through their diligence they have built a sustainable future.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Other people’s recycling is this team's treasure. Gathering bits and bobs along their way to creating their team's financial sustainability using their shields to surge forward in the fight to create a sustainable and cleaner world.
This team’s numbers stand true, they seed out others to join their flock. Sailing over the seas in tiaras into the Team Spirit Award....

They rise above their competition with a sea of documentation. This monster of engineering climbed their way to the top, hammering out any potential issues. By documenting and learning from their mistakes this steel “Leviathon” is a force to be reckoned with.
This team is a beacon in the night. When other teams were stuck in the sandbar, this team lent a helping hand. There’s no error with this team around!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: "Flying” across the field in red and black, this team moves fast. With its breadth of fiery carbon this robot lifts coral up from the depths. Tiny but mighty, they have the heart of a dragon.

Resilient and robust robots often fly under the radar. From an extra re-enforced frame, to hand done design work, this team shows a dedication to quality design. With a box of blue sharpies at their side, they’re sure to take the field by storm.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team was above average by using a 5 camera system. They submerged virtual reality down to the reef. The rest of the field should watch out for this nemesis.

This team demonstrated exceptional performance, ingenuity and consistency in their autonomous and teleop, like a finely tuned equation where even the tiniest variables were accounted for. Just a single flap of a butterfly’s wing can set off a hurricane, this team accounting for even the smallest detail resulting in a spectacular outcome, not chaos.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has a real “eye” for design. They put the “arg” in artwork. Their robot protects the reefs as it sails the high seas.

WHO is the team that is title one, that keeps fighting to keep everything free? WHO is the team that puts sensory items in the bag that keeps fighting for the kids? WHO is the team where all the members mentor? Where AUTO flies them home? WHO? WHO? WHO? 5401 – Fighting owls

This team is an animal with significant outreach, FLL team summer camps, open houses, and external training. Their shared scouting app helps themselves as well as others. Standing on four pillars, they ensure they are never in the doghouse.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team is sturdy and specialized, allowing their strategy to thrive. Their fabrication is cohesive, colorful, and consistent. In this universe they are speedy, not sluggish.
This team focuses on development and continuous improvement. They dive into the design process, allowing their submarine to rise to the top. Don’t underestimate the JV team.

records.teamName: Northeast High School Philadelphia Robotics Team
records.script: This team is as adaptable as they are gracious. Their ability to self-advocate is as strong as their defense. Watch out as they set sail on their design journey.

A young team, they are persistent in their performance, team, and robot development. This friendly, peaceful team drives toward a simple robot design. Their fancy field-centric control system prepares their robot for any pending earthquake.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team will have you watching with amazement as they incorporate their successes in team activity and environmental sustainability. They will have you seeing pink for women, green for the environment, and RED for winning!

Draped in red and black, this team wears their colors with pride. Do not let their laid-back attire fool you, for their true uniform is their unshakeable enthusiasm. It’s clear that when it comes to team spirit, this team is truly a force to be reckoned with.

This team has been design-focused from day one. They are intentional, organized, and buttoned-up all the way down to the color of their staples. Don’t be fooled by their age, their engineering comprehension is no question

This long-standing team shines bright and helps other teams shine bright as well. Don’t let their shark tank scare you, this team swims like Woodie. Let’s take a MOEment to recognize the Miracle Workerz

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This group of mechanics uses a proven method to lift their robot. They jacked up the cage to reach new heights without a doubt. This group of gamers and lawyers does not mess around.

This robot was robust, clean, and elegantly designed. Their un-dead axle uniquely and cleanly integrated multiple functions into their robot. Their unique and innovative design shows that they can either 'find a way or make one'.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team is light on their feet. Their awareness of where they are in space and on the field is apparent as they orbit around the reef. This team has no problem flying close to the sun.

Like coordinated drones, this team’s robot is controlled through their field-centric location system. Their accurate L4 auto was no “moon shot”. During tele-op, their obsessive de-TECtion for reef pipes set them apart.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team is well-organized with strong leadership and a focus on the water theme. They focus on wellness when the competition makes them pucker. The juice from this team never sours.

This team spreads FIRST by starting teams, running impactful events including LEGO drives, and helping girl scouts earn STEM badges. They help make STEM accessible to a continuum of ages, starting with preschoolers, offer multilingual resources and measure EVERYTHING. They are an inspiring advocate for increasing opportunities by procuring STEM spaces, filling the void at local libraries, partnering with sponsors to offer internships, and advocating with their school district and local and regional politicians.
This team's profound love for engineering LOOMS large. Wherever they step, others follow. This team's recent impact is TITANIC.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team's bot is as robust as a HIVE This team designed a light-weight solution to a TALL problem. This team really STUNG the competition with BARBARA.

This team integrates safety with their community involvement. They worked with their chief mentor and members to ensure that everyone is certified in CPD, FIRST aid, and use of an AED. If your robot catches on fire these FIRST Responders will be there to help.

This team is already preparing for their return as seniors next year. FRC is a chaotic place, with so much to learn, but this team has been preparing all school year: building hovercraft and hacking power wheels!

This second year team was able to obtain two new 3-D printers and significant support. The students in their pale blue shirts reminded the judges of rising to the sky. The judges are inspired by the magnificent and impressively excellent Blue Streaked team.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has a focus on the long term with their outreach and recruitment efforts. They make an effort to improve their environment, with projects for recycling and pollinator gardens. To cap it off, their beanies can be seen all over the pits, covering their spare parts!
This team started the day landing on their FEET. They united teams through their button bracket. This team approached the day with feline FUR-osity
This team performed with METRONOME-LIKE consistency. Their entire process was built to handle the SHEER FORCES of competition. As a team, their design came together with a single PULSE.

This team has riveted FIRST core values to their very foundation. Their practice field became home to many teams in their regional alliance. They make great efforts to steel their neighbors for the competition.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team's robot had a creative feature that stood out in the vastness of SPACE. They overcame a challenge by creating a custom controller to steer their SHIP. The judges think you should give their stellar controller a SPIN.

This team used years of vision to put the game in their crosshairs. Their redundant systems and labeling RUNES ensured their machine would be mobile on the field, and repairable in the pit. Their attention to Quality forged a robot as strong as THOR's hammer

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team has shown innovation through the design of a terrific robot through a variety of notable design choices including in their game piece manipulation and a unique use of machine-operator communication. Their tenacious spirit has been easy to see and they have taken a BYTE out of the competition.

When scoring in the reef, it's sometimes hard to SEE. With fully autonomous movement, this team takes the lead. Using cameras to align, and controlled by a BUTTON BOX, the auto award goes to the ossing o-bots!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: These animals are showing off their cute and cuddly theming. With their mascot visible through facepaint, passing down their team stuffed animal, as well as their beautifully painted reefscape and GLITTER robot, this team is thundering through the pit area and playfield.

This team proves that good things come in small packages and decided that building robots was not enough. With outreach that spans galaxies, or at least New Jersey, they have truly left an impact that’s out of this world. They have mastered “learning under nurturing adults” proving that mentorship and innovation go hand in hand. Get ready to cheer for the unstoppable force that is the Lunatecs!
With many new initiatives this season, in their team and community other teams are certainly green with envy.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: With a comprehensive design, multiple prototypes, and a clean build this team sprung into action
This team is swerving on the right path and spreading their wings to a bright future
With their business plan they started with the end in mind. RAY a Drop of Golden Sun….
When faced with challenges, it’s best to not be alone. By banding together with their pack their team has certainly grown

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Their fight to preserve the longevity of their team is the hall mark of these crusaders with extensive recruiting and training initiatives
By setting off on a QUEST this team found a way to boost morale and build friendships. The are definitely “or-canna need a bigger bot” contain their spirit
This team is characterized by clearly defined plan and documentation at every stage of their design and build process. Archimedies would be proud of their ALPHA BETA approach
Working side by side to help a new team have a successful start their support and work space made a huge dufference. It’s obvious the this team does not SEA HORSE arround

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team looked at their existing methods and decided to pivot their approach. With their innovative hang design they found themselves gradually rising out of the reef’s grasp.
With CNC milled parts to picture perfect wiring this team built a high quality robot. The judges give a big TIP OF THE HAT to this quality organization

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This robot navigates the sea with control from point to point. With speed and laser precision they catch and release coral to repair the reef.
While other creatures drifted in the current, this team locked onto the reef. This robot keeps going on it’s own even when superman would be stopped

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team fully embraced their underwater theme. From their robot to their pit and swag these nautical adventures are identified this season by their octopus friends

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Event
records.script: This team exemplifies FIRST values through mentorship, outreach and community service that spans continents. Their impact reaches from Kenya to local hospitals, changing lives through STEM kits, adaptive technology and hundreds of meals for those in need. These legendary fighters truly live to their motto of finding a way or make one.

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Event
records.script: Casting a wide net, this team has reached new depths of engagement. They are inspiring guppies to have megalodon dreams. A wellspring of passion for engineering, congratulations to SCH 1218

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Event
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Don't let this robots clean and neat image fool you. Mechanical prowess and impressive automation creates an innovative design. This team's immaculate process won't leave your brain "fried"

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Event
records.script: On a whim this group of STEM aficionados joined FIRST with a failed grant. With a ghost of a chance of a second year, they dove into the pool of FIRST Uplifted by Gracious Professionalism, they learned how to cultivate sponsors and a future. The judges award for "Fro Ad Hoc to Forever" goes to team 10070, the Ghost Bots

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Event
records.script: These rookies embraced the "each one - teach one" philosophies and this reflected in the pit and on the field. These judges were amazed to find this rookie team helping in other pits with the expertise they gained over the season. This team is RAMp-ing up to a bright future. Congratulations to team 10584, Pennridge RobotRams

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Event
records.script: Having setbacks is a part of life, but those who persist through those challenges will shine. This team rose to the challenge of starting from scratch to rebuild. From one lone wolf to a pack, congratulations, to team 5407!

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Event
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has been planting their seeds for success They keep their team's fire with community events, fundraising, and internships Lets all toast this team with a tall glass of lemonade.

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Event
records.script: From their all around solid robot to their positive atitudes, this team stood tall to the competition. We all saw these birds of a feather flock to gether. The judges were tickled pink with their recycled pit display.

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Event
records.script: This team is an animal charging through the pack with strong documentation and iterative design. Their two stage coral transfer wowed the judges. The score faster than you can say "MOOOOOSSSSEEE"

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Event
records.script: There are plenty of fish in the sea, but this team stands out for GP. From frolicking in the meadow, to reaching new depths, this team has a positive relationship with the whole animal kingdom. Near and DEER to the FIRST community, congratulations to BambiBotz! 4637

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Event
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: They've worked all day and night This team knows it's left from it's right It's a great robot, not powered by steam There is "currently" no "Alternate" to this team

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Event
records.script: This robot has explored the reef with their first rate machine, reaching new heights while the sharks circled. Every part had it's place, with careful consideration for material selections. Even superman would be proud. Congratulationhs team 2539, The Krypton Cougars.

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Event
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team dove into the coral and algae with a clear plan for success. With limelights and beam breaks, and a clean program plan, they scare high in both auto and tele-op. Who knew that flowers could grow under water?

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Event
records.script: This team's automation makes playing the game look easy. They hopped through autonomous to their automations in teleop with ease. They are able to effectively score coral from down under to "jumping to the very top" Congratulations to team 4373, Roobotics

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Event
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team really “dove” into the game to show us the world under the waves. With “Pool noodles” cut fancier than “New Poodles” in their pit, the devil is truly in the details. Congratulations Team 4342, Demon Robotics.

The team has demonstrated an exception a commitment to make a significant impact on the community. They have mentored multiple FLL teams, supported other FRC teams and has opened their facilities to the FIRST community Their outreach resulted in initiating new local and international FIRST teams. You don’t have to worry about getting stung by these yellow jackets.

This team’s scholarship fund and summer camp LIGHT the way for the next generation to SOAR into STEM. Their off season event fans the flames of opportunity for girls in FIRST. Through these sustained efforts, they prove when you fuel the fire for women in STEM, the future looks brighter for us all.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Keep it simple Stan Their check lists keep things on the rails Their build is tight and clean. Berserkers, they are not!
This returning team looks to find joy in many places. Like a good detective, they search high and low to support STEM. 🎶Where in the world is Carmen San Diego?🎶

These rookies continue to bridge the gap for future team members by planning grants to start new programs. They have overcome failures and refocused after repairs, flying straight as an arrow to hit their mark.

This young team joined by their new friends learned there is joy in setbacks. Rising from there, this team recruits new team members by running an IT club and emphasizing the importance of cyber-security, Reusing 99% of their robot material from previous years, this young fawn is a role model bot for young teams.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Their team structure allowed them to navigate difficulties and celebrate their successes. They battled against adversity with resilience and determination, turning challenges into opportunities for growth. Congratulations team 2554, the Warhawks!
This team makes everyone feel welcomed and valued. Their quest inspires camaraderie and school pride. The spirit award is O “FISH” ally here. Congrats team 6808, William Tennet Robotics
They CAN Bus kinda strong Their tower leans right, it ain’t wrong They follow a process, its’ written down, When they’re on the field they go to town!

This team knows the best way to navigate the FRC wilderness is together. With collaboration in mind, they charge ahead providing support to teams in need and assisting young FLL and FTC programs. It’s no Bullwinkle that this team is FIRST core values in Action.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: The judges were impressed by this team’s approach to game piece acquisition, thinking outside just nuts and bolts. While many teams focused on a single intake system, this team doubled down with a 2nd, which ensured greater redundancy and more adaptability on the field. Congrats team 9116, The Canucks and Bolts

This team’s minimalistic approach ensures simplicity and reliability By utilizing space above and below, they avoid complexity and allow easy access for wire management. Their relentless TESTING has obviously paid off.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team has sharp vision, using multiple cameras to swarm the field with control. Their control system is all the buzz, with their automatic precision – no target is safe! With a hive full of innovation, they bring a sting of brilliance
Using Multiple Sensors this team understands time is of the essence. Running fast they gallop through autonomous. There’s nothing horsey about these Mustangs.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Not only does this team have fish in their name, they have FIRST core values in their REEF emphasizing and inspiring their incoming team members. With Fish on their robot, their aquarium comes to life with a focused perspective, possibly for Finding the Beta.

Reaching oceans around the world, this team has spread the FIRST Mission to over 65 teams, across all programs. Ensuring the survival of the FIRST reef, they advocate new policy, from the school board, all the way to Washington DC, supporting other teams to do the same. Diving into unique partnerships impacting the future of all students, this red bird RISES like the tide.

No physical or geographical barrier stood in the way of this team’s impact on FIRST communities. CONQUERING the competition, this team is spreading the FIRST mission across civilizations near and far. Vanquishing programming impediments for the visually impaired, they are building a future where robotics are within reach for everyone, everywhere. We are GREEN with inspiration for these SPARTAN warriors.

The judges were DEVOURED by this team, with the vast number of outreach programs in their local community. Advocating for new STEM facilities. Giving away STEM kits. Cleaning local beaches. Forming the Portland Alliance. Feeling the Music partnering with the Oregon School for the Deaf. Raising $102,000 for Code Can Dance. And these only scratch the surface of this team’s 49 MONSTROUS initiatives and growth. They are BRIDGING THE GAPS and keeping STEM afloat through a lasting legacy of outreach.

This team builds on their already sustained outreach initiatives. They continued their momentum by running workshops on how to run LEGO camps, starting Unified Robotics teams, advocating for an EV curriculum in their CTE program, and even POUNCING on efforts to start FIRST programs in other countries. While encompassed by the ocean, this team doesn’t deter their effort that BUILDS good people.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: With their extensive collection of notebooks, this team found a simple idea can last all season long. The judges MARVELED at their simple arm’s pin point accuracy. There’s no hiding this team’s industrial might in the SHADOWS.
