records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Apollo Division
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Through structured week-long camps, this team raises substantial funds to support the team’s growth and longevity. Their unique low-cost experimental bot not only drives cleaner surroundings, but also provides a training ground for aspiring fresh FRC members. This team is a dynamite when it comes to supporting sustainability programs.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Apollo Division
records.script: This team didn’t just walk the plank — they built it, voted on it, and cheered each other across it with unwavering enthusiasm. From a net-covered pit to a button-filled treasure chest and a robot blooming with teamwork, their shipshape spirit sails through every detail.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Apollo Division
records.script: Like a majestic robotic bird, this team soars through the skies with incredible agility and precision. Their 15 pound shute allows them to cut through the competition. Their simplicity of manufacturing and all-hands-on-deck approach to helping results in an elegantly designed robot.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Apollo Division
records.script: This team has truly displayed FIRST core values both on and off the field, providing crucial resources for other teams and demonstrating openness to everyone. Their unwavering support and energy in the stands brightened this FRC competition event.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Apollo Division
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team engineered a solution so precise, even tension couldn’t resist. Their belt system adjusts like clockwork - flawless, silent, and unstoppable! They also happen to believe that the path to innovation is paved with cheesecake!

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Apollo Division
records.script: This team has a long arm made of custom parts. Their design process applies a strong force to create a robust machine. The product of the two results in a quality iteration cycle that could turn the entire state of Texas.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Apollo Division
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: A combination of sensors and smart code kept this team’s robot from rising against them. Their custom control board, indicator LEDs, dynamic localization, and accurate elevator showed master of control. Filtering out rebellious data helped localize this team into the top of the rankings.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Apollo Division
records.script: When the match starts, this team dives in head first - no drivers, no problems! They make waves with every autonomous move. With their lightweight, tough composite material and a combination of telemetry and odometry, their auto is so lightning fast, even the fish stop to watch! This team charged to the top of the leaderboard.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Apollo Division
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s aesthetics took wing—soaring through the season with a visual style that couldn’t be missed. With LED-lit bots, precision 3D prints, and red, black, and white ‘flight packs’ that uplift young minds, their cohesive look was anything but ruffled. This team’s branding truly soared above the flock—proof that great design is for the birds… of prey.

Making an impact on younger students is the foundation of this team to spark curiosity and innovation. They have spread their wings and inspired teams globally by in-person and Zoom calls This team soared above and beyond in the FIRST program by competing in FLL, FTC, and FRC throughout their time together and are exploring distant waters around the world. Judges are excited to see these eaglets take flight!

This team is an animal on and off the field. They continue to support new teams in their community. The team loves to pounce on opportunities to advocate for STEAM with local and state government authorities.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team demonstrated an exceptional balance between form function and aesthetics creating a robot that stands out for both its design and performance. This teams robot is cooking upon closer inspection judges were impressed with their 3D printed components. While some other teams opted for coral only their recipe for success with was both algae and coral. Tying it all together is a sophisticated differential gear system allowing their intake to seamlessly collect game pieces for from both the ground and the human player station.

This team exemplifies everything FIRST stands for and is consistently helping to spread FIRST values both near and far. From hosting and volunteering at multiple FLL and FTC events, to using their self-built T-shirt cannon to promoting their team at pep rallies and STEM events. Who doesn’t LOVE a good “tick…tick…BOOM!” This teams wide reaching “doodle bot” program has provided robot kits around the world.

Through their determination and creativity, and their never give up attitude, they forged their path and made their presence known. Empty seats at the round table didn’t stay empty for long as they dubbed a new mentor to assist in the quest for excellence. They brought their knight “No Code” to the tournament.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team is one of the only FIRST teams in their area but that will not be the case for long if they have anything to say about it. They have started the process of building up a thriving FLL in their area ensuring a pipeline of future FRC members, engineers and leaders. Their commitment to their community, from food drives to reduced/reuse/recycle initiative is something all teams can learn from.

The students make waves spreading the spirit of FIRST in their community by hosting FIRST events. They stand out with their “Make it Loud” chants, as bright and bold as a coral reef. Their energy serves as a rising tide, as they sparkle in the stands. They never miss a chance to “Seas – the moment”

The team demonstrated exceptional engineering excellence through their relentless, improvement process, returning their coral ejector design to maximize efficiency and functionality. Their algae gripper was engineered with precision to eliminate any wasted movement, enabling it to score coral and collected algae seamlessly on a single motion. They developed a custom swerve module specifically designed for max swerve, used by Rev Robotics making their robot charge all the way.

This team consistently shows the values of Gracious Professionalism everywhere they go. By making their machine shop & practice field available to other teams, to always coming prepared with spare parts should another team be in need both locally and internationally. Their mobile pit assistance crew, the “Robo-medics” come to competitions ready to help any team in need.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Somebody call the governor; their bot swims with speed that is inversely proportional to the relative height of their elevator. With their giant pincer, they process both coral and algae as if it were the “claw of life”. In the end, their magnetism gives them a lift.

This rural team of Texans makes waves and leaves no level 2 coral uncovered. Their bot has an exit velocity…but it’s classified. In true Texas fashion, they set the gold metal standard for consistency and accuracy.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Bringing light to the bottom of the ocean, this school of fish work together like a herd. They had a practical and effective mechanism to place coral accurately and repeatably on the field of play. The sun doesn’t set on their teamwork and innovation.

Demonstrating consistent high performing programming operations, pushes the programming auton to deep waters. Swimming with the competition, the team added additional components above the average school of fish, writing code to create a special recipe. Cooking up a storm from the bottom of the ocean, they spiced up the competition with their flaming auton.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team sparkles from tip to tail and from the stands to the field. Jumping through space, this team used their fin to navigate the waters of Reefscape. Porpoise-ly designed their look, feel and inspiration launches them into excellence of space.
This team has a real passion for showing that STEM is for everyone. They make a strong case for not just helping other teams, but finding fresh ways to keep FIRST thriving for all. The verdict is in!

This team made creating swerve drive a plug and play! They helped multiple FLL and FTC teams and held off season competitions in their area.They have inspired many students into engineering both online and in person by showcasing their bot in multiple community events. Giddy up!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This robot is a true testament to innovation and functionality--sleek, efficient, and practical. With its impressive gold & white design, this bot is built to perform and shine. It's so clean, you could eat off it!

From beginning to end, this team has done it all and still craves more to do. From training new members to volunteering at food banks, they snaked through their community to spread the FIRST spirit. Expect more great things to come from this team-the cycle begins anew!

Although this team has only been around for a few seasons, they have already grown their team by 400%! They exhibit the mission and principles of FIRST and have inspired many to pursue STEM paths. Rising all the way from the pineapple under the sea, this team will continue to soar!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has grown fast, rising to the heights of this competition not just on their star skills, but by nurturing their new talent at home. They have a whole robot at home to train their new members, and their upperclassmen are committed to making everybody shine as bright as possible. Hey now! Welcome the winner of the sustainability award.

This team brings energy, enthusiasm, and unity wherever they go, making their presence known both on and off the field. With their unwavering camaraderie, they embody the spirit of teamwork and competition, always cheering loud & proud in their signature cowboy hats. Their passion and dedication shine just as bright as their purple and gold.

This team embodies consistency and cost efficiency, CHARGING forward with determination to tackle every challenge. They planned their design to repurpose past robots and create a reliable, high-performing machine. Their smart engineering, persistence, and strategic approach helps them RAM through the competition.

This team's namesake is known in the wild as a solitary predator. However, their robotic counterparts are far from that! You can often find them and their positive attitudes graciously lending a helping hand to others, both here and away from competition.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team took a calculated approach, strategically designing a solution that set them apart. Their ingenuity wasn't random--it was the result of deliberate planning, innovation, and a little bit of...dare we say...villain-level brilliance. With every move, they demonstrated control, precision, and a clear trajectory toward competitive excellence.

This team has crafted a machine with the precision of a NASA mission. Their attention to detail ensures every system functions flawlessly, just like a well-calibrated spacecraft ready for launch. With rock-solid reliability and out-of-this-world engineering, they have set the gold standard for quality. Mission Control, we have a winner!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team identified their weaknesses and innovated to overcome and succeed. They focused their efforts to create a better design and address unmet challenges. They went against the grain to engineer better and unique solutions to control and understand their machine.

This team approaches their autonomous with precision and adaptability, ensuring their bot navigates and scores with ease. With two cameras and flexibility to operate from either side, they run up the score during autonomous mode! Their auto is able to see every angle and adjust to any challenge, making their robot LIGHT UP the field!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team spends most of its time on the high seas. From their pits, to their bot, to their outfits at competition, they are iconic! Their bot's namesake may have sunk, but it was reborn as a reef in the ocean and on the field!

Having a strong community outreach program is "PARAMOUNT" to this team. Some of their accomplishments can actually be put on a marquee and shown to the world!! I can...., you can...., we can..., BUT THESE ladies REALLY can! Congratulations team 2881, Lady Cans!

This team inspires us all to explore the boundaries of what is possible. Freely sharing platforms and tools, their meteoric influence can be felt miles away. With their help, "EVERY-BOTTY" has a chance to shoot for the stars! Congratulations team 118, Robonauts

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team knows more about branding than cattle farmers. In their CAD, their prototype and even in their toolboxes, you know they prioritize Form, Fit and Function when you see them. Straight out of the Jimi Hendrix Experience, it's Purple Haze!

When faced with challenges, this team effortlessly flowed to the top. They didn’t rely on tentacles to grab attention—it was their engaging interactions with the judges, captivating imagery, and boundless creativity that stood out. Congratulations to Team 8370 Glow With The Flow on their remarkable achievement!

Their enthusiasm will draw you in. They reached out and amassed from the community via Tik-Tok and Tutoring. I see great things on their event horizon. Our rookie all-stars are Team 10032, Singularity!

This small, community-focused team, established only a few years ago, has demonstrated remarkable growth and ENERY. With unwavering support from their mentors, they have successfully WORKED various programs to inspire children both during the season and offseason. Their exceptional ability to adapt, innovate, and uplift others truly distinguishes them. Congratulations to Team 9054, Johnson City Joules, for earning the Rising All-Star Award!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team's value grows over time. With outreach programs, information sharing and multiple teams, every part is recycled. Team 2468. we appreciate you for making robotics fun and sustainable! Congratulations!

This small team is really making a honk! They're Getting loud and supporting their 12-student team in the stands and in their Treehouse No one is Recoiling at this team's spirit! Congratulations to Team 9577 Recoil

Effectively following the engineering design process, from conception to a fully developed solution, this team offers many elegant options on the field of play. A unique coral intake that can ingest and rotate in one movement, along with a fault tolerant drive system clearly demonstrates a well engineered system that makes others green with envy. Congratulations to Team 624, CRyptonite!

Though their travel time was brief, their commitment to making a difference was undeniable. Just ask the volunteers, who were quick to recognize this team’s exceptional contribution to the competition. Forget the secret codes and conspiracies—these foil hats can’t hide the gracious professionals this team displayed before and during competition.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Intentionally designed for innovation in multiple areas including a one-button driver assist based system on cascade elevation, and an out-of-this-world “ET” solution for handling algae. The magic they use seems more like what you would expect from the sorcerer than the under-study. Their repeated success in autonomous multi-scores will ensure sunny days ahead for Mr Crab. Congratulations to Team Apprentice 2687.

With algae in hand, they take their stance, Over the barge—nothing left to chance. Precision, power, quality supreme, From downtown, they launch—like Kobe and Curry’s dream! And now, the moment we can’t ignore, The Quality Award—it's yours to score!" Congratulations Team 8576, Golden Warrior Robotics

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team will be the first to great you with a cheerful hello. They have creatively combined a donut hole and lightweight lunar technology. Beyond the code and mechanics, this teams showed what FRC is all about: innovation, passion, and a relentless drive to improve. From their first simulation to the launching of their siren, the Howdy Bots are making a splash.

Their use of gyroscopes, encoders, and custom-tuned PID control allowed for seamless navigation and fine alignment in autonomous and tele-operations. This teams is as fearless as a viper and strikes just as fast. Their flawless autonomous operations set the stage for victory in every match. Congratulations Team sixty-eight: HUNDRED!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Some teams compete with style -- this one rules the seas, harnessing the strength of a shark, the cunning of an octopus, and the spirit of the deep sea horse. Their imagery is a force of nature—bold, unforgettable, and as powerful as the waves. For their striking identity and artistic mastery, we proudly present the Imagery Award to… Team 9311 ( Warhorse Robotics)

This team exemplifies FIRST ideals and excels in all aspects of spreading the FIRST mission, impacting their community, inspiring the future, and leaving a legacy. This team has started, mentored, and supported teams across all programs. Their camps and training help ensure that STEM skills are imparted to the next generation, fueling their pipeline from FLL to FRC and beyond. Their advocacy at the local and regional levels, as well as extensive inclusive programming, ensures all voices are heard. This team’s approach to recruiting and mentorship has a proven track record and looks to the future - the seeds planted now blossom into the skills our future leaders need.

This team’s sharp vision feeds the future of STEM with K through 6 camps, mentoring an FLL team, and training new members in CAD, Electronics, and Java. They lend a wing to neighboring and rookie teams. Their nest is full with two clutches, ready to sink a Talon into STEM.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team’s robot demonstrated an elegant, practical design. The team’s clear branding and deliberate design choices are evident in their final product. The judges didn’t need to wrangle with this decision!

This team is on route for greatness as they bring to life their community and peers. These newest patriots call their team to action, exemplifying the principles of FIRST. From Friend to FOE, let’s all catch the bus with them!

From their bot to their branding, these rookies have the maturity of a veteran team. Breaking the mold by starting in the off season has helped push these All Stars to the top. Straight from their neighborhood garage, these Rebels with a cause will prosper for years to come.

The rising sun guides this team on their travels east. This up-and-coming team is one to watch, spreading STEM and acting as role models to future generations. Checking the map to find their place, Robot X marks the spot for this rising star!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: From the metal of bots of FRC years past, this team has set up their bots for success for many years to come. Full of compassion to those in need, this team has also set up cell phone recycle campaigns for victims of domestic violence. Can you hear us now?
This team shows spirit no matter what hand they're dealt. Off season or on, they are suited up and ready to jump into action to face many challenges! Join their game and play those wild cards!

This team has an extremely well-rounded robot backed by a strong engineering process. Functional and practical, elegant and advantageous, this bot has it all! When it comes to autonomous, tele-op, or end game, their blacked-out bot soars across the field.

From hosting FLL events to regularly helping other teams here and around the world, this team continuously conquers the FIRST core values of Gracious Professionalism. You will definitely know this team by their positivity and willingness to help anyone and everyone. These Vikings of grace exemplify gracious professionalism as a role model for all teams.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Creativity in hardware and software design to solve problems and enhance strategic play has helped this team prosper on the field. This team has fielded an efficient, accurate, and well-controlled robot. Their techno-skills are evident in their design.

This team has built a bot to withstand the rigors of competition. From Tennessee to Texas, their exceptional wire and cable management led to a robust bot from concept to build. With a solid build structure, this camo-clad team has built a world class robot!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team controls their robot smoothly while still being forceful. Don’t get caught staring while they look in two different directions. The judges loved their dual cameras processing multiple bytes of information.

This team built a robot that enjoys scoring points all by itself. Ask this bot yourself, “Can you consistently place coral at Level 4, up to 3 times in 15 seconds?” This bot would answer, “Yes, It Can!”

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team did a wonderful job prepping their robot and team for this season. Their magnetic personalities helped the judges appreciate the beauty of their design. Whether baseball or keeping the peace, these rangers really shine.

This team is always ready to Ride to the Rescue! With over 10,000 outreach hours, this team has done a lot to help their local community and the broader FIRST community. They've mentored over a dozen teams and have been seen helping many of the teams competeing at this event, but the highlight has to be their effort developing open-source libraries for programming Swerve Drives; helping to advanced innovation & collaboration for the entire FIRST community. With their Giddy up & Go, this team will paint the world orange! It is our honor to announce this year’s FIRST Impact Award goes to Team 3481 – Bronc Bots!

This team’s outreach efforts have truly taken flight, soaring to new heights in STEM education. Their summer camps and resource-sharing initiatives have hatched a generation of eager learners, now spreading their wings in leadership roles. With an eagle-eyed focus on community impact they have created a nest of innovation. congratulations to team 5427.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Immaculate, shining red pillars rise from this team’s Bot. With nary a wire in sight, expertly crafted components swiftly secure an algae, continuing upward to score a coral in one stroke. Their camouflage cannot hide their elegant and efficient solutions in their own home town. Congratulations to FRC 5572, Rosbots!

This team would not let their small numbers keep them from the competition. With scarse resources and ingenuity, they incorporated scrap wood and spare parts to build a unique robot for this year's game. This robots unique features caught the judges attention and they would like to “axe” everyone to join us in congratulating Team 9664 The Lumberjacks.

This team powered up themselves with outreach, enthusiasm, and a drive to grow—after engaging new students through a 4-H camp, they doubled their size, and made giant leaps in just one year. Always eager to learn, connect, and spread positivity, their energy is as unstoppable as their recruitment efforts and community impact. With a smile as bright as their mascot, Captain Smiley, let’s celebrate the rising all-stars of our event—Team 9444, Perseverance!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Some teams build robots—this team takes things apart to build a future! By collecting broken technology, they teach young minds the power of reverse engineering, sustainability, and creativity; all while salvaging parts for their own engineering projects. Keeping their knowledge strong with peer training and cloud-based documentation, this team proves that sustainability isn’t just about recycling—it’s about reusing, repurposing, and reimagining robotics for generations to come—let’s hear it for Team 8088, Bionic Panthers

This team’s spirit rises from the depths and can’t be contained! With their standout tutus and bubbly bucket hats, you can spot them from across the venue no sonar required! Their team pride runs deep, and their enthusiasm creates waves that ripple through the entire event. For their unstoppable energy, and ability to rally everyone around them, the Team Spirit Award goes to team 2582

This team’s advantages rack up on the field because of the work done at home. These kids worked so hard to get to “Power On” Day but their plan does not stop there. Their colorful prints help collect coral and adjustments made after testing are putting their opponents in a vortex. Congratulations to FRC 3735, VorTX!

This team embodies the Grrrrracious professionalism. From keeping the cubs happy to lending a helping paw, these techs helped make this event a more enjoyable experience. It is our great honor to award team 4610 Beartecs with the Gracious Professionalism award!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team ultimately left the judges glued to their seats with an innovative and cost-effective design. They found an issue with the grip of their wheels and designed and 3d-printed their own to improve their performance on the field. If you mess with the bot you’re gonna get the bull, congratulations team 7521 Ultimate Robotics!

This team did not bolt from the planning and manufacturing needed to build a robust robot. Their high expectations and care to not “ohm”-mit any detail during design has allowed them to overcome any resistance to excellence. Congratulations to 231 High Voltage.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team took the the task of elevator-position-accuracy head on and developed control technology to provide millimeter level accuracy and improve scoring. Their innovative idea to add LED lights to the elevator frames is useful to the operator for situational awareness and also a delight to the audience when it lights up!!! Kudos for implementing a robust Kalman filter and PID controller using the Encoder data for accurate positioning. Congratulations team 1164, Project NEO

With explosive energy and astronomical coding, this team flew above the rest with their amazing autonomous. Finding their way through space using their ‘Lauch Pad’ to secure the win. By pushing one button makes their ship move by itself. It’s not rocket science that we chose team 8114, Rocketteers.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Stepping into this team’s pit felt like diving beneath the waves, surrounded by an immersive underwater world where every detail flowed seamlessly together. Their creativity and attention to theme transformed their space into a deep-sea spectacle, making it clear they weren’t just any ordinary team they were bringing visitors straight to Bikini Bottom! For making a splash with their imaginative and well-executed design, the Imagery Award goes to team 4332

This energetic team, driven by force and determination, is expanding their barrier reef with diverse aquatic adventures. From hosting FLL camps and supporting teams, to community outreach such as shelters and toy drives, they innovate new initiatives that make STEAM accessible for the FIRST community and beyond. This team has made an outstanding IMPACT on the STEAM community. With the twisting force to overcome any challenge, they thrive in the realm of helping others through their extensive and well-rounded initiatives. Their efforts ensure that the spirit of innovation and collaboration continues to grow and flourish.

When aspiring minds want to join the exciting world of STEAM but other activities get in the way, the Greeks ensure they make a way! With the determination of ancient warriors and the precision of modern robotics, they clear the path for future engineers. They are Inspiring Engineering near and far!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team’s design stood strong like a shield, built with modularity that allowed them to adapt to any challenge. Their elevator system wasn’t just engineered—it was overengineered, standing as a testament to their relentless pursuit of excellence. And through an iterative build process, they honed their machine like a blade, refining each element until it was battle-ready. With unwavering dedication and fearless innovation, this team has truly earned their name.

This team came out of the gate running, showing incredible growth and determination since last season. They’ve worked tirelessly to improve their skills and build a stronger, more cohesive team. Not only have they enhanced their robot, but they’ve also created a supportive environment where girls play a key role in every aspect of their design, driving innovation and teamwork. This team is galloping toward success, earning the Judges Award for their impressive growth and their inspiring commitment to inclusivity and teamwork!

This team has quickly risen as a force in robotics, growing from a small community team to an official school program with its own dedicated class. In just their second year, they've gone from relying on others for support to giving back, making robotics more accessible by lowering fees and inspiring younger students with their memorable name. Their commitment to inclusivity shines through initiatives like Derby Girls, encouraging more young women to explore the world of STEM.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team soars to new heights of sustainability by fostering long-term engagement in STEM through mentoring, camps, and events for students of all ages and abilities. By supporting other teams, hosting inclusive STEAM initiatives, and providing robot kits to underserved areas, they ensure the growth of robotics education beyond their local community. Their eagle-eyed dedication to inspiring future innovators creates a lasting impact, building a strong foundation for the next generation of engineers and problem solvers.

IS THAT THUNDER OR JUST TEAM CHEERING? This team's passion and electrifying energy have amplified the atmosphere of this entire competition! From the pits to the playing field, their enthusiasm has been tightened down with precision—no loose screws here! Their vibrant spirit has everyone seeing purple, and their support for fellow competitors proves they've mastered the perfect balance of intensity and sportsmanship that never comes unthreaded!

As explorers of the unknown, this team boldly reached for the stars from the very start of the season. They demonstrated a truly professional approach to the design process, meticulously testing and refining every detail of their robot. Through a combination of precise engineering and innovative solutions, they built a machine that was as reliable as it was powerful, pushing the boundaries of what was possible. This team has successfully launched their way to victory, earning the Excellence in Engineering Award for their exceptional design and dedication to precision engineering!

When support is needed, whether for mechanics or health, this team consistently has a NUMBER of members stepping. A dedicated crew of members always steps up, ready to lend a hand. They embody Gracious Professionalism both on and off the field.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team rocketed into the build season thinking outside the box. Demonstrating exceptional ingenuity with their robot design, they stepped into intense competition with a swagger. Their climb design demonstrates both the Direction and MMMAGNITUDE of the team’s creative vision. OH YEAH! It’s VECTORRRR!!

The judges loved how this team built a robot that executed on its design goals. Alternating between a consistent rugged design and high performance, this robot surges through competition with confident power. Watt team is it? HIIIIIIGH VOOOLTAGE!!!!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: By crafting minimal, modular software components early on, this team sparks innovation and encourages seamless collaboration, even among junior members. As these components SWIRL together, they form a cohesive, functional solution—an inventive and unique strategy for conquering the intricate challenges of robotics.

CORAL-LING ALL ROBOTICS FANS! This team's autonomous precision was nothing short of spectacular! Their robot executes level 4 coral placements with such reliability, you'd think it was hardwired to perfection. They've decoded the secret to autonomous excellence, and their performance has left the competition being green with envy!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Embarking on a grand voyage, this team is set to navigate uncharted waters of adventure and discovery. With their trusty "ship", they are ready to explore new horizons. Their vibrant Mascot, Pit, Robot, and the enthusiastic Members come together in a harmonious blend of creativity and camaraderie, showcasing a unified and friendly spirit. Together, they are prepared to conquer any challenge that comes their way!

TOGETHER, this team ran and hosted events and camps to support their FIRST community. EVERYONE on this team strives to be inclusive and inspiring to others. ACHIEVING excellence meant more than just robots as they raised funds to support their initiatives. MORE languages than just English, this team is a powerhouse and role model for FIRST in their region.

This team’s appreciation for engineering has been fruitful! They kept their eyes peeled for opportunities to increase FIRST participation in their community. They have proven that these raccoons can find innovation even in the trash can!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team went all in on their bot. Their design process paid off in a compact and effective grappling arm. This team put all their chips in Industrial Design.
Fundraising is their route to community success. Camps create a pipeline for younger students, while the robotics team gives students new trade and life skills. Hop on route 44 with us!
This team broke through the barriers of being a small timer. They showed persistence, teamwork, and involvement in their community. They are cycling up into the role of Rookie All-Star!

This team’s service has been crucial to ensuring that everyone has the tools they need to succeed. Co-opertition is their team drive. They soldiered through their challenges and can always be counted on to give a helping hand.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team increased their herd by inviting fellow lambs into their team pipeline. They know the key to sustainability is to train the younger generations with new skills. With their EV charges at their international school, they are sustaining their environment in addition to their team!
This team showed great spirit on and off the field. Their loud roars echoed in the stands. They cheered their team on to victory!

This team approached the design process with a strategic edge. Their use of automated systems enhanced their driver’s ability to perform on the field. This team has a blend of ancient warrior spirit and modern technology.
When someone is in need, this team hops on over. They love to help other teams, and members in their community. This team jumps right in to Gracious Professionalism.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This bot’s frugality and spare parts gave it nine lives. Simple and unique, their grapple lifted straight and high. This team pounced on creativity!
When the music started, their bot sparkled. Checklists and redundancy gave them strong dancefloor moves. This team’s discography is full of quality hits!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team supported their alliance with their fantastic control of their game pieces. With this team’s consistent auto-align, they were a force to contend with! This team applied the right torque to leave the competition spinning.
This team dives deep into programming. Their team’s robot swims fast on the field to score coral. This group of women CAN do it!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: When it comes to looks, this team saddled up and took the reins. Their streamlined look deserves a blue ribbon. They are galloping to the finish line for this award

Their workforce ready presentation was leagues above the coral reefs. Their inclusive STEM outreach in their big city and across the globe blew the judges away. Their initiatives to mentor girls and special education students in robotics, as well as mentoring teams online is truly inspiring. This team empowers students to explore and thrive in various STEM fields. Their passion and commitment to community will leave a lasting mark on FIRST. It is our honor to announce that this year’s FIRST Impact Award goes to... Team 2468 - Who do we Appreciate!

This team is so bright. It’s clear how much they care about their fellow citizens and environment. They impressed the judges with the amount of volunteer hours and their summer camp is out of this world! Advocating for STEM in Title 1 schools, their powerful voice can be heard all the way to Washington DC. Congratulations to FRC Team 1296, Full Metal Jackets.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team created synergy with functionality and efficency. By combining the ability to intake algae and coral at the same time they streamlined their design. This team delivered on harmonization of form, function, and aesthetics. Congratulations to Team 6672, Fusion Corps!

Raising all of their funding from their community, this team caught the judges' eye. They've doubled their team size through active recruiting, mentoring and fundraising for an FLL team, When it came time to choose this award, the judges certainly didn't RECOIL. Give it up for Team 9577!

Building a Team from dust requires commitment from students and the whole community, and this Team garnered both. With a competitive robot in their first season, this team didn't have to worry about rising from the ashes to continue. Watch out, this team is on fire! Team 10062, ATEMS Robotics, is our Rookie All-Star.

Even teams that have been around for years can go through a new beginning. Extreme student turnover, new leadership, and rebuilding school relationships are just some of the barriers they had to overcome. This team is breaking through the haze to become a Rising All-Star. Here's to Team 418, Purple Haze!

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: Extending their Southern hospitality, people from anywhere in their community are welcomed to this charming team. From friends of friends to farmers markets, word travels fast in the capital of Texas. Giving members full rein to wear many hats sustains a “whole ranch operation” Congratulations to Howdy Bots.

Cover your ears when this team is playing as they are L-O-U-D!!! This freshman team plays hard, wins loud, and is fun to watch! They are two protons and two Neutrons strong!!! Congratulations to team 2689, Alpha!

This team is on Fire with their redundancy and efficency. They sused a prototype robot in their engineering process and developed a singles-stage-multi-purpose coral intake solution. They cooked up a masterpiece for this award. Congratulations to team 2714, BBQ

This young team shows their true colors by helping other teams on and off the field. Their willingness to lend a helping hand or robot materials reflects their professionalism. This developmental team from Houston works to share knowledge to make everyone better. Congratulations to Photon 8515.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: When we first saw this team picking up coral off the floor we thought it was an inspried approach to save time scoring, but we were wowed by their unique camera system. While most opted for fixed solutions; this team developed a robust, articulating camera to keep track of the field. Congratulations to team 2158, the AusTIN CANs

This team stalks under the radar as they deliver robust solutions. They focused their design on modularity for support and flexibility. These innovative cats pounce on the competition. Congratulations to team 2582, the PantherBots!

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: Consistent in matches with high scoring play. This team puts coral up with ease with the help of their excellent programming; minimizing stop-to-shoot time. Their integrated controls system really helped them charge through the competion. Congratulations team 3005, the RoboChargers.

Precise movements, good balence, smooth actuations. This team lassos the posts with a copper flapper; initiating an automatic scoring routine, so their corals are spot on. Then, they dive deep at the finsh with a sensor-array-assist in their climber. Congratulations to team 148, the RoboWranglers

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Cookie Monster loves this team!! They coordinate their colorfully loud shirts, creative and bright bow ties with their highly functional and super-pink robot for a fantastic team image! Congratulations to Team 2881, the LadyCans!

This team is a pack leader, advocating for FIRST programs with local officials and legislators to ensure continued support and growth within their state. As ambassadors for FIRST, they bring STEM programs to homeless shelters and children's hospitals, leaving a lasting pawprint on their community. In addition to mentoring teams, running competitions, and starting a mental health awareness program, this team crests the hill, demonstrating their commitment to both STEM and the well-being of others.

Despite the high winds and Engineering in the dark, they are committed to bring STEM to schools and their community. Given the code name 2-3-4D HEX, they are helping build FLL, FTC and FRC teams locally. They demonstrate respect and appreciation for Engineering with their pirate ship robot captained by Jack Sparrow.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team’s combination of form and function seems almost impossible. Their racing truck-inspired electronics keep their bot as elegant as the Fibonacci sequence. There is nothing paradoxical about this team’s Industrious Design.

This team cranked up the pressure by raising coral to new heights! When they mash together, they become a combination of excellence and resilience that removes obstacles is a short amount of time. They excel not only in their design, but they spread the roots of engineering throughout their community.

Through resilience and reinvention, this team has forged a new path forward. Determining their own destiny, this self-directed and self-trained team persevered in their search for leadership. This team is a force in the making, with their dog tags and their not so dimwitted robot.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team’s flight plan assures their continued success. The recruitment and training of future team members gives them longevity. This team flies towards the sun but their innovation keeps them from burning up.

This team brings a surge of energy and enthusiasm, embodying the very equations of power in everything they do. With their unified, loud positive voice, they lead with a spirit that's as bold as the symbol of their helms. This team is ready to conquer all challenges with unyielding spirit, a proud display of crimson red, and a Viking's strength

It is obvious to anyone that has set their eyes on this robot that she is a stunningly beautiful creature. They were ruthless commanders of coral, algae, and climbing. The team schemes and designs demonstrate excellence in engineering.

This team created a stampede of positive change with their peer mentoring at schools, symposiums, and fairs. They scouted ways to help other teams struggling throughout the season with their mentorship and community. They are making a legacy of mentorship and collaboration, so we can let these mustangs run.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s design was a mythical creature before they discovered it. They swam to the island, picked up the beast, and their arm sprung them into the lead. They tamed the dragon lizard and are the kings of creativity.
Who needs luck when you’ve got a stash of spare parts, a user-friendly control panel, and eagle-eyed attention to detail. It's a sure bet they're rolling straight to the quality award.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: With their "Robots R Kool" mindset, there is a robot building army that continues to recruit. Their control PID program’s ability to swiftly plan and place coral throughout the field has been a game-changer. This team is all about designing robust, autonomous robots that have evolved over the years.

When the match started, this team was the biggest whale in town and elevated to the highest stage. Their robot needed no assistance to reach the highest level and let the points roll in. They are the high scorers and rolled ahead of the rest.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: It’s hard not to have a good time around this bright, fun-loving team. Their colorfully themed coats and hats set the gold standard for a cohesive look. Hey, what could go wrong with Oswald to bring you luck?

records.eventName: CHS District Alexandria VA Event presented by US Department of Energy
records.script: This small team has a big impact. Through a combination of tireless work in outreach, and effective advocacy this team punches above their weight. By working with local leaders this team ensures that all students in their region have access to an FLL team, while their work with leaders at the national level advocates from STEM funding across the nation. Whether it's exciting kids by building robots to smash pumpkins, or building golf robots to allow people with disabilities to play golf, this team truly lives up to their motto: "Robotics for all"

records.eventName: CHS District Alexandria VA Event presented by US Department of Energy
records.script: This team stole the show with the diversity of their outreach and commitment to their community. Through education and sustainable practices, this team keeps their hive thriving as the FRC representatives of Southern Maryland. Wanting the judges to know “we are all like this”, the Buzz was truly all about this team.

records.eventName: CHS District Alexandria VA Event presented by US Department of Energy
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team embraces an iterative design process, rigorously testing code and components to the point of failure in order to identify weak components. This robot’s fast elevator system and passthrough system keeps this jungle cat’s robot agile and competitive on the field. Caspian has been swimming around the field standing out in aesthetics and function.

records.eventName: CHS District Alexandria VA Event presented by US Department of Energy
records.script: This team impressed the judges with their unique, real-time implementation of data analysis. Their drive team was able to fly into action with a superior understanding of strategy. These buzzing bees took the sting out of statistics.

records.eventName: CHS District Alexandria VA Event presented by US Department of Energy
records.script: This tri-county team came marching in to their 2nd competition with pride. They impressed the judges with their dedication to STEM and creating a community of culturally responsible black engineers. There’s nothing to stop the Crusade of The Brave 9.

records.eventName: CHS District Alexandria VA Event presented by US Department of Energy
records.script: This team rose to compete with their robot for the first time this year. They identified their needs, sought the right mentorship and facilities to be here today. These are the Droids you’re looking for:

records.eventName: CHS District Alexandria VA Event presented by US Department of Energy
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team covered distance and time constrains with shining innovative use of resources. Meeting physically over a limited time range with minimal use of fossil fuels. This team has managed to create and operate a “super” “novel” way of sustaining a cross-county FRC program.

records.eventName: CHS District Alexandria VA Event presented by US Department of Energy
records.script: This team wowed the judges with their Friday night dinner plans, and left the judges starstruck by their enthusiasm.

records.eventName: CHS District Alexandria VA Event presented by US Department of Energy
records.script: This impressed us with their season-starting game simulation. They managed risks and mitigated them to stay sane. They are crazy about repeatable, reliable process.

records.eventName: CHS District Alexandria VA Event presented by US Department of Energy
records.script: This large team engages partner FRC programs through the pre-season, but it was their generosity and graciousness here that set them apart. This team saw a fellow competitor with an unfinished robot in parts on the floor, and sprung into action. They assembled a coalition of the willing to finish the robot, fix the code, and get their competitor scoring on the field.

records.eventName: CHS District Alexandria VA Event presented by US Department of Energy
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team has embodied the spirit of creativity with a groundbreaking solution that pushes the limits of robot design. Through rigorous prototyping, iterative testing, and a willingness to explore unconventional solutions has PUSHED this team to the top. This robot unique climbing locking mechanism shows innovation is more than just invention.

records.eventName: CHS District Alexandria VA Event presented by US Department of Energy
records.script: The judges were impressed by the attention to clean and orderly design. Their embodies beauty and quality from bumper to bumper. They tripled down on robustness and excellent design.

records.eventName: CHS District Alexandria VA Event presented by US Department of Energy
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team travels in herds but are always in control. Their unique vision and touch helps them graze the field for coral and algae. No one is going to intervene and take control from this team.

records.eventName: CHS District Alexandria VA Event presented by US Department of Energy
records.script: At “Go!”, this team’s robot swam to the top of the reef. They took the fight to tele-op with their strategic automations. Their bot wages the war on its own.

records.eventName: CHS District Alexandria VA Event presented by US Department of Energy
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team impressed the judges with their professional process and handmade touch. Don’t mistake their mascot for a catfish: their underwater feline friend blazed a trail into the judges’ minds.

records.eventName: CHS District Blacksburg VA Event presented by Volvo
records.script: This team WOW'd the judges with their focused, sustainable outreach, striking a powerful impact year after year. Despite their already impressive efforts, they managed to SCALE new initiatives across Virginia, reaching global communities with impact that knows no borders. From the heart of HOKIE NATION, they SHED the skin of their past and strike with precision to inspire the next generation!

records.eventName: CHS District Blacksburg VA Event presented by Volvo
records.script: From the shadows of uncertainty, this team has sparked a fiery path for future innovators. Seeing middle schoolers slipping from the pipeline, they forged FREE after-school programs and breathed life into statewide advocacy. With WISP at their side, they continue to soar higher, lighting the way for a STEM future

records.eventName: CHS District Blacksburg VA Event presented by Volvo
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: As APEX predators, their robot is elegant and efficient. This team’s robot strikes a balance between form and function. Wearing sparkling goggles, they are in command of the Industrial Design ecosystem!

records.eventName: CHS District Blacksburg VA Event presented by Volvo
records.script: This Creative Fusion award goes to a team that SHOT FOR THE STARS by combining engineering and storytelling to inspire the next generation. They brought STEM to life in a unique and imaginative way. Through their original children’s book, “Argo: The Little Robot that Could” they won our hearts!

records.eventName: CHS District Blacksburg VA Event presented by Volvo
records.script: Emerging from a DESERT, this team found each other. They CUT their teeth on this challenge, MAKING it clear they had the right stuff. Their robot reached for the stars to prove this team has DIRECTION and VELOCITY.

records.eventName: CHS District Blacksburg VA Event presented by Volvo
records.script: A small-town team on the rise! Together all new members have gathered teachers from welding, machining, and engineering to create a solid foundation. These students from the Back-Woods are rising to the challenge!

records.eventName: CHS District Blacksburg VA Event presented by Volvo
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team remains grounded and humble in competition, despite their name. They have gallantly persevered through adversity, even having to change their training and practice facility. Not to sound overly emotional or hokey, but this award goes to that OTHER Virginia-college-themed team in Orange!

records.eventName: CHS District Blacksburg VA Event presented by Volvo
records.script: This team showed the judges their skills in building student leadership, project management, enthusiasm for problem-solving, and positivity. The judges were impressed with their high spirits spreading through their team, school, FRC and Community. These students like to BRAWL in the Blue Ridge and show their might!

records.eventName: CHS District Blacksburg VA Event presented by Volvo
records.script: This award goes to a team that has ignited innovation with their exceptional technical expertise and precision. With the right equipment to manufacture their own parts, a gear ratio strong enough to hold back an F-14, and unparalleled attention to detail, their engineering stands out.

records.eventName: CHS District Blacksburg VA Event presented by Volvo
records.script: When other teams needed help, they were not left abandoned. Thanks to this team’s SHARP idea there was a place to NEST. If you want to meet a great GP team, visit them at the Regency Mall.

records.eventName: CHS District Blacksburg VA Event presented by Volvo
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s creativity unfolded like a hidden canopy, offering unexpected shelter for brilliant ideas. Their innovative design, featuring a four-camera system and a uniquely engineered ground intake, demonstrates an unparalleled commitment to rethinking the ordinary!

records.eventName: CHS District Blacksburg VA Event presented by Volvo
records.script: They build both quality people and robots. From paint to wiring, this team’s modularity ensures their gravity-defying climb. Their robot might be a secret agent, but there’s no way to disguise its quality!

records.eventName: CHS District Blacksburg VA Event presented by Volvo
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team SWAM away from the competition. By FLIPPING the script, they were able to CATCH our eye. Knowing when to catch and RELEASE allowed them to CONTROL the seas!

records.eventName: CHS District Blacksburg VA Event presented by Volvo
records.script: Clinging to the challenge with unstoppable agility, this team is built for precision. Their autonomous is lightning-fast, darting across the field to score 3 coral while always ready with a UH-OH BUTTON for quick recovery. With cold-blooded focus and a grip on success, they’ve truly stuck the landing in autonomous!

records.eventName: CHS District Blacksburg VA Event presented by Volvo
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s robot stood out in a forest. Their cohesive look from pit-to-stand was ELECTRIC. These glowing, growing circuits had the judges truly electrified.

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event presented by Herndon Foundation
records.script: The impact award is for the team that is a role model in FIRST and their community. This year's Impact Award winner has many initiatives to emulate, transforming the culture. As this team has aged they work far and wide to impact their community whether it's online, collaborating with others, in the halls of government, or beyond our borders. This team is top tier, molding the next generation of STEM leaders that are sure to be Goud …. A

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event presented by Herndon Foundation
records.script: Over the past year, this team made their mark on the community. They emphasized engaging their area schools, bringing FLL into Title 1 schools, and expanding STEM education to their local Hispanic community. Ready to soar high, let’s skip the 3 - 2 - 1 and go straight to 5 – 4 – …..

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event presented by Herndon Foundation
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team truly wears many hats! They manufactured parts in-house, balancing style and efficiency. Using easily replaceable, multi-functional elements, they squared away a great design for the drive team.

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event presented by Herndon Foundation
records.script: Sometimes a team’s community needs more help than just in STEM. Seeing their community’s need for clothing and food sparked an idea. Creating the ReCharged Boutique to meet that need earned this team the Judges Award for Altruistic Marketing.

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event presented by Herndon Foundation
records.script: This team traveled a unique path for their rookie year Driven by enthusiasm, they built their team with donated materials, innovated out of necessity, and achieved organization and outreach worthy of a future FIRST Impact Award. These top guns broke the sound barrier with their cookie sheet-backed bot.

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event presented by Herndon Foundation
records.script: Turns out you can teach an old dog new tricks, especially after a good night's rest. This team came back after a few years away, energized and ready to go. These are now new dogs barking their way to the top of the most impactful teams.

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event presented by Herndon Foundation
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team meticulously records their work and returns their shared space to its natural state. They recycle old bots and scraps in an attempt to reuse everything. The creators of the "we can find a use for everything" philosophy really impressed the judges.

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event presented by Herndon Foundation
records.script: This team’s toothy grin brightens the competition. They consistently show the spirit of FIRST, throughout their team, in the stands, and on the fields. They want you to know that actually, they are not mean but instead nice.

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event presented by Herndon Foundation
records.script: While some teams stumble through engineering, this team sees the critical path. Developing a high-level process and forward-thinking systems, they serve as an example for others. Guiding the way through the engineering process, these students are the torchbearers.

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event presented by Herndon Foundation
records.script: This team blazes a bright path in their quest to help others. This team unites their community, builds alliances, & encourages younger teams. They have represented themselves with luminous gracious professionalism.

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event presented by Herndon Foundation
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: While many teams focus on scoring coral, this stealthy team’s approach to handling game pieces is exemplary. An aggressive ground intake, a protective tunnel, and a robust delivery mechanism have all been integrated into a unique system. While this robot’s name implies noise and chaos, “STAND MIXER” is anything but.

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event presented by Herndon Foundation
records.script: This team used calculated efforts to outshine the competition. Every bolt, wire, and piece of code reflects their dedication to building a robust robot. This team uses the BO-OI-OING effect to bounce back against other robots.

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event presented by Herndon Foundation
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team charted the depths with advanced technology. With multiple ways to determine its location, this team’s control system helps its drivers score quickly and accurately. Fusing both virtual and reality, this team is always ready to McDive into the competition.

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event presented by Herndon Foundation
records.script: In the heat of competition, this team scores at the top. Their keen eyes scan the field, like a hound on the hunt, striking with speed and accuracy. When it comes to autonomous, this is truly the top dog of the heap.

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event presented by Herndon Foundation
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This Team dove into the competition with a graceful splash. From their uniform to their 3D printed parts this team is instantly recognizable. Congratulations to these tulle-clad terrapins!

records.eventName: CHS District Portsmouth VA Event presented by Newport News Shipyard
records.script: This team has had a profound impact in their community, state, and broader region, Their outreach, advocacy, and sustainability are on fire! These dragons never stop advancing STEM.

records.eventName: CHS District Portsmouth VA Event presented by Newport News Shipyard
records.script: This team's inventiveness and effectiveness in recruitment outreach were superbly impressive. They created a FIRST pipeline with workshops and robotics classes, and mentored many FIRST teams. They shed their skin to birth new ideas to inspire engineering in their community and beyond, learning by teaching 1500 people, and increasing enrollment in robotics classes by 408%.

records.eventName: CHS District Portsmouth VA Event presented by Newport News Shipyard
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: When form, function, and aesthetics were required, they were third to none. Their process and design came together like a well-engineered blueprint resulting in a complete organism. When it comes to industrial design, it's in their DNA.

records.eventName: CHS District Portsmouth VA Event presented by Newport News Shipyard
records.script: Judges Momentum Award With creativity and precision, they navigated through obstacles, demonstrating impressive growth. When the competition called for adaptability and grace, this team rode the waves of challenge with ease. Rising to second place in only their second season, they proved they can make a splash!

records.eventName: CHS District Portsmouth VA Event presented by Newport News Shipyard
records.script: This rookie team unearthed the wisdom of the ancients to behave like veterans. They cracked the code to effectively build and control their swerve drive robot using veteran team techniques like full robot CAD, and a treasury fit for kings. We expect this team from history to have a golden future.

records.eventName: CHS District Portsmouth VA Event presented by Newport News Shipyard
records.script: In the vast sea of innovation, subtle tides hint at a transformation yet to come. Emerging from the trees, this team has turned challenges into a powerful surge of creativity. We honor their rising journey through the woods as they branch out and pave a new trail in robotics.

records.eventName: CHS District Portsmouth VA Event presented by Newport News Shipyard
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team has shown unwavering dedication, resilience, and a commitment to passing on their legacy of excellence. Through decades of dedication, they have embraced sustainability by growing their student numbers, hosting annual open houses, fostering a strong FLL pipeline, and welcoming alumni back as mentors. With a history dating back to 1997, these noble warriors have stood the test of time, proving that true sustainability is about passing knowledge from one generation to the next.

records.eventName: CHS District Portsmouth VA Event presented by Newport News Shipyard
records.script: This team shines like a constellation, embodying the power of unity and enthusiasm. Recognized for their outstanding energy in engaging with judges and showcasing their team spirit, they have truly exemplified what it means to work as one. Like Castor and Pollux, twin stars glowing with team spirit, they light up this competition with their energy and unity!

records.eventName: CHS District Portsmouth VA Event presented by Newport News Shipyard
records.script: This team takes flight soaring through challenges with precision. Masters of design, they craft sleek solutions, especially their wrist. Wearing all black, they dominated with excellent engineering.

records.eventName: CHS District Portsmouth VA Event presented by Newport News Shipyard
records.script: This team's giving spirit and positive attitude captured many other teams this weekend. They provided parts, expertise, kits, and swerve drive assistance to teams during this season, This apex team of the sea described this weekend's competition in two words: "Pop-Off"

records.eventName: CHS District Portsmouth VA Event presented by Newport News Shipyard
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This is a very well-grounded team. Their creation flies above the algae. Their innovations were un-Bee-lievable.

records.eventName: CHS District Portsmouth VA Event presented by Newport News Shipyard
records.script: When the competition called for excellence, they stood out from the rest! With creativity and precision, they demonstrated an exceptional commitment to quality, delivering consistent and reliable performance. Always ready to rise to the occasion, this team proved they could age to perfection.

records.eventName: CHS District Portsmouth VA Event presented by Newport News Shipyard
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: When the competition called for ingenuity, this team proved their ability to adapt and thrive in a coral reef environment with creativity and precision. Their sharp thinking and precise execution stood tall. Always ready to chop down challenges, they developed innovative control systems that set a new standard.

records.eventName: CHS District Portsmouth VA Event presented by Newport News Shipyard
records.script: This team's robot seeks out the reef. Their keen vision leads them directly to the targets. They swoop in for the points.

records.eventName: CHS District Portsmouth VA Event presented by Newport News Shipyard
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team's theme was seamless from the team, to the pit, to the machine. Their luminous pit was visible from the stands to the "reefscape" sea. This team assimilated to have collective ideas on their pit cube design, robot strategy, and distinguishable attire.

This team has been growing and expanding their impactful outreach program with intention, and has seen a lot of success. They bring their continuous improvement mindset to their entire program and fully embrace the opportunities they have to make a positive impact. They value helping other teams across the FIRST program spectrum recognizing that to get through the competition season other teams often need a space to share, or a cup of coffee. For many teams, the summer is a season for camp or the beach, for this team it’s time for hard work and baseball. This team has committed to the mantra, “If you build it they will come”.
This team is geared up to spread the mission of FIRST. This team is the Americone Dream. Inspiring everyone they meet to Do it, Learn it, Teach it.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team built a robot with sensors, electronics, and 3D-printed parts in a robust, tight, and well-integrated package. With many degrees of freedom, this machine floats seamlessly from reef to source with ease. “Do you know what that sound is highness, those are the shrieking eels!”

This team’s passive approach to the game has made them very adept at scoring on multiple levels. Their cherry-picking methods make them a valuable asset to any team. You might find them around the home during the calm summer night.

This team may be small in numbers, with only five students. Despite a low number of sponsors, they proudly display the support of the entire FIRST community—literally—on their robot’s frame with stickers from other schools. They’ve built a robot that somehow survives competition… despite having a piece of polycarbonate so thin it makes everyone flinch whenever it dispenses a coral—but hey, it's still holding strong, just like their team! They’ve also worked very closely with a mentor who might’ve accidentally named their robot Blender.

Our small town guests have come to learn the value of commitment. By having team members accountable, they have been able to establish a means of success. Their team’s persistence on fundraising has resulted in a nice grant from the state.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: With passionate state-wide efforts, this team has established an effervescent environment and generated a mountain-sized impact in their community. They have brought champ to life.
Through enthusiastic sponsor demos and positive FIRST experiences, this team has established a purple pipeline of prosperity. The energy of this team knows no bounds.

From strategy to design verification, this team designed a robot with an engineering rigor that will make their sponsors proud. Their methodical approach keeps them centered and allows them to climb to the top. They are a force to be reckoned with.

This team’s enthusiasm is infectious. They impressed the judges by including all their members in the conversation. They support other robotics programs with funding and volunteer hours. Their Tardigrade robot and team can’t be kept under water!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: No CNC? No problem! This team builds within their resources to spring up and soar through the sky. No need for another motor in this “archy”-type, this team can passively tip down to score.
Their driving is smooth and they climb with agility. They do it by the numbers. They do it by the book. They don't do rivets, but they excel at robotics.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: With some spring in their step, this team brought several unique and practical innovations to the field. Their precise control over both their arm and elevator shows a level of freedom that makes scoring look effortless. When you see their robot in action, the control system practically shouts, Neon Green—that’s their team!

This team’s robot has demonstrated exceptional innovation with autonomous systems that reliably and repeatedly score with precision. The robot navigates the field efficiently and effectively. The resulting robot is truly well above average.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has shown a cohesive front. Their team is used to hard work, day in and day out. They are the color of royalty and support their kingdom.

This team NETTED the judges with their intentional and sustainable outreach programs, along with their DEEP engagement in the FIRST community. Their summer camps have proven to be a strong recruitment strategy, with 44% of the team being former campers. They take on barriers for women and gender minorities by annually hosting a competition that brings in more than 30 FRC teams, along with hosting their first set of FTC competitions this year. Additionally, this team is known to provide first aid kits—a NECESSITY for safety in an FRC event. They even provide scholarships to graduating seniors pursuing higher education. FISH FACT—((SOUND EFFECT)) ding ! The BEARaccuda might be ferocious but this team is quite the opposite.

This team's prime directive is clear....inspire young minds through community outreach and local advocacy. From mentoring future cadets and promoting inclusion, to running STEM camps and expanding FIRST programs through international collaboration.... the judges thought this team was truly stellar. Resistance is futile. There is no stopping them from going where no team has gone before.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: With a simple, thrifty design and prototyping process this team focused on elevator, coral shooter and climber. Building a robot "more than they set out to do".... this team made the robot STRONG!! Creating an aesthetically pleasing custom tint on an engraved panel, this robot "SPARED no expense."

With all the stress of competition, one team whispers, "NEVERMORE". Their care for others ensures no worry stays, their fun-filled gadgets calm the *waves*. With a dedicated *Chief Fun Officer* whose spirit soars, to quote the judges..... "It's Joy Galore!" Presenting the "Advocating Joy" award....
This team has soared into first, leaving nothing in their wake. They help out their teachers showcasing FIRST's vision. These 10 members have left no algae or coral in Moses Lake.

This young team focused on recruiting, more than doubling in size, with only 3 upper classmen. Despite unprecedented challenges, this team mentors FTC, works with their sister teams and participates in the county fair. Their green and purple stood out to the judges. This Happy, Helpful, Hardworking, HIGH TECH team has a great future....

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: With summer camps and FLL involvement, this team is creating the next generation of STEM leaders. They ensure financial sustainability by engaging with sponsors and growing their dedicated rollover fund. This team especially impresses the judges with how they transformed wood into a "PACK OF PARTS" to promote STEM sustainability abroad.

The winner's demonstrated joy in sharing the spirit of FIRST, celebrating both the big gains of STEM appreciation and all the little wins that occur throughout their days here. Bringing a culture of inclusion to their corner of the forest, they make their program good for everyone, whether they are interested in building robots, creating marketing strategies, or anything else that will engage them. They have been meeting and having fun with many of the teams here this weekend, each one being another LINK in the CHAIN for these cats.

This team "green lighted" their robot with robust, reliable software. This team's "string elevator" tugged at our heart strings. With a clean design they clearly had their finger on the pulse of the competition.

This brightly colored team showed amazing collaboration and team work. They blew us away with their gracious professionalism. These astronaut candidates have really "SPARKED" the judges interest as they "SUPPORTED and SUPPLIED" their community.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Through it's unique features of coral intake, outtake, and custom vision system this team caught the eye of the judges. This robot splits in half to rise to the top. Their creative design elements are a HOOT and OUT OF THIS WORLD.

This team reliably soars above the competition. Their cleanly design multi-manipulator consistently executes the mission. The BORDIE packed their commitment to quality in TOTES and brought it to the reef.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: In the innovation in control category, we recognize a team that invested significant effort into building out novel software tooling to inform robot performance. This team developed an innovating machine-learning pipeline to inform robot classifiers and demonstrated a unique and robust approach to global localization. Join us in congratulating a team that optimized for everything but alphabetical priority....
