This team is someone everyone hopes to be part of their alliance during the first 15 seconds. They demonstrate precise localization to the reef of both robot base and end-effector, leading to consistently high scoring autonomous sequences. Through their namesake often leads to an unpleasant surprise, it comes as NO surprise that this team take home the autonomous award.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: No one can miss this team with their big and bright image with the color of others' envy. Imagery for them is a hook to grab the attention that gives them the opportunity to share their obvious FIRST core values all year around. Their feathers never are ruffled even if the feathers can sometimes be found in their wake.......down their GREEN MILE.

From the shores of the Indian Ocean to the Mediterranean Sea to the Gold Coast of Africa, and back to the PNW, this team started, mentored and supported over 30 teams around the globe to spread the mission of FIRST. This team has enabled kids with physical disability see the light of STEM while harnessing the power of partnerships and bringing the vision of FIRST to life. Like the iconic Sparta from Ancient Greece, they have become a leading force in spreading the power of robotics.

This team exemplifies how best to promote STEM within the team, their school, and their community. They have committed to this growth by creating a STEM pipeline through mentoring FLL teams and their EV3 Mindstorm program. Communication is key to their efforts with each team member, letting them know what they can expect from both their team and leadership. They prize DISCOVERY as a foundational path for learning about STEM, FIRST, and, most importantly, themselves. All while creating a better space for everyone. This team brings a unique and inspiring NRG (energy) to our world.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team’s robot is a masterclass in refined engineering — a fusion of sleek, resilient materials and shadowed hues. Don’t be misled by the size of their end effector; this machine moves with fierce precision, unyielding and deliberate — like a predator stalking its prey. Despite this team’s name, a lot more than just aluminum and steel was used to create their machine.

This year's Judges Award goes to a team who grabbed our attention both with outreach and design. In the offseason this team collaborated with other students at their school to create a customized mobility aid for a child with Cerebral Palsy. Their unusual climber this season came from members brand new to the team as well as new to CAD. For passion, drive, and grit, the "CLAW-LABORATION" (collaboration) award.......

Like explorers of the western plains in the days of Lewis and Clark, this team started with nothing. Today, their team features good recruiting and safety culture, and there is NOTHING BAD about their robot either. They may be new, but this heard has stampeded into FRC with impressive team dynamics.

This team impressed the judges with their willingness to take on culture change in their team. After identifying toxic team dynamics, they visited other teams to learn how they could do better, clarifying member roles and responsibilities, and having team social events to build a healthier team culture. Today, this teams is all go and......No H2O

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: With their beady eyes, they found trails for their next opportunity. They have a "NACK"-er for crushing glass to renew their watershed and beaches. They have really earned their SHELL in sustainability.
Celebrating the spirit and exceptional fellowship of this team is not a challenge. Their enthusiasm and attitude are "chivalric". Raise a lance to Galahad.

Did you know how many blends of herbs and spices KFC has? The magic number is 11....the same number of steps this team uses to engineer their success. Their engineering process has clearly proven that they take attention to detail to a whole new level—probably with spreadsheets, late-night debates, and at least one existential crisis over gear ratios. Through continuous testing (aka breaking things and fixing them again), they fine-tuned their prototypes to create a robot that seamlessly rises from shallow depths to high elevations with precision that makes GPS jealous—all while giving the competition an unexpected spray along the way.
Don't let this team fly under your radar! They go above and beyond to support their teammates and competitors. This team didn't need a stealth mission to get to the top of the list..

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: While other teams looked inward for inspiration, this team went deep into the forest. The quest got hairy at times, but they ultimately solved the climb. This teams creativity is definitely not a myth.

With a level of polish rarely seen in FRC, this team sets the bar high with exceptional attention to detail and design. Clever adaptations like integrated anti-vibration plates allowed it to claw its way through the toughest challenges on the field with relentless precision. When it came to scoring L4s this team was dropping buckets.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: With sharp minds and technical flair, they prowl the competition without a care. Their innovation in control system is so RARE-ABLE, it made piloting their robot BEAR-ABLE. Precision, finesse, a movement so rare, no wonder, they are called the MIGHTY CYBEARS
This team's auto gets the match off to a top-hat start. Their state machines are as unique as snowflakes. Their collision avoidance algorithms keep their drives cool.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Blending a fluid theme with a wave of attractive aesthetics. This team has created an inclusive recipe for outstanding and delicious overall design. Grab your chopsticks and ride the NORI wave.

With over five thousand hours of volunteering, this team's impact on the FIRST community is undeniable. As a Cofounder of the Bellevue Alliance, The team's efforts helped secure the STEMnasium in 2023 by inviting other teams to advocate for STEM and FIRST programs at Bellevue School District board meetings. They secured shop space for the FLL teams from 16 elementary schools, an FRC Practice Field, and stipends for all coaches within the district. They inspire and enable the next generation of STEM leaders. They expand their influence beyond their community to engage with the state legislature. Testifying before the Washington State House, this team ensured that all students will receive high school credit for their involvement in FIRST programs. Working with Senator Lisa Wellman, Senate Bill 5617 passed unanimously and was signed into Law in 2023. Building on that success they founded the Robotics STEM Advocacy Alliance providing mentorship and resources to over 40 teams in 17 states and one province resulting in similar legislation in multiple states. Please join us in giving CREDIT WHERE CREDIT IS DUE.

This team understands the power of sustainable and iterative outreach within their community base. Demonstrating year-over-year growth of starting 25 FIRST teams and mentoring 37, as well as their unique apprenticeship model for recruitment, this team brought home their many samples of outreach for the judges to examine closely. AS CAN-didates for this award, this team brought results that the judges think are quite ASTRONOMICAL.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team crafted a robot that shines in every detail. Omni wheels anchor their floor pickup, while the elevator BLENDS intake and delivery seamlessly. All these features come together to make a MISO TASTY MIX.

This team’s outreach efforts were of truly Olympic proportions. They provided supplies and mentoring to STEM programs in Ghana, Libya, and India, and even arranged for one of their FLL teams in India to present their project at FIRST Championship in Houston. The judges are pleased to award the International Growth Award.

This newly young team set sail to the reefs. Navigating the rough waters without assistance from their ancestors, they safely made port. Collecting parts from their environment like a crow building a NEST, their resourcefulness proves they are a rising all-star.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: The culture of and approach to sustainability, which permeated this massive team allowed them to take a LICKING and keep on ticking. This team uses apprenticeships to LAP-UP transition of leadership roles. Many WOOD BAY at their effective recycling efforts, from robot to robot, or even for a motorized wheelchair. The judges present the Sustainability award to this most heavenly team.

This team runs smoothly, like well-oiled gears in a machine. Through multiple initiatives, they have UNBOXED spirit for their team, their community, and the world. Their passion to make the world a better place is inspiring, so PACK UP YOUR PARTS and join them!
This team’s design principles carried through robot build and maintenance. Their powerhouse robot allows their drivers to DRIVE HARD. They can mark this award off their checklist.

This team has brought stories of graciousness, endurance, and persistence. They opened their doors for teams in transit to the Canadian Pacific Regional to use their practice field for some fine-tuning. And, after having to move workspaces, this team continued to pursue their offseason work, forging a continued path with their school board to secure a new habitat. This team exudes so much Gracious Professionalism it makes the gym smell a bit… SKUNKY.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: While every team has designed a coral manipulator, this unique implementation caught the judges’ eyes. They made a SPLASH with their custom 3D printed design, enabling them to score coral on all levels and reef branches to the left or right. By grabbing from the inside, they FLIP the script on coral manipulation.

When it comes to durability, this team’s robot is no MYTH. Their custom chassis keeps electronics safe and compact, ensuring they stay strong through every match. With a design built to endure, they’ve proven that quality isn’t just a FOOTPRINT they leave. It’s a path they follow.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: When you head into battle, you’ll want this team on the front line. On the field we see blazing fast auto-alignment; off the field they share their unique path finding approach with other teams. Forget about THREE HUNDRED. This team has over FORTY THOUSAND ways to score in autonomous.

This team pops up for their effectively automated robot with high accuracy and speed. Their robot is aware of all its surroundings, so touching one button will OWN THE GOAL. Watch this team start auto mode and SPRING into action.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team made big waves bringing their arts and crafts to the forefront. Evoking a traditional flair, the team sprinkled toppings onto their hand-painted robot design, their mascot, and even their sponsorship tier list. When it came to demonstrating their imagery, this team recognized the BIG PICTURE.

This Team's continued efforts to Spread the Mission of FIRST have impacted hundreds of thousands of people through their FLL Curriculum, STEM Summer Camps, and other community events. Through continued involvement in Unified Robotics supporting multiple teams and hosting the Washington Unified Robotics Championship, this team shows that students with intellectual disabilities have a place in STEM. With their Gender Equity workshops in partnership with the King County Library System, the team strives to create a safe space for women, non-binary, and transgender innovators, ensuring FIRST and STEM is accessible for all. W.O.W.s look at the Time! Let's shift into G.E.A.R.S. and bring them down.

This team is committed to spreading STEM education and the FIRST mission throughout their school and community by starting multiple FLL and FTC teams. They also CLAWED their way into the state legislature to advocate for EV education. We're not KITTEN you when we say this team has truly inspired inclusion in engineering by hosting STEM nights that include individuals of all gender identities and establishing a new Unified Robotics team.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Designing a robot with the METTLE to withstand competition is hard, but desigining it to be bulletproof and look good is harder. Using a professional review process, prototyping, and rapid iterative design, this team produced an outstanding robot that outperformed the competition. The tension is unBEARable, so without further ado...

Taking their STEM to local off-season events, How they do this is really intense. Their team is just not immense. Poseidon has come from the sea for this team, Their trident is the entire team. The judges would like to name this the Eight Arms of FIRST award.

Using their strong ANCHOR based in FTC, this team does it all. They aim to balance the DYNAMICS in their team, their school, their sponsors, and in their community. This may be their first year, but these rookies have a CLEAR SHOT at winning it all.

This team has demonstrated great resilience in the face of adversity. Over a few years, they have grown from a few cubs into a roaring community, through offseason workshops and student mentoring. Although the odds were against them, ORANGE you glad they stuck around to make their bot a movie star.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team demonstrates a year-on-year commitment to sustain itself and for FIRST. Creating a plan and executing the plan, this team uses multiple ARCS to complete their CIRCLE. From recruitment to finance, this team is a REVOLUTIONARY model for this award.

This team inspires and empowers EVERYONE, EVERYWHERE with the spirit of FIRST. They carry their UNIFIED spirit to the world and beyond. This team's enthusiasm carries through their leadership to this award.

To elevate your robot above the competition, you must start with a simple and reliable design from the ground up. Waiting through the SOUP of many prototypes, their inspired design rose like the tide, ending with an elegant robot that scored on all levels. We aren't full of beans when we say we could fill six pages with reasons this team impressed us.
This team has a passion for equal opportunity and diversity. They've expanded their reach across oceans, collaborating with teams across the globe. This team isn't just a team, they're a SQUAD.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team impressed the judges with their speed and efficiency on the field. Their innovative design made a huge DIFFERENTIAL in the competition. It may be in their name, but this team is no dinosaur.

With effective project management and process flow, this team was able to rise to the challenge and deliver a Quality robot. With excellent craftsmanship, attention to detail, and a burnished frame, the team blended 3D printing and standard fabrication techniques on key components, allowing this bot to CLAW its way through the field. While most cats don't like water, did you know Panthers do?

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: After finally getting a water game, this team is in its element. They created a novel yet sophisticated coral manipulator and using it is as easy as 1-2-3. We tip our hats to this top team.

This team's robot capably swam through this competition, stinging their opponents along the way. The Tesla of robotics, their robot has unlocked autopilot even during tele-op. They could have reached the top without the home-field advantage!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team didn't just show off imagery, the made a SPLASH! From their ocean inspired pit to their seaside games, this team is staying warm with the sharks. This CRUSH inspired robot SRFs on the field!

This team impressed with their outreach, advocacy and team building. When the team came in, they quickly won us over with their passion and confidence. With their fantastic skills, it will take more than a meteor to stop these raptors.

The team embodies what it means to spread the message of FIRST in their community. They ensured accessibility was available to their workshop despite setbacks. This team uses more than just duct tape to help their community.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: It’s no secret that this team’s bot is streamlined and well designed. Their ability to utilize CNC to manufacture a durable, functional, and magnifying glass catching robot to compete puts them a fedora above the rest. Congratulations to Team 4125 Confidential!

The judge’s award goes to a team that stood out for their unique approach to making a difference. Their efforts were KEY in pushing for change across the BOARD. This team has sent an example for advocacy that we should all COPY.

FIRST has brought this team together, and now they are looking to impact other teams. This is their first year and they have two competitions under their belts. It’s safe to say this is a radical team.

A young team themselves, their MANE focus is spreading the FIRST mission throughout elementary sand middle schools in their area. From hand-drawn playing cards, to kid-made buttons, they take PRIDE in getting their brand out in creative ways. Fear their roar, but don’t worry, they won’t BYTE.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team demonstrated both environmental and team sustainability. They give increased access to recycling education in their community. This team ignited a spark of inspiration in the judges.

With their enthusiastic cheering, this team is not afraid to glow in the limelight. They bring spirit everywhere they go and love to share FIRST. This team brings others out of their cocoons and turns them into butterflies.

This team’s coral handling mechanism impressed the judges with its 360 degree rotation. Vision from a dream brought design to a howling success. No obstacles or limitations could slow these bow tied crusaders down.
This team is not quiet about supporting FIRST and STEM initiatives. You will hear the rumbling of their offices on and off the field. Be careful, their gracious professionalism will blow you away!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team switched GEARS while taking a big risk. by removing the large component of their robot. After training an AI model with more than 30,000 images, they’ve become an algae scoring machine. Despite the team outfit, we SALUTE them for thinking in more than just BLACK and WHITE.

The team’s robot was designed to withstand the dangers of falling coral while making it easier to wire components. Their use of a constant focus spring increased reliability and reduced maintenance on their elevator Their quality work in building their robot- PAWS for effect- contributed to their success.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team is nutty for programming! With 4 cameras and 2 processors, this team ensures smooth control in scoring. Congrats to our furry friends, team 2930, the Sonic Squirrels!

This team might have an I on you, but if their robot loses sight, they have Auto2. From collecting ranking points to collecting W2s, they are always coming and they’re bringing backup. Congratulations, Team 1318 IRS!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s robot’s appearance and color scheme is hard to miss. Their robot is built to navigate the reef instead of soaring with the birds. This team is ready to dive deep with its yellow submarine.

This year's Impact award winner is no stranger to success, in fact their history is the definition of it. This team ran or supported almost 40 outreach events last year alone. In their presentation they gave the judges FIVE reasons to consider them. They participate in all THREE facets of FIRST, FLL, FTC, and FRC. This years Impact award will be the SEVENTH in their 20 year history. If there is a robot heaven there is a place for FIVE THREE SEVEN.

This team really SOARS above the FLOCKS when it comes to inspiring others in STEM. By driving initiatives not only locally but internationally, they have a real “knack” for connecting communities, through STEM. While other HAWKS were still trying to get their FEATHERS wet, they dove deep into the challenge and surfaced as the true inspiration.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team really designed their robot FOUR perfection. Their unique intake systems are SHORE to impress you. They keep design and functionality at the CORE of what they do.

This year's judges award will go to a community based team that has found many unique ways to spread the mission of FIRST. The DEPTH of their effort reaches all ages and includes all abilities. They care enough to advance STEM initiatives from BootCamps, to 4th grade classes, to their Grandparents. They are even nice to their robots. This team is at home in the WATER and their SHARK is creating FIRST WAVES in their community.

This year’s Rising All Star is SMALL but MIGHTY. Their ADVENTURES in robotics began in a chemistry lab, but now they have reached new depths in a new space. These KNIGHTS are now ready to RISE to the CHALLENGE of engaging new SQUIRES.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: When it comes to making an enduring team, others should be RED with envy. This team has developed innovative methods of recycling and team sustainability that should carry them far into the future. They have shown how to be a RAIDER of sustainability.
An air of NOBILITY surrounds this team. Their capes billow as they wheel their KNIGHT to the field. Now we CROWN their efforts.

This team didn’t just pick-up a wrench and start building. Instead, they cranked-up their engineering game, fine-tuning their gears to handle the coral with mechanical mastery. They designed parts of the robot to be multi-functional and move out of the way when no longer needed. This GRAY DUCK is no Lame Duck.

The members of this team are AVID supporters of every team they meet, lending parts and knowledge indiscriminately. This team has already proven they work well AUTONOMOUSLY, but has chosen to collaborate with many teams on and off season. This team goes beyond robotics in their attitudes off and on the field.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s creativity and success with their machine design earned them their spot at the HEAD OF THE PACK. Their unique approaches with handling every aspect of the game allowed them to excel with coral, algae, and hanging. With the use of the innovative 3D printed parts, they proved themselves as TOP DOGS.

This team built a ROCK SOLID FOUNDATION with an aluminum and polycarbonate frame, ensuring durability was never just a SKETCH. Every joint and bolt BRUSHED away past repair woes, turning lessons learned into a ROCK-SOLID MASTERPIECE. They have found success with durability as their CANVAS and quality as their SIGNATURE.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team developed a custom button board to control their robot around the field and gave them control over the HORIZONTAL AND VERTICAL. Their practical approach to meeting their robot’s control needs proves that they can handle stress like GOOD FURNITURE.

This award is given to a design that used 3d printing of the coral grabber. They MUTATED their design, evolving towards excellence. They demonstrated their CRISPR autonomous performance in the crucible of competition as they loaded coral in the top level.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team cleverly used their MULTIPLE BRAINS to find a connection between their brand and this theme. They’ve masterfully masked their robot and themselves with signs of this INTELLIGENT BRAIN. You might think this team came from the depths of the ocean but no, from a town of 2 RIVERS.

records.eventName: Wisconsin Regional presented by GE HealthCare
records.script: This team took a BYTE out of the information gap by sharing programming knowledge across the world. Strong support of FLL programs is providing this team with a strong foundation allowing them to fortify their DEN. The impact of their extensive workshop catalogue and hosting of FIRST events is PAWsitive, powerful, and BEARly believable. Where others stop, this team continues to “GO”.

records.eventName: Wisconsin Regional presented by GE HealthCare
records.script: This team has depths in their DNA. The reach of their awesomeness is easy to fathom, a tsunami across their community and engagement to all ages.

records.eventName: Wisconsin Regional presented by GE HealthCare
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: With an INNOVATIVE horizontal intake & a QR code management system, This team’s Winn-ing design really succeeds in the deep

records.eventName: Wisconsin Regional presented by GE HealthCare
records.script: This team impressed the judges with their monster of a robot. Their performance on and off the field helped them stand out in a sea of competition. Their advanced manipulation of coral from the sea floor helped them rise to the top of the reef.

records.eventName: Wisconsin Regional presented by GE HealthCare
records.script: This team quickly grasped the FIRST ethos and the value of patience. Celebrating their recent 30th day anniversary. Congratulations,

records.eventName: Wisconsin Regional presented by GE HealthCare
records.script: This community team of 28 did not stay blue, instead they quadrupled resources to take a focus on the future. They are a model of FIRST and are rising with a roar!

records.eventName: Wisconsin Regional presented by GE HealthCare
records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This team doesn’t wing it, they have a flight plan. Through their stem nights and 4000 lbs of batteries recycled, they really soared

records.eventName: Wisconsin Regional presented by GE HealthCare
records.script: Their spirit could be considered magical. Like a rocket booster, their energy is out of this world.

records.eventName: Wisconsin Regional presented by GE HealthCare
records.script: This year’s recipient exemplifies outstanding engineering rigor. From meticulous planning and thorough design reviews to rigorous failure mode analysis, prototype evaluation and comprehensive documentation, this team left no stone unturned. Their robot’s performance on the field was a testament to their dedication: lightning-fast, consistently accurate, and impeccability controlled. A truly exceptional engineering design that may have even caused a few jitters among the competition.

records.eventName: Wisconsin Regional presented by GE HealthCare
records.script: This team developed a spirit that transcends all of the teams they mentored, acting as community collaborators in this vast den of gracious professionals.

records.eventName: Wisconsin Regional presented by GE HealthCare
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This year’s creativity award winner burned through the competition by designing a robot that met all challenges. Their robot design also allowed for improvement as the season progressed. Their use of 3D printed wheels and a completely machined structure made the robot robust with great aesthetics. This team performed consistently and never flamed out.

records.eventName: Wisconsin Regional presented by GE HealthCare
records.script: Their plan was clear with a focus on the access and replaceability of critical components. They achieved this through hard work, helpfulness, and continuing to learn as one team. The quality of this well-rounded bot set the table for a fantastic performance.

records.eventName: Wisconsin Regional presented by GE HealthCare
records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team is looking through a new lens with their innovative and multi-level system. They climbed the hill and worked extensively to develop a unique and exciting vision system. This approach propelled them to their quest to top the competition.

records.eventName: Wisconsin Regional presented by GE HealthCare
records.script: This team ‘funneled’ coral through their robot quickly and reliably. Using 4 different cameras, redundant encoder calibration and a robust overall design, this team was one of the highest scoring robots in autonomous. Their robot clearly has a good sense of direction, not getting lost even though it had to cross the ’state line’ to get here.

records.eventName: Wisconsin Regional presented by GE HealthCare
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Everywhere in the competition this team is a vibrant expression, recognizable from the pits to the playfield. It is easy to understand how their colors paint the reef.

This team’s outreach efforts impressed the judges with activities in local schools through FTC, and targeted efforts to expand STEM access across genders and ability, they’ve directly impacted thousands with positive experiences. From a program advocating to go GREEN at events, they are also focused on encouraging young women to explore STEM and FIRST and sustainable collaborations- to improve the quality of life for all in their area. This team is a force FOUR CHANGE. The judges, and their DROID, have seen their YELLOW path, and it clearly shows how this team is PREPA’D to keep impacting far and wide.

This team REACHES and IGNITES MINDS across the borders. They RUN, RAISE, ROPE, REPURPOSE, and REVIVE engineering knowledge and commitment with ROBUST passion. “The future of FIRST is safe in their hands”

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team differentiated themselves with their sleek and stunning machine . An industrial approach to design and material selection has KEPT THEIR WHEELS FIRMLY ON THE GROUND. The generative design gives them a LIFT TO SOAR above the others.

This team took a unique approach to fundraising through creating pretty-printed-playthings to expand their family tree. Their wild turtle chase had you snapping pics all around. Despite their recent challenges, this team has been a TOUGH NUT TO CRACK.

As a small group of entrepreneurs, THIS TEAM WILL GROW TO BE STRONG. Their balanced team approach will sustain their future. ORANGE YOU GLAD that they doubled the impact in their county, putting FIRST INTO OVERDRIVE.
These rising young stars are up for any challenge. With their “KIDS TEACHING KIDS” sustainability model, they have been BLITZING through this season.

records.awardName: Team Sustainability Award sponsored by Dow
records.script: This TRAILBLAZING team FLIES HIGH knowing that sustainability “STARTS WITH THEM”. SOLVING COMMUNITY PROBLEMS, creating sustainable and environmentally-friendly ROBOT PARTS, this team has a wide REACH. This team tips the PHOENIX SCALE, restarting from ASHES each year.

This team found themselves on an island with little representation in FIRST. They’ve made EPIC leaps and bounds to bring STEM to over 22,000 people. Let’s have them emerge from their den in their “BADGER -ALLS”.

This team did not have a CRABBIE attitude towards documenting every step of the engineering design process. Starting from kickoff, these students cataloged their MOSCOW analysis, subsystem research, prototypes, testing forms and video, and iterations between competitions. In the battle of wants and needs, these WARRIORS came out on top.
This FLOCK is a welcoming ambassador for both local and global teams. They host tailgates, boot camps, and library events, because FIRST is FAMILY.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This robot's unique design helped the judges to put the pin on this team. Despite their once stout design, the intentional design helps keep their robot well ROUNDED. When it came to robot design, this team kept everything on the TABLE.

Rather than getting TIED up in KNOTS, this team wasn’t afraid to RIP the band-aid off and fix weaknesses identified in early failure analysis reviews. Starting with DFMEAs for each subsystem always asking the 5Y’s and having a test bot by Build Week 4, this team lived by their mantra of "DON’T BREAK DOWN". Their extensive library of historical lessons learned would make any CSI investigator proud.

records.awardName: Innovation in Control Award sponsored by nVent
records.script: This team’s unique, cost effective vision solution drove them to a 3 coral autonomous. What started off as just a picture online, sharpened to a system accurate to a 1/16th of an inch. This team’s VR headset brought them to the TOP OF THE HILL.

This team’s control system was taken to the next level by the large amount of sensors on their bot. Their advanced automation even made their button board into an obsolete fidget toy. This team’s almost fully autonomous robot helped them BUST the competition.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s collaborative CANVAS truly colored us impressed. Their alliance partners TAG in to commemorate their success. You all know these neon green operators. They advocate for FIRST and Inspire tomorrow’s innovators.
